text:
URE ANSWERS (captured 2026-05-27 via team-lead relay; re-persisting after harness restart killed coordinator before relay). *** SCOPE-CHANGING OVERRIDE — read carefully ***

Q8 [5wbhm status audit — claim statement]: Question presented as trivial-case sign-off (expected verdict 'confirmed'). USER chose OVERRIDE: 'Substantive URE input — reword the claim statement'. Then when asked for exact wording, USER RESPONSE (VERBATIM):

  'Go is the authoritative implementation of the SKILL.md generation pipeline, but has only been verified for 7 skills. Python generation pipeline and content is slightly less up-to-date for these 7 skills, but the rest would be used as reference as they haven't been fully ported over yet.'

IMPACT — this is NO LONGER a trivial 'confirmed' status audit. The reworded claim has TWO parts that change the audit shape:
1. Authority is QUALIFIED, not absolute: Go authoritative but verified for only 7 skills => expected verdict shifts from 'confirmed' toward 'qualified'.
2. Coverage overlay: the deliverable must ENUMERATE which 7 skills are Go-verified vs the remaining (~30) that still use Python pipeline/content as reference because they aren't fully ported.

REVISED 5wbhm scope for PROPOSAL drafting:
- Claim (verbatim above) replaces the pre-filled 'Go authoritative; Python deprecated' claim.
- Verdict vocabulary unchanged: confirmed/refuted/qualified — but expected verdict is now 'qualified'.
- Evidence must establish: (a) WHICH 7 skills are verified Go-authoritative, (b) that Python is 'slightly less up-to-date' for those 7 (i.e., Go is ahead), (c) that the other skills still rely on Python as reference (not yet ported).
- Deliverable (pasture/AGENTS.md 'Code generation' section) must include the 7-skill enumeration + the not-yet-ported remainder, not just a binary authority statement.
- Cross-reference x5071 (port remaining 30 Python skills) — the 'not fully ported' remainder is exactly x5071's scope.

Note: this couples 5wbhm to the 7-overlapping-skills set referenced in PYTHON_TO_GO_MIGRATION.md + ROADMAP §1i (skill-drift CI check across 7 overlapping skills). Coordinator should reconcile 'the 7' against that doc when drafting.

text:
mh4ek coverage audit complete. Deliverable: docs/audits/mh4ek-constraint-coverage.md

ESCALATION per PROPOSAL-1 §10 — two non-trivial semantic judgment calls requiring team-lead review before UAT:

1. C-review-binary (verdict: divergent): Python enforces via string-level check; Go enforces via VoteType typed enum (compile-time structural prevention). Same constraint intent, different mechanism. Request team-lead judgment: is 'type system prevents invalid values at compile time' equivalent to the Python runtime check, or is it a semantic gap?

C-worker-gates (verdict: divergent): Spans two Python methods. check_blocker_gate() (blocker count check) IS ported and tested in Go. check_worker_gates() (has_todos + tests_pass + typecheck_pass quality gates) is entirely absent from Go runtime. - True constraint count: 27 (constraints.py SoT) + 1 addendum (C-actionable-errors, catalog-only)
- Verdicts: 1 ported (C-review-consensus), 0 untested, 24 missing, 2 divergent (C-worker-gates, C-review-binary)
- 28 gap tasks filed (all discovered-from:aura-plugins-mh4ek, aura:residual, P3)
- Key surprise: Go has NO RuntimeConstraintChecker equivalent — ActivityCheckConstraints only implements consensus+blocker gates via state machine; all other C-* IDs exist only as codegen schema metadata

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE 11 UAT (mh4ek) cont. 2026-05-30 — BUCKET A answer + MAJOR ARCHITECTURAL FINDING surfaced by user.

BUCKET A QUESTION presented: 'These 3 (C-review-consensus/C-review-binary/C-actionable-errors) are machine-enforced in Go at level (1)programmatic-check-or-(2)type-system, not (3)prompt-only. Disposition?'
USER RESPONSE (verbatim): 'Accept all 3 as enforced — close their verify-tasks (Recommended)'.

USER RESPONSE 2 (verbatim, architectural challenge): 'I'm confused here: does the type-system guarantee have to do with the multi-agent orchestrator pastured or pasture-msg, or does it have to do with the skill generation or schema generation? Because the orchestrator does NOT have to be used or mentioned by the corresponding skills.'

COORDINATOR VERIFIED (grep, 2026-05-30) — USER IS CORRECT. The pasture Go codebase has TWO DISJOINT halves:
(1) ORCHESTRATOR: pastured (Temporal worker) + pasture-msg (control CLI) + internal/temporal. Real (1)/(2) enforcement lives ONLY here: consensus gate (ValidateAdvance), blocker gate, VoteType enum (votes via 'pasture-msg signal vote' → RecordVote).
(2) SKILL+BD layer: internal/codegen generates skills/*/SKILL.md; agents execute via bd. Reviewer SKILL.md L278 votes via FREE-TEXT 'bd comments add <id> "VOTE: ACCEPT - ..."'. Supervisor SKILL.md uses only bd. NO skill references pasture-msg/pastured/temporal (only install-cli does).

NO BRIDGE: nothing reads bd 'VOTE:' comments → RecordVote signal. workflow_review.go does not read bd tasks. The two halves never touch. The SAME codegen that owns VoteType emits the instruction to bypass it (specs_data_body.go:1876).

IMPLICATION (reframes mh4ek verdict): In the execution model agents ACTUALLY use (skill+bd), even C-review-consensus and C-review-binary are (3) prompt-only — their (1)/(2) enforcement exists only in the orchestrator, which the agent workflow never invokes. Only C-actionable-errors genuinely binds at runtime — and only for the pasture TOOLS' OWN error output (internal/* packages), not protocol artifacts.

=> Bucket A revised: C-actionable-errors = confirmed-enforced (scope: tool errors). C-review-binary + C-review-consensus = enforced-ONLY-IF-orchestrated; (3) prompt-only in the skill+bd path. The gap-vs-design verdict for the whole audit now hinges on: IS the Temporal orchestrator intended to be in the loop, or is skill+bd the primary model? Surfacing to user as the pivotal question.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE 11 UAT (mh4ek) — PIVOTAL ARCHITECTURE DECISION (user, 2026-05-30).

QUESTION presented: 'Orchestrator (pastured/pasture-msg) has real (1)/(2) enforcement but skills never invoke it + no bd<->Temporal bridge. What is the INTENDED relationship between orchestrator and skill+bd agent workflow?' Options: orchestrator-primary-not-wired / skill+bd-primary-orchestrator-optional / bridge-the-two / defer-to-vji97.

USER RESPONSE (verbatim): 'Skill+bd is the primary model; orchestrator is optional/future observability' + elaboration: 'The current skills / agents / schema are the prioritized, near-term driver. Once we have all of the generators for these ported to Golang, the multi-agent orchestrator should be the primary driver, integrated with running agents via skills + hooks.'

=> PHASED ARCHITECTURE (binding decision rule for mh4ek verdict):
- NEAR-TERM (now): skill+bd is primary. Enforcement layers that COUNT now = (a) generated SKILL.md guidance (3), (b) pasture-task CLI validation, (c) Claude Code hooks. Priority = finish porting the generators (skill-gen, schema-gen) to Go.
- FUTURE (after all generators ported to Go): Temporal orchestrator becomes primary driver, integrated with agents via skills + hooks. The orchestrator's (1)/(2) gates (consensus, blocker, VoteType) activate THEN.

DECISION RULE for each constraint's disposition:
- Enforced by type/convention regardless of orchestrator (e.g. C-actionable-errors via StructuredError on tool errors) => confirmed-enforced.
- Workflow-state gates living in orchestrator (consensus, blocker, clean-review-exit, max-cycles, worker-quality-gates) => by-design: near-term SKILL.md guidance, FUTURE orchestrator enforcement. Not a near-term gap.
- Agent-judgment constraints (explore-ephemeral, vertical-slices, ure-verbatim, integration-points, followup-*, severity-*, etc.) => by-design: SKILL.md guidance is the intended near-term layer.
- Mechanically checkable in CLI (dep-direction, naming regex, leaf>=1, slice-review-before-close, never-delete) or hook (agent-commit, supervisor-no-impl) => CANDIDATE near-term enforcement upgrades; user decides per-item whether to machine-back now vs leave as guidance.

mh4ek verdict moves PROVISIONAL -> RESOLVED-QUALIFIED: audit documents the two-worlds architecture + per-constraint near-term enforcement layer. Continuing per-item walk for the CLI/hook candidates.

text:
PLAN-REVIEW B (round 2) — TECHNICAL FEASIBILITY — VOTE: ACCEPT

ROUND-1 RESOLUTION:
- B-B1 (D4 delete) RESOLVED: change #2 + D4' remove the delete; sup-review-severity-groups/impl-rev-b3 PROMOTED to frag-rev-severity-groups. Verified the delete would have dangled 'Per [...]' refs at specs_data_body.go:605 (supervisor) and :1986 (impl-review) and stripped the directive from supervisor+impl-review (C-severity-eager renders only into reviewer via roleConstraints).
- B-I1 (owner-key namespace) RESOLVED: owners derived; keys in SkillBodySpecs dir-key space (map keyed by dir-string @specs_data_body.go:12; render lookups @skills.go:447 string(roleID) + :493 subSkillDirKey).

NEW IMPORTANT (1): Existing passing test TestSkillBodySpecsCompleteness (specs_test.go:332) iterates SkillBodySpecs[key].Sections/.Behaviors and asserts non-empty Title/Content (lines 405/410) + non-empty behavior ID/Given/When/Then/ShouldNot (lines 426-435). Proposal says 'mirrored Go tests' but does not call out updating THIS existing test to skip FragmentID-only marker entries. Mechanical fix, but must be in SLICE-3/4 scope. (Note: ValidateSkillStructure @markdown.go:54 operates on RENDERED markdown post-resolution, so it does NOT choke on markers — only this struct-level test does.)

Already surfaced for UAT (D1); flagging for the record.

SINGLE-SOURCE FEASIBILITY: OK.
- Markers coexist+resolve: []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec are plain ordered slices; pre-render pass at skills.go:447/:493 swaps markers for resolved fragments before ctx assignment — placement preserved (slice order), deterministic.
- FragmentToOwnerRefs(): direct analog of working ConstraintToRoleRefs() (context.go:577) inverting a consumer-keyed map. Feasible.
- Checks runnable at tools/codegen/main.go: already collects errors + os.Exit(1); add ValidateGlobalIDs() before the loop to fail go generate. Feasible.

EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED: severity-tree prose is BYTE-IDENTICAL (len=1525) after canonicalizing the Per[] ref; all 6 review-behavior pairs (sup-review-* <-> impl-rev-b1..b6) are byte-identical in G/W/T/ShouldNot (only IDs differ).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE-4 PLAN REVIEW ROUND 2 — Reviewer C (ELEGANCE / complexity-matching lens). Independent Opus re-review of PROPOSAL-2 (revises PROPOSAL-1 after 3/3 REVISE). Verified against code: context.go (roleConstraints/ConstraintToRoleRefs), specs.go (SkillBody/ProseSection/BehaviorSpec), skills.go:447-451/495-497 (body→ctx copy), templates/skill.go.tmpl:198-217 (range BodyBehaviors/BodySections), specs_data_body.go (dup clusters + Per[...] cross-refs).

VOTE: ACCEPT

ROUND-1 RESOLUTION (C-I1/C-I2/C-I3/C-M1/C-M2):
- C-I1 (owners-on-fragment INVERTS pattern): RESOLVED. Change#1+D1 drop `Owners`. Single source = consumer placement markers (consumer-keyed, exactly like roleConstraints[role]={cid}); FragmentToOwnerRefs() is the DERIVED inversion, mirroring ConstraintToRoleRefs() verbatim. Faithful single-source mirror. No residual dual-source.
- C-I2 (dual-source + reconciliation): RESOLVED. §5 states "NO reconciliation check (ownership definitional)"; D1 "Removes dual-source + the reconciliation check." Clean.
- C-I3 (D4 conflates rendering surfaces — the BLOCKER): RESOLVED. Change#2 → D4' promote-not-delete. Verified: C-severity-eager lives ONLY in roleConstraints[RoleReviewer] (context.go:151; supervisor count=0), so deleting sup-review-severity-groups/impl-rev-b3 would strip the directive from supervisor+impl-review (they never receive it via the constraint) AND dangle Per[...] prose at specs_data_body.go:605/:1986. Promote-and-share is correct.
- C-M1 (one-payload validated not commented): RESOLVED. §1 "exactly one payload per Kind (VALIDATED, not commented)" + §5(c) in ValidateGlobalIDs.
- C-M2 (frag-{domain}-* naming): RESOLVED. Change#6 + migration table use frag-rev-* throughout.

NEW BLOCKER: none.
NEW IMPORTANT: none.

MINOR (non-blocking):
- M1: Change#3 cross-ref canonicalization rewrites prose 'Per [sup-review-severity-groups]'/'Per [impl-rev-b3]' to the canonical frag id. Since the behavior template renders **[{{.ID}}]** literally (skill.go.tmpl:200), the canonical id (e.g. frag-rev-severity-groups) becomes the VISIBLE marker text in every consumer — D7 acknowledges this. The user-facing prose will read "Per [frag-rev-severity-groups]" — slightly less mnemonic than the old role-scoped id, but it IS the only way to make shared prose strictly-identical (R3) and is correct. Worth a golden-diff eyeball at UAT that the rendered phrasing reads naturally.
- M2: SLICE-5 (R7) leaves "in-epoch vs follow-on" to UAT. Fine, but the slice's only deliverable (extend ValidateGlobalIDs to agent/role-behavior/handoff namespace) overlaps SLICE-2's validator. If kept in-epoch, fold into SLICE-2 to avoid a near-empty slice; if deferred, drop SLICE-5 from this plan. Either is clean — flag for UAT.

MARKER-MECHANISM ELEGANCE (struct-overload vs distinct FragmentRef):
The marker is a ProseSection/BehaviorSpec with only FragmentID set, acting as an in-slice placeholder. This IS a mild type-overload (the struct is both content-carrier and ref). A distinct tiny `FragmentRef{ID string}` type would be more self-documenting and would let the validator distinguish "ref" from "malformed empty section" structurally rather than by zero-value sniffing. HOWEVER the overload is JUSTIFIED here: (a) SkillBody.Sections/Behaviors are typed []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec — a FragmentRef would force a third slice or an interface, complicating SkillBody and the templates; (b) D5's whole value is templates-unchanged + pre-render resolution; a separate ref type breaks that by adding a new field/branch. The overload keeps the marker at the exact slice position with zero template churn, and ValidateGlobalIDs §5(b) already enforces "every FragmentID marker resolves," so the zero-value-sniff is checked, not silent. RECOMMENDATION: keep the overload as proposed; it matches the existing []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec grain and is the lower-complexity choice. Optionally (MINOR) add a helper constructor (e.g. fragRef(id) / behaviorRef(id)) in the registry so call sites read as refs, not half-empty structs — pure readability, no type change.

COMPLEXITY-MATCH vs URD: Proportionate. Registry mirrors ConstraintSpecs (R2/R4); strictly-identical via distinct fragments not parameterization (R3 — no override knobs); build-time hard error mirrors existing validator grain (R5); promote-not-delete preserves the 29-skill no-regression priority (P1). No over-reach (no plugin system, no per-consumer variation). No under-reach (one-payload + resolve + uniqueness all build-failed, not test-only). R7 appropriately minimal post-rescope (audit found agents source RoleSpec.Behaviors / handoffs are field-driven → no shareable body-prose there today, so SLICE-5 is just namespace-uniformity, not a second mechanism). Slice breakdown (mechanism → validator → behavior-migrate+canonicalize → vote-options/blocker-dual-parent reconcile → R7 namespace) is a clean dependency order.

NEW INCONSISTENCY from the revision: none found. The revision is internally consistent; the canonical picks + one-payload validation + derived owners all align with the roleConstraints precedent.

SUMMARY: PROPOSAL-2 correctly adopts the round-1 simplification (drop Owners; derive owners from consumer placement markers as the inverse of consumer-keyed inclusion), faithfully mirroring ConstraintSpec/roleConstraints/ConstraintToRoleRefs. The D4 BLOCKER is resolved by promote-not-delete with verified rationale (C-severity-eager is reviewer-only). One-payload is validated; naming adopted; no dual-source residue. The marker struct-overload is the justified low-complexity choice given the existing []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec template grain. Zero BLOCKER, zero IMPORTANT → ACCEPT. Two MINOR (canonical-id prose readability eyeball at UAT; SLICE-5 fold-or-defer) are non-blocking.

Over/under-engineering: parity enforcement is proportionate (build-fail + test = the user's explicit 'YES' decision; makes 'one source of truth' a compile guarantee, not belt-and-suspenders). Nothing speculative beyond typed-refs + parity.

Note (doc accuracy, not a code issue): description says it mirrors 'RoleId/PhaseId/CommandId' — there is NO CommandId type in the codebase (CommandSpec.Id is bare string, comment-only 'CommandId wire value' at specs.go:153). author: David Huu Pham
text:
## URE — Verbatim Q&A record (3 rounds, AskUserQuestion)

### Round 1

#### Q1 [I7 clean exit]
Q: "I7 (clean-review exit) vs the existing 3-cycle cap. Today the protocol caps review-fix cycles at 3 per slice, and PROCESS.md allows exiting after cycle 3 'with IMPORTANT findings remaining → FOLLOWUP; proceed' — meaning the very last fixes might never get re-reviewed. Your feedback says a wave MUST end on a clean re-review round. How should these reconcile?"
Options presented:
  - "Re-review is exempt from cap": 3-cycle cap counts only fix-generating rounds; a final fix-free re-review always required, doesn't count to cap; BLOCKERs block, IMPORTANTs may still defer after clean re-review.
  - "Hard clean or escalate": MUST end 0 BLOCKER+0 IMPORTANT via fresh reviewers; if cycle 3 dirty, escalate to architect; remove proceed-dirty.
  - "Keep cap, add re-review gate only": leave 3-cycle+FOLLOWUP as-is, just require fixes re-reviewed once before close.
A (verbatim, custom): "Remove cap for now, unlimited cycles"

#### Q2 [I6 fix workflow]
Q: "I6 (fix-request validation cases). How heavyweight should fix-type handling be — eliciting validation cases in the URE, confirming them in the UAT, and turning failing real-data cases into fixtures during implementation?"
Options: "Full lifecycle + new axis" (request-type axis fix|feature|chore|refactor; URE elicits validation cases, UAT confirms, workers evaluate+fixture failing cases; new C-fix-validation-cases + shared fragment) / "Lightweight, no new axis" / "Elicit + confirm only".
A (verbatim): "Full lifecycle"

#### Q3 [I10 scope]
Q: "I10 (SendMessage tool grant). Which generated agent definitions should receive the SendMessage tool in their frontmatter?"
Options: "All 5 roles" (epoch, architect, supervisor, worker, reviewer) / "Supervisor + worker + epoch" / "Supervisor + worker only".
A (verbatim): "All 5 roles"

#### Q4 [I3 strength]
Q: "I3 (interface-first decomposition) — strength of the rule. Combined with I9 (slices may have any number of leaf tasks)."
Options: "Soft preference" / "Strong SHOULD + rationale" (architect SHOULD default to interface-first slice, must justify linear in IMPL_PLAN) / "Hard rule".
A (verbatim): "Strong SHOULD + rationale"

### Round 2

#### Q5 [I7 clean def]
Q: "Since I7 removes the cycle cap (iterate until clean), what exactly defines 'clean' for closing a review wave? Today 'clean' = 0 BLOCKER + 0 IMPORTANT, with MINOR allowed to defer to a FOLLOWUP epic."
Options: "0 BLOCKER + 0 IMPORTANT" (IMPORTANTs must be fixed, only MINOR defers; iterate until holds) / "0 BLOCKER only" (IMPORTANTs may defer after re-review).
A (verbatim): "0 BLOCKER + 0 IMPORTANT"

#### Q6 [I7 safety valve]
Q: "With no hard cap, how do we guard against an infinite review-fix loop without re-introducing 'proceed dirty'?"
Options: "Advisory escalation, never auto-proceed" / "Pure unlimited" (no valve, iterate until clean, rely on human interruption) / "Escalate to architect re-plan after K".
A (verbatim): "Pure unlimited"

author: David Huu Pham
text:
USER DIRECTIVE (verbatim): "We should also include the syncing of the marketplace with the ./bin/pasture-release sync-versions as well"

Decision: extend `pasture-release registry sync-versions` so it ALSO reconciles each registered plugin's cross-repo marketplace entry — not just intra-plugin file drift (which is all it does today via DiscoverVersionFiles).

Proposed behavior:
- For each registered plugin: read its canonical version (plugin.json = SoT), then look up its registered marketplace entry (FindPlugin already returns the MarketplaceEntry) and compare the entry's version.
- If drifted, report a VersionDrift and (unless --dry-run) write the corrected version into the marketplace's plugins[<name>].version, leaving the marketplace's own metadata.version untouched (same rule as the --plugin step-9 sync).
- Keep file-write-only semantics (no auto commit/push); existing --dry-run flag applies.
- This would have caught the v0.0.1→0.0.2 drift this task came from (sync-versions said "version-consistent" because it ignored the marketplace entry).

Immediate manual fix already applied: marketplace pasture entry bumped 0.0.1→0.0.2 on main (aura-plugins 3c78b46); parent submodule re-pointed to released pasture main 5589bc7 (v0.0.2).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
IMPL-UAT verification (team-lead, real binary) — FOUND PRE-EXISTING BUG in non-TTY detection (guard identical since 81b6959; C1/C2 commit 7a675d0 did not introduce it):
stdinIsTTY uses `info.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice` to mean 'is a terminal'. But /dev/null is ALSO a character device -> misdetected as a TTY. Observed (at 7a675d0):
  - `sync-versions </dev/null` (classic CI non-interactive) -> PROMPTS + 'Aborted' + exit 0  [WRONG; ratified C3 says error+exit1]
  - `printf 'n\n' | sync-versions` (pipe) -> errors 'refusing... non-TTY' + exit 1  [errors, but inconsistent]
Real TTY: only an actual terminal should prompt. Fix = proper isatty (golang.org/x/term IsTerminal(fd), already transitively in go.sum; or x/sys/unix IoctlGetTermios but that needs windows build-tags). Tests passed because they STUB stdinIsTTY — the DEFAULT impl is what's wrong; add a test of the real default against /dev/null + pipe + (best-effort) tty.
SAFETY: still safe (never applies unconfirmed writes); deviation is exit-code/UX (/dev/null aborts exit0 instead of error exit1). Pending user decision on dep + scope.

User confirmed (2026-06-06): DBOS supports a Go SDK AND a SQLite backend — resolves the earlier open question; DBOS (embedded durable execution, no separate server, Go+SQLite) is the leading candidate vs option 3 (plain state-machine-over-SQLite). No existing GitHub issue for orchestrator-engine buildout or provenance integration (provenance integ tracked only in bd aura-plugins-9wdwc + ROADMAP §2q). author: David Huu Pham
text: Phase-1 research done: DBOS-Go + pure-Go SQLite (SqliteSystemDB w/ modernc) CONFIRMED first-class single-machine, CGO-free, crash-recoverable. Ranking: 1) DBOS-Go+SQLite 2) plain-SQLite-state-machine 3) keep-Temporal. DBOS pre-1.0 (v0.16.0) → pin + kill-9 resume spike before commit. Full report on pasture#13. PROPOSAL-1 REVISE-1 (addresses plan-review-B REVISE; A correctness + C elegance already ACCEPT).

## Test-plan additions to SLICE-1 L4 (resolve B's two gaps)
(a) INJECTABLE git-metadata gatherer: HookRecord takes a gatherer dependency (func(sha string) (map[string]string, error), default = real-git gatherGitMeta). Unit test injects a FAKE gatherer to verify merge precedence WITHOUT shelling git: explicit --message/--author/--branch/--timestamp flags OVERRIDE git-derived values; git-derived fills only when the flag is absent.
(b) REAL-GIT integration test: git init a t.TempDir() repo + make a commit; run HookRecord with --sha ONLY (no metadata flags); assert the git-derived message/author/branch/timestamp landed in the recorded row. (c) PAYLOAD-DECODE verification: add a test helper (or inline) that SELECTs audit_events.payload and JSON-decodes it, asserting sha + each metadata key/value is present. The existing queryAuditEvent helper does NOT select the payload column, so 'metadata in payload' was previously unverifiable — this makes the assertion performable.

- Exit codes: reuse errors.ExitCode(err); the handler must errors.As-unwrap the *dispatchErrors aggregate (hooks.go) to reach the underlying *StructuredError Category (the top-level Dispatch error is not itself structured). Do NOT hand-roll a 0/1/5 switch.

VOTE: ACCEPT (Reviewer B / TEST QUALITY, round 1) — SLICE-1 epoch-6l5yo

AXIS=TestQuality BLOCKER=0 IMPORTANT=0 MINOR=3

All three REVISE-1 mandatory test-plan additions are present and the assertions are REAL (not stubs); tests compile and pass (handlers 42s, hooks 2.3s, cmd/pasture 53s, all ok). Coverage: HookRecord 87.5%, mergeMeta 100%, gatherGitMeta 100%, parse/list 100%.

REVISE-1 verification:
(a) Injectable gatherer, BOTH directions: TestHookRecord_MergePrecedence_FlagsOverrideGit (flags win where set, git fills where absent) + _GitFillsWhenFlagsAbsent (no flags → all git). Fake gatherer injected; no git shelled. Real assertions via payload decode. ✓
(b) Real-git integration: TestHookRecord_RealGit_DerivesMetadataFromCommit — git init temp repo (-b trunk) + deterministic identity + real commit, HookRecord with --sha ONLY (Gatherer nil → production gatherGitMeta via t.Chdir), asserts message/author/branch=trunk/timestamp landed. (c) Payload-decode: decodeAuditPayload SELECTs audit_events.payload, JSON-decodes, asserts sha + each metadata key/value via assertString (real value equality, not non-nil). 'metadata in payload' genuinely verified. ✓
(d) Error cases: TestHookRecord_UnknownEvent_ActionableError (asserts CategoryValidation + exit 1 + Fix lists 'git-commit') and _MissingSHA_ActionableError (whitespace-only → validation + exit 1). Actionable content asserted, not just 'an error'. ✓
Integration smoke: TestHookRecord_WritesOneGitCommitRowAndEdge — temp pasture.db dispatch asserts exactly ONE GitCommit row (event_type filter), sha in payload, exactly one ContextGit edge keyed on sha. ✓
6 git_recorder_test.go updates: STRENGTHENED not weakened — TestGitRecorder_DispatchesViaManager now asserts countAuditEventsByType(EventGitCommit)==1 (the actual row) in addition to the edge; fixture + 4 Handle tests + RegisterDefaultRecorders now dispatch HookGitCommit, mirroring production wiring. The dispatch→record path is meaningfully exercised via the new event. ✓
Principles: SUT (HookRecord + full Manager wire + real SQLite) NOT mocked; only the git gatherer dependency is faked. Observable outcomes asserted (DB rows, exit codes, error category/content). Shared fixtures (strptr, decodeAuditPayload, countContextEdges, requireValidationError). No flaky time/sleep/ordering in the new hook tests. Cobra-wiring test absence is the explicitly-DEFERRED REVISE-1 item and matches the project's handler-level convention (no cmd/* test invokes RunE). storage-exit-5 must-fail also explicitly deferred. ✓

MINOR findings (do NOT block; all severities must still reach 0 before wave close):
- MINOR-1 (hook_test.go / hook.go:198-206): the documented 'explicit empty-flag override' semantic (flag != nil but *flag=="" wins over a git-derived value) is never asserted as an observable outcome. mergeMeta shows 100% line coverage but no test distinguishes strptr("")+git-has-value → payload value is "" (override) vs git value (fill). Fix: add a case to TestHookRecord_MergePrecedence_FlagsOverrideGit with Message: strptr("") while the fake gatherer returns a non-empty message, asserting payload[message]=="". Cheap, pins the type-doc contract.
- MINOR-2 (hook_test.go:299-317): TestHookRecord_UnknownEvent uses 'if stderrors.As(err,&se)' to guard the Fix-content assertion, so if As() ever fails the supported-events check is silently skipped (the prior requireValidationError already As-asserts, but here the guard could mask a regression). - MINOR-3 (hook_test.go:233 / cmd/pasture/hook.go RunE): the cmd-layer pointer-conversion logic (Changed() → &v for the 4 optional flags, Args: cobra.NoArgs) is untested. author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEWER C (ELEGANCE & COMPLEXITY-MATCHING) — SLICE-1 round 1

AXIS=Elegance BLOCKER=0 IMPORTANT=0 MINOR=3
Gates: gofmt clean, go vet clean, go test -race PASS (handlers 47.5s, hooks 3.5s).

VOTE: ACCEPT (no BLOCKER/IMPORTANT; 3 MINOR polish items, non-blocking).

== BLOCKER (0) ==
None. The implementation builds EXACTLY to the ratified design (PROPOSAL-1 + REVISE-1 + plan-UAT): Manager-path seam, HookGitCommit enum, WithSubscribedEvents REPLACING the HookSliceCompleted default, errors.ExitCode-derived exit codes (no hand-rolled 0/1/5 switch), injectable GitMetaGatherer with flag-over-git precedence, *string absent-vs-empty flags. No design defect breaks the contract.

== IMPORTANT (0) ==
None.
- Cobra RunE -> standalone handler convention is a near-exact copy of cmd/pasture/migrate.go (code, hErr := handlers.X(); printError(hErr); exitWithCode(code); return nil). Perfect match.
- Handler-does-validation (not cobra MarkFlagRequired) matches task_events.go and is justified: keeps validation testable at handler level + yields actionable StructuredErrors. Consistent.
- *string optional flags to distinguish absent (git may fill) vs explicit-empty (override) is idiomatic and well-documented; mergeMeta encodes the precedence cleanly.
- gatherGitMeta is cleanly isolated behind the GitMetaGatherer func-type seam (injectable, best-effort, never errors). Not leaky.
- Typed SupportedHookEvent enum + hookEventBindings map is the right shape for the ratified extensible seam — minimal, statically defined, no speculative plugin machinery. Complexity proportional to the problem.
- Pre-existing lint items (dispatchErrors.Error() string-builder in hooks.go; no query_test.go exists in internal/hooks) confirmed genuinely pre-existing / untouched by this diff and correctly left out-of-scope.

== MINOR (3) ==

MINOR-C1: Stringly-typed 'sha' key duplicated in handler.
  internal/handlers/hook.go:172 — data := map[string]any{"sha": sha}.
  The hooks package already EXPORTS the canonical key as a typed constant: hooks.GitCommitDataKey = "sha" (git_recorder.go:59), and the recorder uses it everywhere (Handle reads data[GitCommitDataKey]). The handler — the producer that must agree with that consumer — hardcodes the bare string instead. This is exactly the cross-package key-drift the typed-constant convention exists to prevent.
  FIX: data := map[string]any{hooks.GitCommitDataKey: sha}.

MINOR-C2: Two-source supported-event set (slice + map keys must stay in sync).
  internal/handlers/hook.go:64-73 — supportedHookEvents []SupportedHookEvent AND hookEventBindings map[SupportedHookEvent]hooks.HookEvent both enumerate the same CLI events. The slice exists only to render an ORDERED list in errors/help; the map is the lookup. A future event must be added to BOTH (the comments say so), a two-place edit that can drift. Acceptable for one entry, but the cleaner shape is a single ordered source: derive the list from an ordered []struct{cli; hook} (or keep the map for lookup but generate the display list from a single ordered slice of pairs). Not blocking at N=1.
  FIX (optional): collapse to one ordered source of (cliEvent, hookEvent) pairs; build both the lookup and the display list from it.

MINOR-C3: cliEvent return from parseSupportedHookEvent is near-redundant.
  internal/handlers/hook.go:119,191 — parseSupportedHookEvent returns (cliEvent, hookEvent, err) but cliEvent is only used for the success Fprintf 'recorded %s event for sha %s'. Since parse trims/normalises raw into cliEvent, this is fine, but the 3-value return is slightly heavier than needed; the success message could equally print in.Event (already validated) or a single returned value. Trivial; flag only for tightness.

Naming/placement/DRY otherwise clean: file placement matches (cmd/pasture/hook.go + internal/handlers/hook.go), doc comments are substantive without boilerplate, error messages satisfy what/why/where/impact/fix and read in plain English per errors.go convention, tests assert observable DB outcomes (payload JSON decode + context_edges) not internal state, SUT not mocked (only the git gatherer injected), shared helpers (decodeAuditPayload/countContextEdges) factored. Complexity is proportional. No dead code.

Spec conformance verified:
- MANAGER PATH seam confirmed: HookRecord builds hooks.NewManager()+RegisterDefaultRecorders -> Dispatch(HookPayload{HookGitCommit}) -> GitRecorder.Handle -> RecordCommit -> tasks.RecordGitEvent. NO direct tasks.RecordGitEvent call from the handler. Matches RATIFIED design.
- Subscription = HookGitCommit ONLY via WithSubscribedEvents (replaces default). No recording regression: the old default (HookSliceCompleted) only ever received SHA-less slice payloads which Handle no-ops on, so the swap stops a guaranteed-no-op dispatch, nothing real. 6 sanctioned test updates all consistent; temporal pkg still green.
- Exit codes correct: dispatchErrors.Unwrap() []error + errors.As reaches the underlying *StructuredError; RecordGitEvent returns CategoryStorage (->5) for write failures and CategoryValidation (->1) for bad input; Handle wraps with %w preserving the chain. Storage failure cannot mis-map to 1.
- Metadata merge precedence correct: mergeMeta — non-nil flag wins (incl explicit empty), nil flag -> git fills if present&non-empty. *string distinguishes absent vs empty. No inversion, no nil-deref (default gatherer never returns nil map; flag-only path also safe).
- Actionable errors present for unknown --event (lists supported events incl git-commit) and missing --sha (what/why/where/impact/fix).
- No Temporal coupling introduced (handlers/hooks import only errors/hooks/tasks).
- Resource cleanup: defer tracker.Close()/auditDB.Close() registered immediately post-open; cover all later error + dispatch paths.

MINOR-1 internal/hooks/git_recorder.go:28,75,102,139,254ff doc comments — Stale post-graduation prose. Package doc + NewGitRecorder still say the default sub is HookSliceCompleted and "until [HookGitCommit] lands, callers stick with the default"; that future has arrived (RegisterDefaultRecorders now always overrides to HookGitCommit). Why it matters: misleading to the next maintainer about the production wiring. Fix: update the comments to state HookGitCommit is the production subscription and HookSliceCompleted is a vestigial constructor default only.

MINOR-2 internal/handlers/hook.go:248-279 gatherGitMeta — resolves against process CWD, not the sha's repo. `git show -s <sha>` and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` run in os.Getwd(); running from outside the commit's repo silently yields wrong/empty metadata (best-effort, no error — by contract). Fix: add a doc note that metadata derivation requires running inside the commit's checkout, or accept an optional repo-dir.

MINOR-3 internal/handlers/hook.go:270-275 branch derivation — records the CURRENT HEAD branch (rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD), not the branch commit <sha> belongs to. Coincide for a just-fired post-commit hook; latent gap when recording an older/foreign sha. Fix: document the "current HEAD" semantics in the helper comment.

Severity groups: IMPORTANT + MINOR(non-blocking) noted here; no BLOCKER so slice not blocked by this review on correctness axis.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URE AMENDMENT (2026-06-08, decided during Phase-4 review): the activities-table exactly-once question surfaced a binding reversal.

BACKGROUND (grounding): Provenance (the library) writes the activities table via zombiezen.com/go/sqlite; pasture/DBOS use modernc.org/sqlite (database/sql, required by DBOS Config.SqliteSystemDB *sql.DB). BOTH are pure-Go/CGO-free (the CGO driver is mattn/go-sqlite3, used by neither; zombiezen is built on modernc.org/libc). They interoperate at the FILE level (WAL) but NOT at the transaction level (different connection objects can't share a *sql.Tx). DBOS-Go v0.16.0 has NO public transactional-step API (runAsTxn is private). => exactly-once for an external row requires a deterministic idempotency key on the same connection as the write.

DECISION CHANGE — REVERSES original D5/§8 'Provenance library unmodified':
Q (architect): exactly-once for the provenance-owned activities table is blocked unless we (1) keep a pasture-owned sidecar [dual-write window], (2) bypass the library [brittle], (3) add an idempotent StartActivity to the provenance library [reverses §8], or (4) defer to #14.
User (verbatim): 'Is modernc not interoperable with zombiezen? also: we could just do this. (3) Add an idempotent StartActivity to the provenance library. Natively exactly-once, cleanest — but edits provenance, which the team froze (§8); that's #14's decision.' then 'Yes: let's do that. Should also update the URE to match.'

NEW D5/§8: the Provenance library MAY be modified ADDITIVELY (backward-compatible) for idempotent activity recording. Specifically: add StartActivityIdempotent(id ActivityID, ...) using the library's existing INSERT OR IGNORE idiom (edges.go/labels.go) + ON CONFLICT(id) DO NOTHING on activities.id (already a TEXT PRIMARY KEY — NO schema change). pasture supplies a deterministic ActivityID (uuid V5 over epoch/phase/kind/step_seq). Existing StartActivity (random uuid V7) is untouched. This pulls a small bounded piece of #14 (provenance-integration correctness) forward.

NEW validation case: exactly-once now EXTENDS to the activities table (deterministic-key idempotent insert), not just orchestration state + audit_events. Cost: provenance repo change (additive) + provenance release + pasture go.mod bump.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SLICE-2-REVIEW-B-1 (test-quality axis, reviewer-b) — VOTE: REVISE

Reviewed commit 7d8d71d vs cbcaa8a (+integration with 27c40a8). Gates run independently: gofmt clean, go vet clean, CGO_ENABLED=0 build ok, CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 green for internal/handlers (70.5s), cmd/pasture (61.1s), internal/engine (28.5s) — real on-disk t.TempDir pasture.db engines, genuinely exercised under the race detector.

What is GOOD: SUT never mocked — controller tests run a real engine + real DBOS Send; CLI tests build and exec the real pasture binary (TestMain) and assert real exit codes; query surface well covered (cmd/pasture/query_test.go seeds a real engine, reads via the compiled binary, asserts JSON fields incl. sessions + slice progress); engine layer (control_test.go) asserts projection outcomes rigorously incl. consensus gate, session idempotency (replay), slice-progress accumulation, full 12-phase round trip + audit rows; deleted mock-based handler tests were replaced by a strictly better real-engine approach in principle.

FINDINGS (1 BLOCKER / 2 IMPORTANT / 2 MINOR):
- B1 BLOCKER (aura-plugins-z9bol, dual-parented to this slice): the 4 signal happy-path tests in controller_test.go are named *_MutatesProjection but assert ONLY exit 0 from dbos.Send — no test reads the projection after a handler call. dbos.Send succeeds for ANY topic/payload, so the controller's topic/payload mapping (this slice's L1 deliverable) is unverified anywhere: engine tests bypass the controller via raw Send; CLI tests are validation-only. A wrong-topic/wrong-struct regression in dbosController would leave the whole suite green. Compounding: openController's seed poll (lines 64-73) does not t.Fatal on timeout — silent wrong-state seeding. Fix is cheap (poll-assert projection per the waitPhase pattern; for votes, assert the gated review→plan-review advance passes with handler-submitted votes).
- B2 IMPORTANT (aura-plugins-9b544): EpochCancel/terminate success path has ZERO coverage at any layer — regression vs deleted epoch_test.go (TestEpochCancel_Success/TestEpochTerminate_Success); CancelWorkflow is half the L2 lifecycle deliverable and is testable against the real engine.
- B3 IMPORTANT (aura-plugins-atupa): workflow-error → exit 3 mapping untested for every verb — regression vs deleted suite which asserted exit 3 everywhere; exit codes are public CLI API. Cheap real-engine tests: signal a never-started epoch id → assert exit 3 + CategoryWorkflow.
- B4 MINOR (aura-plugins-utbch): slice start/complete have validation-only coverage; true round-trip needs S3 sub-workflows — defensible now, but must land as an S3 acceptance item, not be forgotten.
- B5 MINOR (aura-plugins-cxa5d): internal layer label 'L6' in test-file header comments (controller_test.go:3, signals_test.go:3) violates the references rule in AGENTS.md.

Accuracy note on the completion claim: of the '17 real-engine round-trips', 12 are validation rejections on an idle controller and only 5 touch a running workflow (none asserting projection); signals_test.go has 21 test functions (6 help-surface / 14 validation / 1 success), not 23. Not a finding per se, but the round-trip framing currently overstates what the tests prove — B1 closes that gap for real.

Re-review: with B1-B3 fixed I expect to ACCEPT; B4/B5 do not block.

Signal topics: all 6 sends in internal/handlers/controller.go use protocol.SignalTopic constants (no hardcoded strings); Recv side (internal/engine/control.go) consumes advance_phase/submit_vote/register_session/slice_progress by the same constants; start_slice/complete_slice Recv correctly deferred to S3 sub-workflows per IP5 (S2 owns constants+send only). 6. No go.temporal.io in new S2 code (internal/engine, internal/handlers, cmd/pasture, pkg/protocol — grep clean).
7. Shipped code/comments/help/errors: no Beads IDs, PROPOSAL-N, §, SLICE-N in NEW shipped code; errors are plain-language actionable; the one GH cite (issues/13) is a durable URL.

FINDINGS — 0 BLOCKER / 3 IMPORTANT / 2 MINOR:
- IMPORTANT aura-plugins-yll24: 'epoch terminate --reason' accepted but silently dropped (cmd/pasture/epoch.go); regression vs pasture-msg which fed it to the terminate path and promised audit recording. Fix: record it or remove the flag.
- IMPORTANT aura-plugins-r1evw: retirement incomplete in user-facing docs — README.md:13 ('make build # produces ... bin/pasture-msg' now false), README.md:23 ('nix build .#pasture-msg' now fails), README.md:7/32, docs/VERSIONING.md, skills/install-cli/SKILL.md (install loop/go install/nix profile all target pasture-msg). install-cli edits may be barred by the 'NO skills/*/SKILL.md edits' hard guard — supervisor to rule/route.
- IMPORTANT aura-plugins-sqaqh: internal/handlers/controller_test.go *_MutatesProjection tests assert exit codes only; the L6 invariant 'signals durably mutate the projection' is never asserted through the folded handler path (only engine-level control_test.go). Add a projection-read assert (poll ReadProjection) or rename.

- MINOR aura-plugins-szz7e: StartEpoch error hint claims duplicate-id as likely cause, but dbos.RunWorkflow with an existing id is idempotent attach — hint steers users wrong.

RATIONALE FOR ACCEPT: no BLOCKER — no security issue, no test failure, no broken production code path; spec-vs-code gaps found are recoverable (flag drop, docs, test assertions) and filed with fixes. Per severity rules IMPORTANT/MINOR do not block the slice. Note for supervisor: axis-A BLOCKER group had triplicates (yqeok closed empty by me; osm1h, tcb5i are duplicates needing disposition). Interim daemonless UX note (not a finding, by design per controller.go comment): side-channel signals reach the projection only when a host process drains them (next advance or 30s-idle host), so 'signal vote' → immediate 'query state' can read stale — durable, eventually consistent.

author: David Huu Pham
text: Architect RULING (binding, mechanism precise): RECORD the reason via the NON-DEDUP audit path. The cancel HANDLER records an EpochCancelled/EpochTerminated audit event carrying the reason via the existing legacy RecordEvent path (NULL dedup_key — explicitly supported + coexistence-tested), attributed to a STABLE existing agent (engine agent fine; ensure the agent row exists for the FK), THEN performs CancelWorkflow. Rationale: (1) the engine-owns-forensic invariant is about REPLAYED workflow steps needing deterministic dedup keys — a CLI cancel is a one-shot action, so the non-dedup path is exactly right, NO DedupKey involved; (2) record-then-force-cancel beats a terminate signal because cancel often targets a wedged workflow where a signal wouldn't fire. Small lift (one RecordEvent + agent attribution + CancelWorkflow); fallback if it balloons = drop the flag + P3 follow-up. Bonus: the cancellation event surfaces in the status surface later. Echo-only REJECTED.

CLI test (TestCLI_EpochCancel_WorkflowError_NonexistentEpoch): invokes 'pasture epoch cancel --epoch-id <never-started-id>' and asserts exit code 3.

DEVIATION: The original finding proposed testing PhaseAdvance/SignalVote/SliceStart/SliceComplete against unstarted epochs for exit 3. However, these handlers use dbos.Send which is fire-and-forget — it inserts a notification row and returns nil even when the destination workflow does not exist (the FK violation is logged server-side but never returned to the caller). Exit 3 via the Send path is structurally unreachable. Only CancelWorkflow (which blocks on engine state) reliably returns a nonexistent-workflow error. Coverage of CategoryWorkflow → exit 3 is achieved via EpochCancel at both handler and CLI level.

text: PARITY EVIDENCE (supervisor brief asked for Temporal-original comparison): the Temporal original (internal/temporal/workflow_slice.go:144-161) delegates tmux/subprocess to the 'execute_slice_command' activity with a real StartToCloseTimeout. text:
## s1_1 Classification (4 axes)

- **Scope: MEDIUM-LARGE.** 5 heterogeneous items spanning: Go code in pasture (item 1, cmd/pasture-release error message), protocol constraint/doc authoring (items 2, 3, 4 — codegen pipeline specs_data + hand-authored protocol docs), and agent-topology/skill restructuring (item 5 — standing reviewer team, per-role model selection, epoch subsuming roles). Comparable in shape to the previous improvements.md epoch (r1cdc, I1–I10).
- **Complexity: MODERATE.** Item 1 is trivial (single error-string + test). Items 2–4 are constraint-propagation work (attach-by-ID per references standard, codegen regen). Item 5 is the hard one: changes the epoch/reviewer/worker orchestration topology and model assignments — touches multiple SKILL.md generators and the team-spawning instructions.
- **Risk: MEDIUM.** Items 2–4 alter instructions consumed by every future agent run (regression risk = degraded agent behavior, caught at review/UAT). Item 5 changes live orchestration topology; a wrong design can break review waves. No data-loss/security surface.
- **Domain novelty: LOW.** Same domain as the prior improvements epoch — pasture skills, codegen (specs_data_body.go / specs_data.go), protocol docs. Known patterns and prior art exist in-repo (references standard pasture#19, epoch I1–I10 PR #6).

**Ambiguity flagged for URE (Phase 2):** Item 2 (test quality/speed) shows logs from agent-data-leverage/peasant, a different repo. Candidate interpretations: (a) encode test-quality/test-speed design principles as pasture protocol constraints for workers/reviewers; (b) audit pasture's own Go test suite; (c) actual peasant test work (out of scope for a pasture worktree). To be resolved at URE.

- kvs4r facts: recovery_test.go is //go:build recovery; killCycle harness forks victim, SIGKILLs mid-step, resumes; waits via armProbeReadySignal + waitForProbeReadySignal(t, ready, 60s) — signal/bounded-timeout, ZERO time.Sleep. Reusing this harness + real on-disk SQLite is exactly right; no reinvention.

Re-review will be fast: the only change needed is the hook_test.go serial carve-out in R5 + its acceptance criteria.

text: REVIEWER-B (test-quality) ACCEPTS architect's fix A′: replace the inline RunAsStep block with a real e.emitVoteRecorded(...) call + inject the kill-stall at the audit.Trail seam (delegating wrapper whose RecordEventReturningId does the real inner write THEN stalls on the 3rd VoteRecorded write when stall>0). author: David Huu Pham
text:
ROUND-2 RESOLUTION (architect-adjudicated, 2026-06-15) — AGREED FIX = A′ + MINOR-waiver. Consensus: reviewer-b (test-quality) ACCEPT + reviewer-c (elegance) ACCEPT.

ARCHITECT CATCH (corrected both candidate approaches): exactly-once-under-replay is only exercised if the SIGKILL lands INSIDE the vote step (after the INSERT, before DBOS records the step complete) so resume re-runs the closure → 2nd INSERT → DedupKey/ON-CONFLICT collapse. Reviewer-b's plain-A (stall in a SEPARATE RunAsStep) and reviewer-c's naive-B (stall at Recv-block / on the post-drain transition) BOTH move the kill OUTSIDE the vote step → 3 votes commit → resume replays from memo without re-running the INSERT → ON-CONFLICT never exercised → coverage gutted. The transition probe avoids this via the in-step OnTransition seam; the vote path has NO such seam (HookVoteRecorded declared hooks.go:40 but ZERO production dispatch — confirmed). The inline copy was FORCED, not lazy.

SEAM USED: the injected audit.Trail. emitVoteRecorded (workflow.go:164/176-190) calls e.trail.RecordEventReturningId INSIDE its real dbos.RunAsStep, and e.trail=cfg.Trail (engine.go:189/254, exported e.Trail()) is an injected dependency → a delegating Trail wrapper stalling on the 3rd vote write lands the kill inside the REAL vote step. Zero production change.

AGREED FIX A′:
1. recovery_vote_test.go: replace the inlined RunAsStep+DedupKey+RecordEventReturningId block (lines 155-184) with a real call: e.emitVoteRecorded(ctx, in.EpochID, protocol.PhaseReview, protocol.ReviewVoteSignal{Axis:axis, Vote:protocol.VoteAccept, ReviewerId:reviewerID}, stepSeq). The REAL emitVoteRecorded becomes the SUT (real DedupKey arg order, real RunAsStep wrapping, real payload shape).
2. Add a delegating audit.Trail wrapper (5 methods: RecordEvent, RecordEventReturningId, QueryEvents, RecordSessionEntries, QuerySessionEntries — delegate to inner tracker). In RecordEventReturningId: do the REAL inner write FIRST, then if event.EventType==EventVoteRecorded AND it is the 3rd such physical write AND stall>0 → signalRecoveryVoteReady() + bounded stall (select time.After/ctx.Done). Build helper engine with Trail: stallTrail, Tracker: tracker.

CAVEATS (reviewer-b, hard requirements):
C1. Inner write FIRST, THEN stall (INSERT must be durably on disk before the kill).
C2. Counter = physical inner VoteRecorded writes; stall only on the 3rd when stall>0. Resume (stall=0) never stalls; DBOS replays only the incomplete 3rd step → exactly 1 physical re-write → ON-CONFLICT collapse.
C3. Post-replay assertion: exactly len(protocol.AllReviewAxes)=3 VoteRecorded rows with distinct dedup keys + keep existing before/after reflect.DeepEqual.

CAVEAT (reviewer-c):
C4. Stall is process-local (victim stalls on 3rd write; resumer stall=0 delegates straight through, no re-block on replay), mirroring the OnTransition stall/signalReady pattern. Keep //go:build recovery; verify 'go test -tags recovery ./internal/engine/' is actually run (off the normal make test path).

DISPOSITION OF MINOR (helper-dup): WAIVED as structurally forced — A′ must be package engine (white-box) to reach unexported e.emitVoteRecorded; recovery_test.go is package engine_test (black-box); helpers can't cross the boundary; the cure would breach S4's file-ownership (editing recovery_test.go, outside S4's column) — disproportionate for a P4 OPTIONAL test. MINOR → 0 by waiver. Both reviewers explicitly agree.

B-correct (drive real EpochControlWorkflow black-box) considered + declined: higher fidelity (pins control.go:150 drain loop + clears MINOR by fix) but requires walking the control workflow through phase gates to reach review — disproportionate for a P4 optional completeness test. Neither reviewer insists on it.

text:
VOTE: REVISE (axis C — decomposition/elegance). IMPL_PLAN yl0y8, 6 slices / 13 leaves.

WHAT'S RIGHT (confirmed):
- Spatial file-ownership is collision-free for PARALLEL leaves. harness.go is EXCLUSIVE to S1-L1 (ak9sn); S2-S5 each own their own component file and never edit harness.go; S6 owns nix only. Within S1 the 4 leaves own disjoint files (harness.go / skills.go / main.go / harness_test.go+testdata). After S1 closes, S2-S6 impl+test leaves own pairwise-disjoint files.
- Stub->fill pattern is sound: ak9sn scaffolds the 4 component files + 2 templates as COMPILING stubs and writes the FULL OpenCodeTarget literal up-front (referencing the stub symbols); each S*-L1 later fills the BODY of its own stub. This is the 'S1 pre-wires field assignments' option from PROPOSAL §4 — the cleaner one — so my earlier c1 concern is fully resolved (no slice edits the shared literal). The shared-file touch (scaffold then fill) is strictly SEQUENCED via S2-S6 gating on SLICE-1 closure, not a parallel collision.
- Gating/DAG: IMPL_PLAN blocked-by 6 slices; each slice blocked-by its leaves; S2-S6 leaves blocked-by SLICE-1 so the foundation lands first. bd ready correctly shows ONLY S1's 4 leaves. Interface-first holds (S1 compiles + byte-identical golden guard before any OpenCode bytes).
- Granularity proportional: no trivial 1-line leaves, no leaf doing 3 unrelated things; models.dev snapshot as its own leaf (iyvgw) is justified (distinct committed artifact + catalog-existence test). Slice order R1->emitters->nix sound.

TWO BLOCKING DECOMPOSITION GAPS (fix before handoff):

GAP-1 — registry lives in the WRONG package, making S1-L4's assigned tests unreachable within its file ownership. S1-L3 (l12xx) puts harnessRegistry + the unregistered-harness 'fail fast listing claude-code,opencode' resolution in tools/codegen/main.go (package main). But S1-L4 (sveg1) OWNS only internal/codegen/harness_test.go (package codegen) and is tasked with the combined -targets=claude-code,opencode routing test (b3) AND the unregistered-harness error test. package codegen CANNOT import package main — so sveg1 cannot write its assigned tests without either editing main.go (collision with l12xx) or acquiring a tools/codegen test file (ownership change). This also DIVERGES from the in-repo precedent: acp.GetAdapter + its registry + its unknown-format test all live in package acp (internal/acp/adapter.go + adapter_test.go), NOT in a main. FIX: move harnessRegistry + a ResolveHarness(targets string) ([]TargetHarness, error) (actionable unknown-harness error mirroring acp.GetAdapter) into harness.go (S1-L1/ak9sn, package codegen); main.go (l12xx) only parses -targets and calls codegen.ResolveHarness then loops. Then sveg1's routing + error tests are all reachable in package codegen, main.go stays thin, and the design matches the adapter.go precedent (more elegant too).

GAP-2 — per-slice TEST leaves are not blocked-by their IMPL leaves, but each leaf runs 'make test' gates before commit. In SLICE-2 the test (klr5q: asserts 29 valid OpenCode skills w/ real frontmatter+body) and the impl (husd5: real templates) are UNORDERED siblings (both only blocked-by SLICE-1). A parallel worker on klr5q runs 'make test' against S1's PLACEHOLDER templates -> red gates -> stuck/STOP. Same shape in S3 (mxcxr/iyvgw test vs pig3c impl), S4 (6d0gj vs 45gf2), S5 (5dfox vs oxbre). FIX (either): (a) chain each test leaf blocked-by its impl leaf — bd dep add klr5q --blocked-by husd5; mxcxr/iyvgw --blocked-by pig3c; 6d0gj --blocked-by 45gf2; 5dfox --blocked-by oxbre — OR (b) merge each slice's impl+test into ONE leaf (TDD-cohesive, still collision-free since one worker owns both the impl file and its _test.go; matches the 'name leaves after real work units' guidance).

Everything else is ACCEPT-quality; these are two targeted fixes, not a structural redo.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

## Axis: Hygiene / Decomposition — Reviewer B (Round 1)

Reviewed PROPOSAL-1 (05myu), URD (92jd2), REQUEST (pbrl8) against pasture main checkout (9228c10). Verified all 5 slices' cited files directly (internal/release/{runner.go,git.go}; cmd/pasture-release/{main_test.go,testdata/cli_smoke.yaml}; internal/config/{viper.go,viper_test.go,config_test.go}; internal/testutil/env.go; internal/handlers/controller.go + epoch.go/phase.go/session.go/signal.go/slice.go; cmd/pasture/{epoch,phase,session,signal,slice}.go).

### IMPORTANT-1 — SLICE-4 file-ownership list materially undercounts real footprint
Files cited: "internal/handlers/controller.go (+ cmd/pasture controller callers as needed)". Verified: OpenEpochController is called via a SINGLE shared helper `runWithController` (defined once in cmd/pasture/epoch.go) that is invoked from **5** cmd/pasture files (epoch.go x3, signal.go x2, slice.go x2, session.go x1, phase.go x1 — 8 call sites total). Each of the corresponding **5** internal/handlers/*.go modules (epoch.go, phase.go, session.go, signal.go, slice.go) independently couples its own argument-validation (requireEpochID / validateEpochID / sliceId checks) with a ctrl-taking function signature — the exact "validate is downstream of ctrl-open" shape D4 targets exists identically in all 5, not just epoch.go. An architecturally-correct fix (validate before runWithController opens ctrl) requires decoupling validation from ctrl construction in all 5 handler modules and reworking the single shared `runWithController`/RunE call sites accordingly — that's ~11 files, not "controller.go + as needed". Recommend the plan enumerate them explicitly so a worker doesn't under-scope to epoch.go alone.

### IMPORTANT-2 — SLICE-4 DoD test is epoch-shaped only; risks leaving phase/session/signal/slice with the identical stray-db bug
URD DoD: "add a test — invalid args -> error returned AND db path does not exist" (singular). Given IMPORTANT-1, if only the epoch verbs get fixed+tested, `pasture phase advance --epoch-id ""` / `pasture signal vote ...` / `pasture slice start` etc. with invalid args still create a stray db — the same end-user-visible bug the URD's own framing describes generically ("engine opened before handler validation; stray db on invalid invocation"), not epoch-specific. Recommend the DoD require representative no-db-side-effect coverage across all 5 verb families (or explicitly scope D4 down to epoch-only in the URD/proposal, if that's the intended MVP cut — as currently written the URD text and the DoD test don't agree on scope).

### MINOR-1 — SLICE-2 "negative-control case" implies a schema addition not called out
DoD: "add a negative-control case (stderr substring absent from stdout)" / FAIL(wrong) criterion needs an assertion of absence. Current smokeCaseFixture (main_test.go) only has Contains-style fields (want_stdout_contains / want_stderr_contains); there's no not-contains assertion today. Recommend the plan explicitly note a schema addition (e.g. want_stdout_not_contains / want_stderr_not_contains, or an equivalent hardcoded Go negative-control subtest) so the "regression to merged buffers would fail" property is actually falsifiable rather than left to worker interpretation.

### MINOR-2 — SLICE-3 shared-file risk (internal/testutil/env.go) not covered by the per-slice gate
Plan says SLICE-3 "possibly" touches internal/testutil/env.go. Verified SetEnv/UnsetEnv/SetHermeticEnv in that file are consumed by internal/engine, internal/tasks, internal/audit, internal/handlers, cmd/pastured, cmd/pasture, internal/config — 7+ packages. The per-slice gate is scoped to `go test -race ./internal/config/...`, which would not catch a regression in shared testutil surfaced elsewhere. Not blocking (the proposal's batch-level "one authoritative build+test at the end" is the real safety net) — but call this out for the SLICE-3 worker: prefer keeping the DI refactor additive/scoped to a new internal/config-local file over editing shared env.go, and if env.go must change, run a full `go test ./...` before treating SLICE-3 as done rather than waiting for the batch-end gate.

### MINOR-3 — SLICE-3's "no t.Parallel() touches os.Setenv" DoD is not guaranteed by `-race` alone
`go test -race` only flags *actual* concurrent conflicting access; a lone parallel test calling os.Setenv without another concurrently-running parallel test touching the same var may pass `-race` cleanly despite violating the DI boundary. This is enforced today by code review / the AGENTS.md principle SLICE-5 documents, not by an automated gate. Not blocking — just flagging that "-race green" is necessary but not sufficient evidence for this specific DoD line.

### Clean areas (no findings)
- File ownership across SLICE-1/2/3/5 is disjoint; no two slices touch the same file directly.
- SLICE-5-after-SLICE-3 is the only real ordering dependency; SLICE-1/2/4 are correctly independent.
- No internal refs (Beads IDs / SLICE-N / PROPOSAL-N) found smuggled into any slice's shipped-artefact scope; the URD's origin_finding reference lives in Beads description frontmatter only (correct per C-frontmatter-refs). AGENTS.md target content (testdata/, LoadFixtures, FixtureName) are real, verified symbols in internal/testutil/fixtures.go.
- Single-shared-checkout staging discipline is sound for SLICE-1/2/3/5; no shared generated/lock files anticipated (no new deps required by any slice as scoped).

## Fix suggestion
Revise SLICE-4's file list to enumerate all 5 handlers/*.go + 5 cmd/pasture/*.go files, and either broaden the DoD test to cover all verb families or explicitly narrow D4's scope to epoch-only in both URD and proposal text (pick one, make it explicit). SLICE-2/3 items are non-blocking suggestions to tighten falsifiability — happy to ACCEPT once SLICE-4's scope is made explicit.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: ACCEPT

Reviewed as axis C (elegance / end-user / maintainability) against PROPOSAL-1 (05myu), URD (92jd2), and the pasture code at internal/config/{viper,config}.go, internal/handlers/controller.go+epoch.go, cmd/pasture/{epoch,session,slice,phase,signal}.go, cmd/pasture-release/main_test.go + testdata/cli_smoke.yaml, internal/release/{runner,git}.go.

No BLOCKER-level issues. Two actionable non-blocking findings for the SLICE-3 and SLICE-4 workers to incorporate:

1. [IMPORTANT] SLICE-3 shape — prefer "inject the OS boundary" over "hand-roll the merge". The proposal says "extract a PURE resolve(defaults, yaml, env, flags) core" — if taken literally as a from-scratch merge over raw string maps, this DISCARDS viper's native GetString/GetBool/nested-key type coercion, which every future config key would then need to reimplement by hand. That's a regression relative to the user's stated goal ("keep this architecture as it grows"): more keys = more hand-written coercion, not less. Cleaner seam, less churn, same DoD: keep viper as the merge/coercion engine inside the core, and only externalize the OS-touching inputs — file path -> bytes (viper already takes a path param; swap to v.ReadConfig(bytes.Reader) fed by the shell), and env var name -> value via an injectable lookup, e.g. `bindEnvVar(v, viperKey, envVarName string, lookupEnv func(string) (string, bool))` that calls `v.Set` only when found. This is the SAME idiom the file already uses for CLI flags (bindChangedFlag: manually reads cmd.Flags(), calls v.Set only if .Changed) — extending it to env is a small, idiomatic, low-risk diff, not a new abstraction. Production wires lookupEnv=os.LookupEnv; logic tests inject a fake map and run t.Parallel() with zero os.Environ access. Satisfies the URD DoD exactly (no t.Parallel() test touches os.Setenv; priority-chain assertions stay green) with far less surface area than reimplementing viper's merge by hand.

2. [IMPORTANT] SLICE-4 scope is under-described — validate-before-open touches 5 files, not ~1. `runWithController` (cmd/pasture/epoch.go) is the shared open+call path for ALL controller verbs, used by epoch.go, session.go, slice.go, phase.go, and signal.go (~8 handler verbs total). Each verb's argument validation currently lives INSIDE the handlers.XxxYyy function, which only runs AFTER runWithController has already opened the controller/db — so the "db created on invalid invocation" wart exists in all 5 files, not just epoch.go. The proposal's file list ("controller.go + cmd/pasture controller callers as needed") doesn't name the shared seam, so a worker patching only epoch.go would leave 4/5 verb groups with the original bug. Recommend SLICE-4 explicitly design ONE shared fix at the `runWithController` seam (e.g. `runWithController(validate func() error, fn func(EpochController) (int, error)) error`, calling validate() before OpenEpochController) so all 8 verbs get validate-before-open uniformly, and widen the gate to `go test ./cmd/pasture/... ./internal/handlers/...` (all 5 files), not just the epoch-specific path.

Also verified clean, no notes needed:
- SLICE-1 (comment honesty): confirmed runner.go:224-225's comment ("so a failed release does not leave a dangling commit") overstates git.go:113 GitRollback's actual behavior (deletes tag + resets working tree; the release commit is NOT undone). Reword-only is correct, minimal, no behavior change.
- SLICE-2 (stream split): clean, low-risk, matches the user's explicit choice. The planned negative-control case (stderr substring absent from stdout) is the right adversarial check to prove real separation vs the current merged-buffer behavior.
- SLICE-3 vs SLICE-5 coherence: once (1) above is adopted, the AGENTS.md principle in SLICE-5 should read as "pass real inputs (files/env/flags) explicitly into your resolution function instead of letting library calls reach into hidden OS/global state" — a durable, generalizable principle — rather than "hand-roll your config library's merge logic," which would be bad general advice to enshrine.
- Slice granularity: 5 slices (1:1 with pre-existing beads tasks, independent except SLICE-5→SLICE-3) is right-sized — not over- or under-decomposed for this scope.

VERDICT: ACCEPT

text:
VOTE: REVISE (Reviewer A / CORRECTNESS axis, round 1)

Grounded in the actual pasture code (/home/minttea/codebases/dayvidpham/pasture/main). SLICE-1, SLICE-2, SLICE-5 are sound as written — no findings. SLICE-3 and SLICE-4 have concrete, file-cited gaps that should be folded into the proposal text before Phase-8 IMPL_PLAN authoring.

--- SLICE-1 (esqny) — ACCEPT, no findings ---
Confirmed the comment is genuinely misleading: after GitCommit() runs (runner.go:210), the working tree already matches HEAD, so GitRollback's `checkout -- .` (git.go:119) is a no-op for the commit — it only deletes the tag. The commit at runner.go:210 is left in place. Reword-only (no behavior change) matches the actual code. Sane.

--- SLICE-2 (hd0ho) — ACCEPT, no findings ---
Read cmd/pasture-release/main.go (no cmd.SetOut/SetErr override; SilenceUsage:true at line 81, SilenceErrors unset) + testdata/cli_smoke.yaml (5 cases). Cobra's default routing applies: --help → OutOrStdout() (stdout), Execute() errors → c.PrintErrln → ErrOrStderr() (stderr). Walked all 5 existing cases against this routing — none would flip when stdout/stderr are split into separate buffers:
  - help-exits-zero / check-help / registry-help / patch-help: stdout-only asserts, all satisfied by --help output (always stdout).
  - unknown-subcommand-exits-nonzero: stderr-only assert ("unknown command"), satisfied by Cobra's Find() error, which is stderr via PrintErrln.
No case currently passes by "accident" (merged-buffer false positive). Negative-control case (already in the plan) is the right additional guard.

--- SLICE-3 (p87cs) — REVISE-worthy findings ---
[IMPORTANT] internal/config/viper.go:60-95 + internal/config/testdata/config_loading.yaml (fixtures `malformed-yaml-returns-error`, `missing-file-returns-error`) — The plan's DoD doesn't call out a real behavior contract that the pure resolve() core MUST preserve: today, when v.ReadInConfig() fails (malformed YAML or missing file), resolvePasturedConfigWithFile still returns a populated cfg from defaults/env/CLI (fileErr is returned SEPARATELY, not fatal) — proven by both testdata fixtures asserting want_error:true AND want_audit_trail:"sqlite" (the default) in the same case. If the pure resolve(defaults, yaml, env, flags) core is implemented naively (e.g., short-circuits on a yaml-read error instead of treating "yaml absent/errored" as a zero-value input to the merge), these two existing fixture tests will regress. Suggested fix: add this to SLICE-3's DoD explicitly — "a YAML read error still yields default/env/CLI-driven config for the other layers; only the read error itself changes."
[IMPORTANT] internal/config/viper.go:20-33 (bindChangedFlag) — Priority-inversion risk requested by my review mandate: today, CLI-flag precedence is achieved via `v.Set()` (viper's "explicit override" tier, which outranks BindEnv's "env" tier) ONLY when `f.Changed == true` (line 30). A pure resolve() taking "flags" as one of its 4 data parameters must encode changed-ness (not just the final flag value) — otherwise an unset flag holding its cobra zero-value default would wrongly out-rank env/YAML/defaults. The plan doesn't specify this. Suggested fix: state explicitly that the "flags" parameter to resolve() is `map[string]FlagValue{Value, Changed bool}` (or equivalent, e.g. a pre-filtered map containing ONLY flags with Changed==true), mirroring today's bindChangedFlag filter.
Otherwise confirmed feasible: viper.BindEnv itself can't be fed injected env (it calls os.Getenv internally at Get-time), so achieving "zero os.Environ access in the pure core" requires bypassing viper's BindEnv facility entirely and hand-rolling the env layer in the impure shell — consistent with what the plan already implies, just want it explicit. -race cleanliness is achievable given the above.

--- SLICE-4 (j2cyq) — REVISE-worthy finding ---
[IMPORTANT, borderline BLOCKER for IMPL_PLAN] Confirmed the underlying bug via cmd/pasture/epoch.go:14-20 (`runWithController`): `handlers.OpenEpochController(flagDBPath)` — which creates+migrates the SQLite db via `audit.NewSqliteAuditTrail(dbPath)` at internal/handlers/controller.go:74 — runs BEFORE `fn(ctrl)`, and ALL handler argument validation (requireEpochID/validateEpochID in internal/handlers/epoch.go:64-139, axis.IsValid()/vote.IsValid()/mutual-exclusion checks in signal.go:19-138, mode.IsValid() in slice.go:17-118, equivalent checks in session.go and phase.go) lives INSIDE the handlers.XXX(ctrl, ...) functions, which are only invoked from inside fn(ctrl) — i.e. AFTER ctrl (and the db) already exists. This is NOT epoch-specific: the same `runWithController` helper is shared by all 5 cmd/pasture/*.go caller files (epoch.go, signal.go, slice.go, session.go, phase.go — 7 RunE closures total), confirmed by grep.
Validation itself needs nothing from ctrl (pure string/enum checks on flag values) — reordering is semantically safe. But the ORIGINAL j2cyq task (created 2026-06-10, aura-plugins-j2cyq) proposed a DIFFERENT, less invasive mechanism: "sync.OnceValues lazy construction inside dbosController; handlers/tests unchanged." URD Q4's confirmed answer explicitly REJECTED that lazy option in favor of "Reorder: validate then open" — which is the harder path precisely because it requires validation to run before ctrl is even constructed, and validation logic today is embedded inside functions that take ctrl as their first parameter.
The proposal's current scope statement ("Files: internal/handlers/controller.go (+ cmd/pasture controller callers as needed)") and DoD ("add a test — invalid args -> error returned AND db path does not exist", singular) undercounts this: it reads as an epoch-only or controller.go-only change. Suggested fix: amend SLICE-4 to (a) name the actual mechanism — e.g. split each of the 7 handler entry points into `ValidateX(args) error` + `X(ctrl, args)`, with each cmd/pasture RunE calling Validate before `runWithController`, OR give `runWithController` a `validate func() error` parameter it calls before `OpenEpochController` — and (b) state explicitly that the fix applies uniformly across all 5 caller files / 7 commands (epoch start/cancel/terminate, signal vote/complete, slice start/complete, session register, phase advance), with DoD coverage for each family, not just one epoch-path test. Otherwise a narrow implementation would only partially satisfy D4's actual wording ("the controller path... run handler argument validation BEFORE opening") which by its own text is general, not epoch-scoped.

--- SLICE-5 (7u4sg) — ACCEPT, no findings ---
testutil.FixtureName, testutil.LoadFixtures, CLISmoke/ConfigLoading constants (internal/testutil/fixtures.go) and AGENTS.md all exist and are real. Author-last-after-SLICE-3 ordering is correct so it documents the pattern SLICE-3 establishes (including the resolve()-signature clarifications above).

Actionable ask for the architect: fold the SLICE-3 and SLICE-4 findings above into PROPOSAL-2 text (mechanism + scope, not a redesign) — the underlying design decisions (D3, D4) are sound; the gaps are precision/completeness gaps that the proposal's own review posture explicitly asked this round to check ("D3 priority-chain preservation... D4 no-db-on-invalid").

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: ACCEPT (Reviewer A / CORRECTNESS axis, round 2 — re-review of PROPOSAL-2)

Verified against the actual on-disk code (still pre-refactor at review time: internal/config/viper.go untouched, package config; internal/handlers/controller.go + cmd/pasture/*.go untouched). All 3 r1 findings are resolved with technically sound mechanisms:

--- A1 (yaml-error-fallback contract) — RESOLVED ---
PROPOSAL-2 keeps viper as the merge engine and leaves ReadInConfig()/fileErr handling completely untouched (only the two v.BindEnv calls are replaced with bindEnvVar). Since the YAML file-read path and the override-tier (env/flags) path are separate internal viper stores, and neither is being touched by the other change, the two testdata/config_loading.yaml fixtures (`malformed-yaml-returns-error`, `missing-file-returns-error` — want_error:true AND audit_trail falls back to default) will continue to pass exactly as before. Confirmed sound.

--- A2 (priority-inversion risk / Changed-ness) — RESOLVED ---
bindChangedFlag is explicitly left untouched, still gated on `f.Changed` (viper.go:30) — so an unset flag never calls v.Set() and can never wrongly outrank env/YAML/defaults; that was the actual inversion risk and it's fully closed since nothing about that gate changes.
Priority proof also checks out independently: both bindEnvVar and bindChangedFlag write via v.Set(), which lands in viper's SAME "explicit override" tier — a plain last-write-wins map assignment per key (v.override[key] = value), not a merge. Calling bindEnvVar (env) BEFORE bindChangedFlag (CLI) in the same function body means: if the CLI flag is Changed, its later Set() call overwrites whatever the env Set() call wrote for that key -> CLI wins. If the CLI flag is NOT changed, bindChangedFlag makes no call at all, so the override map keeps whatever bindEnvVar wrote (or nothing) -> falls through to viper's own tier ranking (override > config(YAML) > default). Net: CLI > env > YAML > default, preserved by construction. Same mechanism the ORIGINAL v1 code already relied on for CLI-over-Config precedence, just extended one tier further (env into override) — consistent design, not a new risk.

text:
VOTE: ACCEPT — 0/0/0 (clean round)

Reviewed the round-2 delta (git diff main -- internal/config/viper.go internal/handlers/phase.go cmd/pasture/phase.go internal/handlers/controller_test.go) and ran go build/vet + go test on internal/config, internal/handlers, cmd/pasture — all green (including the new regression-guard test).

1. [2i7t4, MINOR, fixed] ValidatePhaseAdvance now returns (protocol.PhaseId, error); PhaseAdvance consumes the returned value directly, no re-parse, no discarded error. On the asymmetry question (phase is the only validator that returns a value; the other 8 return only error): this is justified, not a smell. Phase is the only verb where "validate" and "parse into canonical form" are the same operation and produce genuinely new information the op needs (ParsePhaseId resolves the p1..p12 shorthand to the canonical PhaseId). Every other validator (epoch id, session id/role, axis/vote, mode, output/error mutual-exclusion) checks an already-final typed value — there's nothing to derive, so nothing to return. Forcing the other 8 to also return a value would be artificial symmetry with no payload. The new TestHandler_PhaseAdvance_UnknownPhase_IsErrorNotSilentNoOp is a good addition too — it makes concrete why PhaseAdvance must keep self-guarding (an unrecognised phase parses to the zero-value PhaseId, which the engine would otherwise silently no-op on), which is exactly the "defense-in-depth has a real payoff, not just decoration" case I was implicitly trusting in round 1. Confirmed clean.

2. [drao5, MINOR, fixed] bindEnvVar + bindChangedFlag folded into one per-key table/loop in resolvePasturedConfigWithFile. For 2 keys this is not overkill — it's proportionate to the exact problem it closes (ordering safety). It's still a plain compile-time literal (no interfaces, no runtime config, no generics), doesn't touch the type-coercion path (that's still v.GetString(...) below, correctly left alone), and it makes the AGENTS.md "a future key is just add a row" claim literally true instead of convention-true. A future key that gets the two binds in the wrong order would have to actively write them backwards inside the same loop body — much harder to do by accident than interleaving two separate straight-line blocks. Confirmed clean, genuine improvement.

Also confirmed: cmd/pasture/validate_before_open_test.go and internal/config/viper_internal_test.go are now staged/tracked (git status shows them as `A`, not `??`) — the round-1 IMPORTANT finding (6cp7n) is resolved.
