## Delta hygiene check

**ValidatePhaseAdvance signature change (`error` → `(protocol.PhaseId, error)`)**: no dead/orphaned callers. Grepped all `ValidatePhaseAdvance(` call sites repo-wide (defs + tests included) — exactly 2 non-test call sites (internal/handlers/phase.go:61 inside `PhaseAdvance`, cmd/pasture/phase.go:33 inside the CLI's `validate` closure), both updated to the 2-return-value form. `go build ./...` succeeds, which would fail on any stale single-return caller — confirms no orphans compiler-side too. The CLI closure discards the returned `protocol.PhaseId` (`_, err := ...`) — this is correct, not dead-value discarding: `runWithController`'s `validate func() error` signature is niladic-return-error-only by design (established in round 1), so the CLI layer can't thread the parsed value forward anyway; the actual signal-building path inside `PhaseAdvance` uses its own `ValidatePhaseAdvance` call's returned `toPhase` value directly (no re-parse, no discarded error) — this is the fix, replacing the round-1 `toPhase, _ := protocol.ParsePhaseId(...)` re-parse-and-discard pattern.

**New controller_test.go test is a real gate, not tautological**: `TestHandler_PhaseAdvance_UnknownPhase_IsErrorNotSilentNoOp` calls `handlers.PhaseAdvance` directly (bypassing the CLI) with an unrecognised phase and asserts BOTH `err != nil` AND `code != 0`. Ran it verbose — passes, genuinely exercises the real handler (not mocked), and its rationale comment accurately describes the regression it guards (unrecognised phase parsing to zero-value PhaseId → silent no-op forwarded to the engine as "success"). Not a duplicate of the adjacent pre-existing `TestHandler_PhaseAdvance_RejectsUnknownPhase` (that one only asserts exit code == 1 specifically; the new one asserts the more general "never silently succeeds" invariant with an explicit why-comment) — deliberate defense-in-depth, not redundant test cruft.

**cmd/pasture/phase.go delta**: CLI RunE now passes a proper `func() error { _, err := handlers.ValidatePhaseAdvance(...); return err }` closure, matching the SLICE-4 pattern established for all other 8 call sites in round 1. Consistent.

**internal/config/viper.go table/loop**: two flat `bindEnvVar(...)` + `bindChangedFlag(...)` call pairs collapsed into one `for _, b := range []struct{viperKey, envVar, flagName string}{...}` loop, keeping each key's env-then-flag pair adjacent per iteration. No unused symbols — `bindEnvVar` still defined once, called once (in the loop body) instead of twice inline; `EnvAuditTrail`/`EnvAuditDBPath`/`"audit-trail"`/`"audit-db-path"` all still referenced (now as table row literals instead of call arguments) — nothing orphaned. This is a genuine elegance improvement: makes the "env before flag, per key" invariant structural (same loop iteration) rather than relying on two side-by-side sequential loops that happened to preserve ordering — reduces risk of future key-addition mistakes. Semantics unchanged (verified via full test run, see below).

VOTE: ACCEPT — 0/0/0, clean (Reviewer A / CORRECTNESS, re-review of the independent-review fix round)

This IMPORTANT was a real regression that my own earlier 0/0/0 rounds missed
(the bindEnvVar seam I approved in round 1). Verified the fix as thoroughly as I
could, including a live reproduction of the ORIGINAL bug — not just trusting the
description.

(a) Empty-env masking — CONFIRMED FIXED, and reproduced the regression live:
  - Static trace: cmd/pastured/main.go's initAuditTrail (unrelated file, not in
    this diff) has `case types.BackendMemory, "": return
    audit.NewInMemoryAuditTrail()` — an empty AuditTrail resolves to the
    non-durable in-memory backend. Pre-fix, bindEnvVar's `if val, ok :=
    lookupEnv(envVar); ok { v.Set(...) }` would call v.Set(viperKey, "") for a
    SET-BUT-EMPTY env var, landing "" in viper's override tier, which outranks
    SetDefault("sqlite") — so cfg.AuditTrail resolved to "" instead of "sqlite".
  - Ran TestResolve_EmptySetEnvIsUnset (new): passes, asserts default sqlite
    survives a set-but-empty PASTURE_AUDIT_TRAIL.
  - Went further and reproduced this live end-to-end with real binaries: built
    the FIXED pastured from the current tree and ran it with
    PASTURE_AUDIT_TRAIL="" — logs `auditTrail=sqlite` (correct). Then archived
    HEAD (f3dfa39, i.e. the state BEFORE this staged fix) into an isolated /tmp
    copy (never touched the actual reviewed worktree), built pastured from that
    unmodified pre-fix source, ran it with the same PASTURE_AUDIT_TRAIL="" — logs
    `auditTrail=""`. This directly reproduces the silent durable-to-in-memory
    flip team-lead described, and confirms the fix (`ok && val != ""`) closes it.
  - This matches viper.BindEnv's actual default (AllowEmptyEnv defaults false,
    i.e. Viper itself already treats a set-but-empty env var as unset) — so the
    fix restores parity with the pre-refactor viper.BindEnv behavior, not a new
    policy.

(b) ValidateEpochCancel now format-validates — CONFIRMED, and correctly closes a
    real gap in SLICE-4's own coverage (not scope creep): EpochStart/Terminate
    already format-validated; Cancel didn't, so a malformed
    `epoch cancel --epoch-id <bad>` would previously pass ValidateEpochCancel's
    emptiness-only check and reach OpenEpochController, creating a stray db —
    exactly the failure mode SLICE-4 exists to prevent, just missed for the
    cancel verb specifically. New fixture case epoch_cancel_malformed_id
    (want_exit 1) passes. Ran the control, TestCLI_ValidInvocation_OpensDatabase
    (uses a well-formed-but-never-started id via `epoch cancel`) — still exits 3
    and still creates the db, so the valid-format path is unaffected.

(c) config_yaml_test.go -> white-box migration — CONFIRMED preserved:
    testdata/config_loading.yaml is byte-for-byte unchanged (same 3 cases:

    test — is now an explicit dedicated case,
    TestResolvePasturedConfigFromFile_SurfacesFileError, in viper_test.go; ran
    it, passes. No dangling references to the deleted clearAllEnvVars /
    buildConfigFilePath helpers (grepped, none).

(d) 9-case fixture — CONFIRMED: epoch (start, cancel, terminate) + signal (bad
    axis, output/error conflict) + slice (bad mode, output/error conflict) +
    session (empty role) + phase (bad phase) = 9 cases, ran them all plus the
    control — all pass.

is now exactly 1:1 with the validator set: 4 new *_malformed_epoch_id rows
(signal vote, signal complete, session register, phase advance) join the 3
already covering epoch start/cancel/terminate = 7/7, all passing.

non-empty string key, with no pasture-specific schema like the epoch id's

correct but a real, live hazard this project's own fixture convention creates:
every want_*_contains/want_*_excludes field is "skip-if-empty" by design, so a

STAGED survivor, not a plain-untracked one — the comment's chosen framing fits
the rarer sub-case (git add itself failing) better than the more probable one.
Doesn't affect behavior or test outcomes, purely a doc-precision nit.

in this same diff (for the config_yaml_test.go pointer) but doesn't mention the
new KnownFields(true) strict-decode convention at all — a missed, cheap
opportunity to keep the doc complete given it was already open.

complete and consistent (7/7 epoch verbs symmetric, 2/2 slice verbs correctly
exempted, full fixture parity, race-clean, full-suite-green). Neither MINOR
blocks landing.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URD AMENDMENT 1 — normative corrections from deep Codex contract and lifecycle review

This comment augments R1–R11 and is part of the single source of truth. Where it conflicts with the original task body, this amendment governs.

R12 — Source/output roots and existing prerequisite
Adopt aura-plugins-oj7we as the GenerationRoots foundation. Canonical/verbatim inputs are always read from SourceRoot; generated artifacts are written only beneath OutputRoot. Do not duplicate this work.

R13 — Complete, context-aware runtime compiler
Use a stable SkillKey catalog and typed opaque RuntimeRef values rendered by a RuntimeDialect with RuntimeContext (harness, surface, owner skill/role, canonical source location). Compile every rendered text owner: SkillBody, ConstraintSpecs, WorkflowSpecs, ProcedureSteps, SharedFragmentSpecs, CommandSpec metadata, and RoleSpec introductions/behaviors. Plain global string replacement is forbidden. Required semantics include self-invocation elision, initial spawn versus follow-up dispatch versus notification, agent lifetime/fan-out/barrier, mode-aware user-input fallback, work tiers, instruction source, attribution, and repository capability. Claude output must remain byte-identical unless an intentional, separately reviewed semantic correction is required. OpenCode retains its accepted output initially but uses the same seam.

R14 — Honest plugin boundary and namespace
The product wording is: The Pasture plugin installs Pasture skills and provides an explicit setup workflow for native Codex agents. The plugin manifest has no invented agents component. Frontmatter skill names stay unqualified; installed invocations are namespaced as pasture:<skill>. The setup skill and swarm skill set allow_implicit_invocation=false. Swarm remains an explicitly labeled compatibility skill that launches the Claude-backed aura-swarm until a real Codex backend exists.

R15 — One canonical native-agent bundle
Store the canonical bundle inside the setup skill assets:
plugins/pasture/skills/install-codex-agents/assets/agent-bundle/manifest.json
plugins/pasture/skills/install-codex-agents/assets/agent-bundle/agents/pasture-*.toml
The manifest includes schema version, plugin/bundle semver, minimum tested Codex version, canonical role ID, public name, relative filename, SHA-256, and target policy projection. Both the companion installer and Aura Home Manager consume these exact bytes; there is no duplicate agent output tree.

Public agent names are pasture_epoch, pasture_architect, pasture_supervisor, pasture_worker, and pasture_reviewer. Never override built-in worker or explorer. Each agent stops with an actionable prerequisite error if Pasture plugin skills are unavailable. Optional model, reasoning, sandbox, MCP, and skill configuration remain omitted initially and inherit live session policy; the reviewer writes Beads state, so a blanket read-only policy would be incorrect.

R16 — Transactional Go installer lifecycle
Implement cross-platform commands in the existing Pasture CLI:
pasture codex agents plan --bundle <manifest>
pasture codex agents install --bundle <manifest>
pasture codex agents status
pasture codex agents uninstall

Target CODEX_HOME/agents (default ~/.codex/agents). Store ledger and lock under CODEX_HOME/pasture, outside the recursively scanned TOML tree. Plan makes zero writes. Install validates all inputs before mutation, locks, stages on the same filesystem, atomically replaces, and has recoverable journal/rollback behavior. An identical reinstall is a true no-op with unchanged mtimes. Refuse unowned collisions, symlink destinations, duplicate agent names found recursively, locally modified managed files, tampered bundle hashes, traversal, malformed TOML, and downgrade without explicit authorization. Uninstall removes only ledger-owned files whose current hash still matches. Modified and unowned files survive with actionable diagnostics. Agents remain independently uninstallable after plugin removal.

The setup skill checks for pasture and codex, routes to pasture:install-cli if the CLI is absent, resolves its bundle relative to itself without inspecting plugin cache internals, shows plan, obtains scoped permission, installs, and reports that a fresh thread is required.

R17 — Exclusive installation authority
Exactly one authority owns generated agents for a Codex home: companion, home-manager, or future project mode. Companion refuses Home Manager symlinks and same-name project/personal conflicts. Home Manager is opt-in, does not force existing files, and requires companion uninstall before switching. Project export remains outside MVP but conflicts are detected. Aura must not directly install plugin skill trees because that would create unnamespaced duplicate skills and break cross-skill namespaced invocations.

R18 — Distribution and version ownership
Aura owns .agents/plugins/marketplace.json as the aggregate Codex marketplace. Its Pasture git-subdir source is pinned to an immutable release tag or commit SHA, never main. Pasture owns plugins/pasture. The Codex plugin manifest and bundle manifest share the same full semver derived from the canonical release version; committed outputs contain no development cachebuster. Extend the generate-drift work already based on Pasture PR #35 so make generate covers claude-code, opencode,codex. The Aura marketplace remains versionless.

R19 — Required lifecycle and compatibility acceptance
In addition to the original BDD cases, tests must prove: exact catalog-derived inventory of 31 canonical plus one setup skill; exact metadata coverage; no double namespace; all referenced assets resolve; built-ins remain unshadowed; isolated plugin install creates skills but no native agents; five namespaced agents load only after explicit installation in a fresh thread; CODEX_HOME override leaves the default home untouched; plan writes nothing; identical install preserves mtimes; all preflight failure modes leave zero partial mutation; injected mid-install failure recovers the prior set; upgrades and downgrades enforce policy; uninstall preserves modified/unowned files; plugin removal makes remaining agents fail actionably; companion/Home Manager/project conflicts are rejected; Home Manager symlink loading and removal are demonstrated with Codex; no cache path is constructed; all version-bearing artifacts agree; unsupported manifest agent fields fail; generated Codex output has zero unapproved Claude operations; unrelated prompts cannot implicitly trigger state-changing setup; support claims cover local CLI/desktop/IDE, not ChatGPT web.

Delivery remains a two-repository change. Pasture is the source-of-truth PR (referencing issue 24) and Aura is the aggregate marketplace/Home Manager consumer. The implementation may use stacked immutable commit references while review is open, but final merge order is Pasture before Aura.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: ELEGANCE / MAINTAINABILITY / SCOPE
Round: 1
Summary: 2 BLOCKER, 6 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR. Classification is advisory inside this binary plan review; no Phase-10 severity tree was created. The safety goals are justified, but the proposal currently leaves two unfulfillable invariants and adds duplicate ownership at the compiler, catalog, installer, and slice boundaries.

BLOCKER 1 — The Codex-native compiler excludes two shipped operational skill trees.
Evidence: The proposed canonical visitor covers SkillBody, constraints, workflows, procedures, fragments, command fields, and role fields, while both protocol and install-cli remain recursive verbatim copies. Current skills/install-cli/SKILL.md identifies itself as a Claude Code skill and instructs /pasture:install-cli. The protocol skill links CLAUDE.md and PROCESS.md as operational sources; the copied trees currently contain 9 Skill( references, 7 TeamCreate references, 1 SendMessage reference, 2 AskUserQuestion references, 11 Task tool references, 107 /pasture: references, and 11 Claude Code references. The proposal nevertheless claims all 32 skills are Codex-native and that generated Codex output has zero unapproved Claude operations.
Consequence: The plugin can validate structurally while shipping two user-visible skills that reactivate Claude invocation and orchestration semantics. A lexical allowlist would hide the problem, and maintaining target-specific fixes by hand would create a second protocol source of truth.
Exact correction: Add an explicit target-aware strategy for every normative Markdown file packaged by protocol and install-cli. Generate a Codex install-cli SKILL.md with $pasture:install-cli syntax. For protocol, either compile normative PROCESS, AGENTS, CONSTRAINTS, CLAUDE-equivalent, SKILLS, and README text through the same RuntimeDialect, or package only demonstrably runtime-neutral references and omit Claude operational directives. Mark historical examples non-normative and keep them outside active instruction paths. Run the leakage guard across every packaged executable or normative Markdown asset, with named evidence-based exceptions only.

BLOCKER 2 — project cannot be an exclusive owner of a Codex home, and the CLI cannot detect the claimed conflict set.
Evidence: The owner algebra is companion | home-manager | project for a given CODEX_HOME, yet project agents live in arbitrary repository .codex/agents directories outside CODEX_HOME. There can be many projects, and plan/install accept only --bundle, so no project scope is identified. Project export is also explicitly outside MVP.
Consequence: The invariant is either cwd-dependent, silently incomplete, or requires an unbounded filesystem scan. It conflates file ownership with Codex precedence layers and bakes an out-of-scope mode into the ledger and installer API.
Exact correction: Scope exclusive authority to the five user-level files under one CODEX_HOME: companion XOR home-manager. Treat project agents as an independent Codex override layer, not as an owner of CODEX_HOME. If current-project collision checking is desired, add an explicit --project-root contract and document that it checks only that repository; otherwise warn about Codex precedence without claiming global detection. Defer project authority and ledger representation until project export is in scope.

IMPORTANT 1 — The core runtime API is only nominally typed.
Evidence: The public sketch uses RT(parts ...any) string and later reparses the resulting string in CompileRuntimeText. The any boundary accepts invalid values and discards RuntimeRef structure before dialect rendering.
Consequence: The most security-sensitive migration depends on hidden marker encoding, escaping, and runtime type switches. Refactoring and audit become harder, and arbitrary prose can collide with compiler tokens.
Exact correction: Remove ...any. Prefer a RuntimeText value made from explicit Literal and Ref parts and render it without reparsing; if preserving string fields is essential for migration scope, restrict insertion to RT(ref RuntimeRef) string, define one reserved collision-proof encoding and escaping contract, and prove round-trip and rejection behavior. Keep literal concatenation outside the token constructor.

IMPORTANT 2 — The new SkillKey registry risks becoming a fifth inventory source rather than replacing existing ones.
Evidence: The current generator already has roleSkillDirs, commandSkillDirs, TargetHarness.Verbatim, CommandSpecs Name/File, and tests that manually mirror inventories. The proposal adds a 31-entry SkillKey registry plus a separate Codex UI registry and relies on bijection tests, but does not say which existing maps are removed or derived.
Consequence: Adding or renaming one skill requires synchronized edits in several registries. Tests detect drift after the fact but do not establish one artifact owner.
Exact correction: Define one canonical SkillDescriptor catalog containing SkillKey, directory, source kind, and role or command ID. Replace roleSkillDirs, commandSkillDirs, and verbatim inventory iteration with projections from that catalog. Keep only genuinely target-local UI text as a keyed overlay and require exhaustive coverage. Derive all-target inventory, invocation addresses, and output paths from the descriptor catalog.

IMPORTANT 3 — whole-set atomic replacement is not a defined achievable filesystem guarantee.
Evidence: The five managed TOMLs share CODEX_HOME/agents with unmanaged files. A directory swap would replace user content, while five per-file renames are not loader-atomic because Codex does not honor the Pasture lock or ledger. The proposal simultaneously promises atomically replacing the whole managed set and a recoverable journal.
Consequence: Implementors can satisfy command rollback tests while a concurrently starting Codex process observes a mixed old/new set, or they can overcomplicate the design chasing an impossible cross-file atomic primitive.
Exact correction: State the exact supported invariant. Either prove a current-Codex-compatible single atomic indirection that preserves unmanaged agents, or define a recoverable transaction: stage outside agents, journal old hashes/backups, replace files individually, commit ledger last, recover before every command, never report success for a partial generation, and tell users not to start a new thread until status is healthy. Rename tests and product language from loader-atomic to recoverable all-or-error unless true loader atomicity is demonstrated.

IMPORTANT 4 — status cannot report desired bundle or plugin drift with its declared inputs.
Evidence: plan and install accept --bundle, but status accepts none while promising stale and plugin/agent version drift. Cache paths are correctly forbidden, and status must still work after plugin removal.
Consequence: The implementation must secretly inspect cwd/cache/plugin CLI state, or return claims it cannot substantiate.
Exact correction: Define status with two modes: pasture codex agents status reports ledger-versus-disk health and interrupted transaction state; pasture codex agents status --bundle manifest additionally verifies desired bundle/version/hash drift. The setup skill must pass its own manifest. If Codex plugin-list integration is retained, specify it as an optional separately labeled observation rather than the source of installed-agent truth. Name the explicit downgrade flag in the command contract as well.

IMPORTANT 5 — The slices contradict their own exclusive file ownership rule.
Evidence: Foundation owns internal/codegen/harness.go while Slice 1 adds the Codex TargetHarness there; Slice 1 owns the UI registry while Slice 2 explicitly extends it; Slice 3 owns version projection after plugin and bundle emitters settle, which requires those emitters to consume the version contract. The proposal then forbids workers from editing another slice files without reassignment.
Consequence: Buildable intermediate slices and merge ownership are unclear, integration changes become surprise cross-slice edits, and review scope cannot be attributed cleanly.
Exact correction: Add one supervisor-owned integration leaf for shared target wiring, or revise ownership so Foundation owns all neutral interfaces/catalog and one named file owner owns each shared Codex target/registry file through final integration. Put the complete 32-entry UI registry, including setup metadata, in its owning slice from the start. Specify how bundle and version providers plug in without later editing another slice files. If that cannot be made clean, collapse Slices 1–3 into one sequential Pasture distribution slice rather than claiming false parallelism.

IMPORTANT 6 — The Home Manager surface and manifest consumption remain underspecified, inviting another role list.
Evidence: The existing nix/hm-module.nix hardcodes roleNames. The proposal says Home Manager consumes exact bundle bytes but does not define the public option name/default or require filenames and public names to be derived from manifest.json.
Consequence: Aura can install the right bytes while maintaining a second five-role filename inventory that drifts from bundle membership; users also cannot assess the promised opt-in behavior from the proposal.
Exact correction: Specify CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.codex.agents.enable with default false, and derive Home Manager file mappings from the parsed canonical bundle manifest after validating safe relative paths, unique public names, expected authority, and hashes. Do not add a second Codex role/filename list. Put companion-ledger conflict checking in a named activation step because Nix evaluation cannot inspect mutable home state reliably.

Required revision exit: update the proposal and URD amendment where necessary, then run a fresh three-axis round. ACCEPT requires a fix-free round with none of the above findings outstanding.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: TEST-QUALITY / FAILURE-MODEL, round 1

Result: 3 BLOCKER, 6 IMPORTANT, 1 MINOR. This is not a fix-free round.

BLOCKER B1 — Active verbatim assets bypass the runtime compiler.
Evidence: Architecture B limits the canonical visitor to Go-owned SkillBody, constraint/workflow/procedure/fragment/command/role fields, while Architecture C says protocol/install-cli assets are recursively packaged. The actual active files are not runtime-neutral: skills/protocol/PROCESS.md:206 prescribes the Task tool and Skill invocation, lines 409-415 prescribe TeamCreate, Opus, Task, and Skill, skills/install-cli/SKILL.md:6-15 calls itself a Claude Code skill with slash invocation, and schema.xml contains Skill(...), Task, SendMessage, AskUserQuestion, and Claude model names. These are instructions reached from the protocol skill, not harmless historical fixtures. The proposed hotspot goldens and canonical lexical guard can therefore pass while the installed Codex plugin still teaches Claude-only operations.
Consequence: R2, R10, BDD 1, and the claim that all 32 skills are operationally native are unproven and currently false for two catalog skills plus their linked schema/reference files.
Exact correction: Make every shipped executable/reference text a target-owned input. Generate or dialect-compile protocol, install-cli, and the plugin-local schema; exclude or conspicuously isolate Claude-only documents from the Codex package. Extend the visitor/asset emitter and lexical guard over every Markdown, XML, YAML, JSON, and TOML file reachable in plugins/pasture, with a reviewed per-file/per-line allowlist only for explicitly comparative examples. Add assertions for the known PROCESS.md, install-cli, and schema.xml hotspots and link-walk the installed cached plugin, not just the source tree.

BLOCKER B2 — The promised multi-file transaction is not defined or tested at the durability boundary.
Evidence: Architecture E runs common preflight before taking the install lock, claims atomic replacement of five independently discovered TOMLs with the ledger written last, and promises recovery at every injected failure point. The test list covers returned-error injection but not process death, concurrent processes, fsync ordering, stale locks, or a path/symlink swap between preflight and rename. A filesystem cannot atomically replace an arbitrary set of flat files plus a ledger as one operation without an explicit generation/commit-marker protocol. This repository already demonstrates the required distinction in cmd/pasture-migrate-crash and internal/engine/recovery_test.go: in-process errors are not a substitute for SIGKILL recovery.
Consequence: A crash can leave new files with no ledger, a mixed old/new set, or an interrupted uninstall that the next run misclassifies as unowned; concurrent install/uninstall can invalidate the no-overwrite and exactly-one-owner guarantees.
Exact correction: Specify the transaction state machine, authoritative commit point, journal schema, fsync and directory-fsync order, and the honest guarantee (old complete generation or new complete generation, or a clearly weaker recoverable guarantee). All mutating commands must acquire the same cross-process lock before authoritative preflight and revalidate at each mutation; status must take a coherent snapshot. Add a build-tagged subprocess probe that is killed after every durable boundary and then exercises status/recovery/install/uninstall. Add two-process contention, stale-lock, concurrent upgrade/uninstall, symlink/path-swap, permission, ENOSPC/short-write, and cleanup-failure cases on every supported OS. Do not claim set-level atomicity until those observable tests pass.

BLOCKER B3 — Home Manager ownership enforcement is placed at an impossible layer and has no executable test harness.
Evidence: Architecture F says Home Manager asserts the companion ledger/files are absent, and BDD 7 says evaluation fails on companion ownership. Nix evaluation cannot inspect the future runtime home safely. The current Aura flake has no Home Manager input/check fixture, and nix/hm-module.nix only builds home.file mappings; nix flake check --no-build does not instantiate or activate this module. A plain home.file collision also does not validate the companion ledger or prove no partial switch.
Consequence: The declarative path can silently violate the exclusive-owner contract or fail only mid-activation, and the enable/disable/removal claim is not covered by any real production path.
Exact correction: Split pure evaluation invariants from runtime ownership checks. Add a pinned Home Manager test input and a real module fixture/check for option defaults, exact five manifest-derived sources, no Codex skills, and missing/hash-mismatched bundle failures. Add a pre-link home.activation guard that checks ledger and managed regular files before link generation. Execute enable, repeat-enable, conflict, upgrade, disable, and modified/unowned preservation scenarios against a temporary HOME; assert a conflict performs no managed mutation. Then run the pinned Codex loader against the produced symlink generation and after removal. State clearly which of evaluation versus activation owns each failure.

IMPORTANT I1 — Current-Codex smoke is not bound to a deterministic observable.
Evidence: The proposal repeatedly requires skill discovery, agent selection, invocation, and missing-plugin behavioral stops, but names only plugin add/list/remove. codex plugin list exposes plugins, not the loaded skill and custom-agent catalogs; model-driven invocation is networked and nondeterministic. The gate also says current Codex while the manifest says minimum tested Codex, without a pinned CI version, acquisition method, offline/network split, or skip/fail policy.
Consequence: A green smoke may prove only that files were cached, while a CI failure can depend on ambient Codex upgrades, authentication, network, or model behavior.
Exact correction: Define three layers: hermetic repo contract tests; a pinned CLI loader test in a temporary CODEX_HOME using a deterministic debug/app-server/config observable for exact skill and agent catalogs; and separately labeled network/model UAT. Record exact CLI version and command/output schema, prove default HOME is untouched, start a fresh process for catalog refresh, and make CI policy explicit. Treat agent prerequisite/model compliance as structural plus manual UAT unless a deterministic runtime observable exists.

IMPORTANT I2 — Status and version-drift claims have no source of truth.
Evidence: status has no bundle argument yet promises plugin/agent version drift, while the design forbids cache-path inspection and must still work after plugin removal. The proposal also says codegen derives plugin and bundle versions from canonical release metadata while pasture-release discovers/synchronizes both, leaving two possible writers. Current release discovery is ordered and centered on .claude-plugin/plugin.json; partial sibling writes are possible if a second writer is added naively.
Consequence: status cannot distinguish installed integrity from available-bundle or installed-plugin drift, and release operations can create the very version mismatch the gate is meant to prevent.
Exact correction: Separate status dimensions. Ledger-only status reports managed integrity; status --bundle compares an explicitly verified bundle; optional plugin status uses a documented injected codex plugin list JSON inspector and reports unknown when unavailable. Choose one version writer: update the canonical release version, then deterministically generate both Codex manifests; pasture-release should validate or invoke that path, not independently rewrite generated siblings. Test missing plugin/CLI/bundle, malformed versions, prerelease/build metadata policy, partial generation failure, dry run, idempotence, and all three version-bearing outputs.

IMPORTANT I3 — Regression and drift tests do not prove full artifact determinism.
Evidence: Architecture says OpenCode preserves accepted output, but BDD 1 only says it remains accepted and the Foundation exit requires byte stability only for Claude. Existing full-file emission writes known outputs but does not inherently remove stale generated files. Targeted Codex hotspot goldens plus a registry count can miss an obsolete skill directory, asset, metadata file, or manifest entry left from a previous catalog.
Consequence: The all-target drift job can be clean while carrying stale/duplicate artifacts, or OpenCode can change unintentionally during the runtime migration.
Exact correction: Require byte-for-byte baselines and exact recursive inventories for both existing Claude and OpenCode trees. Generate all targets into an empty temp output, compare paths and bytes against tracked committed artifacts, then regenerate in place and assert git diff plus untracked output is empty. Seed a stale file/directory and require codegen to delete it through an owned-output manifest or fail actionably. Make any OpenCode baseline change an explicit separately reviewed exception.

IMPORTANT I4 — Creator validation is not reproducible from the repositories.
Evidence: The research records that plugin-creator and skill-creator validators live in the user Codex installation, have PyYAML/environment requirements, and differ from the runtime. The proposal says they run in a declared environment but assigns no immutable validator source, revision/hash, provisioning command, or CI owner.
Consequence: A required landing gate can be unavailable to CI and other contributors, or silently change underneath the branch.
Exact correction: Pin and provision the exact validator artifacts in a declared Nix/CI environment with provenance and hash, or make repo-owned Go schema/shape tests the mandatory gate and record creator validation as a versioned compatibility job. Test the known validator/runtime disagreement cases and print the validator and Codex versions in evidence.

IMPORTANT I5 — The production CLI surface lacks black-box acceptance contracts.
Evidence: Slice 2 names pasture codex agents commands but the validation matrix does not require Cobra registration/help, stdout versus stderr, exit codes, JSON schema, flag parsing, or the built binary. The setup skill needs a stable plan/status surface. This repository already has the correct production seam in cmd/pasture/main_test.go, which builds and runs the actual binary.
Consequence: Core filesystem tests could pass while the shipped command is unwired, emits unstable model-parsed text, touches the task DB, or returns success on conflict.
Exact correction: Add subprocess tests through the compiled pasture binary for every command and flag, including --help, --format=json stable plan/status schemas, text output, exit categories, absent HOME/CODEX_HOME, bundle resolution, permission failures, unchanged stdout/stderr on no-op, and proof the task database/default home are untouched. The setup skill smoke must consume this public command rather than an internal package function.

IMPORTANT I6 — Project-layer conflict discovery is unspecified.
Evidence: Preflight promises to recursively detect same-name project/personal agents even though project export is out of scope, but no project-root discovery rule or flag is defined. Invocation from a nested directory, Git worktree, multiple ancestor .codex directories, or outside Git can produce different visible agent layers.
Consequence: Exactly-one-owner can pass in tests that scan one fixture and fail in a real repository where Codex resolves another project layer.
Exact correction: Define the Codex-equivalent project root and precedence algorithm, expose an explicit --project-root or --no-project-check policy when discovery is ambiguous, and report every scanned root. Test nested paths, worktrees, non-Git directories, multiple layers, alternate filenames with duplicate names, symlinked directories, unreadable/malformed unrelated TOMLs, and case-folding behavior on supported filesystems.

MINOR M1 — Visitor exhaustiveness needs a field-owner sentinel test and diagnostic contract.
Evidence: The matrix covers ref kinds, dialects, and surfaces but does not prove that every current and future string-bearing spec field is visited; a newly added field can bypass compilation until a lexical pattern happens to catch it. Error checks mention actionable location only for unknown/uncompiled refs, not every installer/manifest failure class.
Consequence: Future canonical fields can regress silently, and actionable-error quality can degrade while tests only assert non-nil error.
Exact correction: Populate every renderable owner field with unique sentinel RuntimeRefs and assert all are compiled for each surface/dialect; make adding a new owner fail compile or reflection-based coverage. Use a shared error assertion for what, why, where, when/operation, caller impact, and repair across representative failure classes.

Verified strengths: the proposal correctly separates plugin skills from native agent TOMLs, namespaces native agents, disables implicit setup/swarm invocation, derives expected skill inventory from a registry, keeps one canonical bundle, preserves unmanaged files, and requires a clean three-axis review round. Those strengths do not close the executable gaps above.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: adversarial correctness, security, and distribution.
Standard applied: fix-free means zero BLOCKER, IMPORTANT, and MINOR findings. This round is not clean.

BLOCKER B1 — The proposed delegation topology cannot run under the Codex default depth limit.
Evidence: FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-1 emits native epoch, architect, supervisor, worker, and reviewer agents while retaining nested delegation: an epoch agent spawns architect/supervisor, and those agents spawn reviewers/workers. The proposal omits all agent depth policy and capability setup. Current official Codex subagent documentation states agents.max_depth defaults to 1, so a root can spawn a direct child but that child cannot spawn descendants: https://developers.openai.com/codex/subagents. A spawned pasture_epoch at depth 1 cannot launch its architect; even invoking the epoch skill in the root leaves architect/supervisor children unable to launch depth-2 reviewers/workers.
Consequence: the advertised 12-phase workflow and mandatory three-reviewer gates dead-end in normal default Codex configuration. Agent TOMLs can validate and load while the product is operationally unusable.
Exact correction: add a tested orchestration-depth contract. Compute and document the depth required by each entry path, including the full epoch when epoch itself is a custom child; either flatten spawning through the root or require an explicit supported agents.max_depth value. Do not assume an agent-local setting wins over live parent overrides. The setup/status flow must detect or actionably report insufficient effective capability, show the exact user-approved config change, and require a fresh thread. Add end-to-end cases proving default configuration either completes through a supported fallback or stops before mutation with exact remediation, and proving a configured full epoch reaches architect review and supervisor worker/reviewer descendants.

BLOCKER B2 — Fresh-user setup has no versioned bootstrap contract for the Pasture CLI.
Evidence: the bundle manifest records plugin and Codex versions but no Pasture CLI/API compatibility. The setup skill only checks whether pasture exists and otherwise routes to $pasture:install-cli. The current checked-in skills/install-cli/SKILL.md fetches the latest GitHub release or installs @latest; it cannot select the immutable plugin revision. A feature plugin can therefore be fetched from a pinned commit while latest pasture lacks the codex agents command or supports a different bundle schema. The proposal also does not require a Pasture release-version bump and published binary before the Aura entry becomes available.
Consequence: the primary new-user path can install all plugin skills yet be unable to install any native agent, or can run an incompatible mutator against the bundle. A passing locally built smoke would not prove the distributed path.
Exact correction: version the installer protocol in manifest.json with the minimum/exact compatible Pasture CLI semver and source revision. Give the CLI a machine-readable capability/version command and have setup verify it, not mere executable presence. Make install-cli accept and verify an exact release tag or immutable revision plus published checksums rather than latest. Add the release bump and release-artifact publication to Slice 3, and gate Aura marketplace availability on that release. The durable Aura source must be a release tag or post-merge reachable SHA; a feature-branch SHA may be used only for stacked review and must be refreshed before Aura merge. Test fresh install using the actual released/downloaded binary, old/new CLI rejection, and schema compatibility.

BLOCKER B3 — The whole-set atomicity and no-partial-authority promise has no feasible commit mechanism or race model.
Evidence: Codex recursively discovers every TOML below the agents directory. The proposal writes five independent files into that shared loader-visible tree and writes a ledger last, while claiming it atomically replaces the whole managed set and that no partial set becomes authoritative. Per-file atomic rename plus a Pasture-only lock cannot make five files atomically visible to a concurrent or newly starting Codex loader, which does not honor that lock. The plan-display to permission to install sequence can also become stale, and the text does not require authoritative preflight to run again under the lock. Symlink-parent checks performed before mutation remain susceptible to parent replacement.
Consequence: interruption or concurrent startup can observe mixed agent generations, duplicate or missing roles, or ledger/files from different generations; a path race can redirect writes. This violates R16, R19, and BDD cases 3 and 4.
Exact correction: specify a concrete, implementable transaction state machine and threat model before slicing. Acquire the lock before the authoritative state read, recompute and redisplay or bind consent to a plan digest, revalidate bundle, ledger, destination identities, ownership, modes, and no-follow path components under lock, define fsync and journal ordering, commit point, rollback, and startup recovery. Either prove a single loader-visible atomic indirection against current Codex on Linux and macOS, or narrow the requirement from atomic whole-set visibility to crash-recoverable quiescent installation and amend the URD/BDD truthfully. Add concurrent-installer, concurrent-reader, stale-plan, symlink-swap, process-kill-at-each-boundary, directory-mode, and recovery tests.

IMPORTANT I1 — The runtime compiler does not cover the complete production render graph, especially the verbatim install path.
Evidence: the visitor list names SkillBody, constraints, workflows, procedure steps, fragments, CommandSpec, and parts of RoleSpec, but generated templates also render transitions, coordination commands, checklists, review axes, figures, nested example and recipe fields, ownership narrative, and external/verbatim trees. Current skills/install-cli/SKILL.md explicitly says Claude Code, teaches /pasture:install-cli, fetches latest, and writes downloaded executables directly. It is copied verbatim today. Protocol assets intentionally contain comparative/historical Claude syntax.
Consequence: the Codex plugin can pass generated-spec guards while shipping a broken Codex fallback and accidental Claude operations, contradicting R2, R13, and R19.
Exact correction: enumerate every string-bearing node reachable from each Codex template and compile it recursively. Add a target-neutral or explicit Codex renderer for install-cli rather than copying its Claude body. Treat protocol documentation as a separately classified reference asset with precise allowlists, not a blanket generated-output exemption. Scan the final plugin archive, including copied files and figures, and require each allowed Claude token to carry an explicit reason/location golden.

IMPORTANT I2 — Agent delivery availability and context inheritance are missing from the dispatch contract.
Evidence: plugin installation intentionally creates zero custom agents, but CodexDialect does not state whether AgentPurpose renders a namespaced pasture_* custom type, a built-in type plus $pasture:* activation, or a runtime fallback. RuntimeContext has no installed-agent capability. The proposed spawn mapping also omits Codex fork/context inheritance even though canonical TeamCreate assignments assume zero prior context and the current spawn surface defaults to inherited context unless fork behavior is explicit.
Consequence: plugin-only workflows may reference unavailable agent types; installed-agent workflows may never use the generated types; or subagents may receive conversation context the protocol says they do not have, increasing prompt leakage and changing behavior.
Exact correction: add typed AgentDelivery and ContextInheritance/ForkPolicy semantics. Define and test both supported modes: plugin-only uses a proven generic/built-in child with an explicit namespaced role-skill prompt, while installed mode may use pasture_* and elides self-activation. Render fork policy explicitly, normally none for self-contained Beads handoffs, and test prompt contents, no double role loading, unavailable-agent fallback, and no accidental context inheritance.

IMPORTANT I3 — The exclusive-owner invariant is overbroad and cannot be enforced for project layers; Home Manager enforcement is placed at the wrong abstraction level.
Evidence: project agents live in arbitrary repository .codex/agents trees, not in a Codex home. Current Codex loads config layers and lets a higher layer merge/override the same agent name; a personal installer cannot discover every present or future project repository. The proposal nevertheless promises companion, Home Manager, or project as exactly one owner and rejection of project/personal conflicts. Separately, pure Nix evaluation cannot reliably assert mutable files or a companion ledger in the users live home; this requires activation-time checking.
Consequence: status can claim exclusivity that becomes false on the next cwd, while a Home Manager switch can still collide at activation or rely on an impure evaluation check.
Exact correction: scope exclusive ownership to the five personal paths under one CODEX_HOME, between companion and Home Manager only. Treat project definitions as a higher-precedence Codex layer: detect and warn/refuse only for the active resolved project when relevant, and do not claim global discovery. Implement a Home Manager activation DAG guard before link creation that checks the companion ledger plus every destination using lstat semantics and fails with uninstall instructions; do not use evaluation-time home inspection. Test both direction switches, active-project overrides, stale ledger, disabled cleanup, and non-default CODEX_HOME policy.

IMPORTANT I4 — The advertised CLI surface cannot implement two of its promised behaviors.
Evidence: status has no --bundle or other current-plugin input, yet it promises plugin/agent version drift; after plugin removal it can know only ledger/local integrity. Install promises explicitly authorized downgrade, but the command synopsis defines no --allow-downgrade or equivalent. No stable machine-readable output is specified for the setup skill or Home Manager diagnostics.
Consequence: implementation must either inspect unsupported plugin cache internals, silently omit promised state, or invent incompatible flags during a slice.
Exact correction: define status [--bundle <manifest>] with clear bundle-less semantics, plus a stable --format=json schema; have the setup skill pass its own bundle. Add install --allow-downgrade with an exact confirmation/audit rule. Define exit codes for healthy, drift, conflict, interrupted transaction, and unsupported schema, and cover them at the real Cobra entry point.

IMPORTANT I5 — Required non-plugin runtime dependencies are absent from the distribution contract.
Evidence: generated production instructions contain extensive bd operations and mandatory git agent-commit usage; swarm additionally requires aura-swarm. The companion setup checks only pasture and codex, and install-cli installs only Pasture binaries. agents/openai.yaml can declare only supported MCP dependencies, so these executable prerequisites will not be installed by plugin metadata.
Consequence: a user can complete plugin and agent installation, then fail immediately at Phase 1 or landing with command-not-found. The plugin prerequisite embedded in agents is insufficient and the product claim is not operationally complete.
Exact correction: add a generated prerequisite matrix and user-facing plugin/setup documentation for bd, git agent-commit, pasture, codex, and the explicitly optional Claude-backed aura-swarm. Setup/status must probe required executable capabilities and stop actionably before a workflow that needs them. Either distribute a supported git agent-commit implementation or define a safe, ratified fallback for Codex environments. Add clean-machine smoke cases that prove both failure diagnostics and the fully provisioned path.

IMPORTANT I6 — Protocol command identity and actual Codex invocation identity remain conflated at rendered user surfaces.
Evidence: the proposal correctly says CommandSpec.Name is human/protocol metadata and cannot be transliterated, but current templates render that field under Command and in subskill headers. Several protocol names such as pasture:architect:propose-plan do not equal the effective plugin invocation $pasture:architect-propose-plan.
Consequence: generated Codex docs can be internally type-safe yet instruct users or children to invoke a non-existent name.
Exact correction: add distinct typed ProtocolCommandName and SkillInvocation projections to template contexts. Label protocol-only tables explicitly and render the exact registry-derived effective $pasture:<directory> address everywhere an invocation is actionable. Add a whole-archive test that resolves every actionable invocation to exactly one generated skill.

MINOR M1 — The proposed typed token API still exposes an untyped escape hatch.
Evidence: func RT(parts ...any) string accepts arbitrary values and collapses semantic references back into an opaque string, weakening the private RuntimeRef and exhaustiveness claims.
Consequence: malformed or accidentally stringified values can enter privileged generated instructions and errors move from compile time to lexical cleanup.
Exact correction: return a RuntimeText value built from a closed RuntimePart interface or typed constructors, keep raw text and refs structurally separate until rendering, and make plain-string conversion available only after successful dialect compilation.

MINOR M2 — Marketplace behavior is not concrete enough to be reviewable.
Evidence: the proposal requires policy and category but does not select installation, authentication, product gating, ordering, or the exact sha versus ref representation. Those values affect availability in the desktop marketplace and stacked-PR safety.
Consequence: Slice 4 must make user-facing policy decisions that were supposed to be ratified in the plan.
Exact correction: specify the exact Aura entry now: ordering rule, category, AVAILABLE versus INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT, authentication timing for a plugin with no authentication, omitted products unless intentionally gated, and sha/ref rules for stacked review versus merge-ready release.

Round summary: 3 BLOCKER, 6 IMPORTANT, 2 MINOR. VOTE: REVISE. A new proposal must address every item and receive a new independent correctness review; this review record itself may now close.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URD AMENDMENT 2 — normative resolution of Proposal 1 adversarial review

This amendment supersedes conflicting portions of Amendment 1, especially its claims of a global companion|home-manager|project owner algebra, five-file whole-set atomic visibility, recursive verbatim Codex skills, and nested default Codex delegation.

R20 — Default-depth Codex orchestration
The supported Codex entry path is the root thread invoking pasture:epoch or another Pasture role skill. Codex rendering keeps all spawned agents as depth-1 leaves because current Codex defaults agents.max_depth to 1 and recommends that default. The root thread owns phase transitions, reviewer fan-out, worker dispatch, waits, follow-up_task, and consolidation. Architect and supervisor role skills execute in the root when they must coordinate; their native agent projections may produce bounded artifacts but must not recursively spawn. A spawned pasture_epoch is not advertised as a full root orchestrator and must direct the caller to invoke the epoch skill in the root. max_threads shortfall is handled by bounded/serial fan-out. Tests prove the default-depth path reaches plan review, worker execution, and code review without increasing max_depth.

R21 — Structural runtime text and one skill catalog
Replace all existing roleSkillDirs, commandSkillDirs, verbatim inventory iteration, and new skill-key maps with one SkillDescriptor catalog containing key, directory, source kind, and role/command/support identity. Target UI text remains an exhaustive keyed overlay. Runtime-sensitive content uses closed RuntimeText parts (Literal and RuntimeRef), never parts ...any or an opaque string round trip. ProtocolCommandName and effective SkillInvocation are distinct typed projections. Every actionable invocation in the final archive must resolve to exactly one generated skill.

R22 — Complete production render graph and target-owned support assets
Every normative/executable file shipped in plugins/pasture is target-owned and checked. protocol and install-cli are not recursively copied into Codex. Move normative protocol asset sources behind the runtime compiler or generate a smaller native reference set from canonical specs; generate the plugin-local schema with CodexDialect. Codex install-cli is generated from typed install semantics and uses exact version/revision inputs. Exclude Claude-only historical documents from active Codex instruction paths; any comparative fixture is non-normative and requires a file/line/reason golden. Scan the complete final archive across Markdown, XML, YAML, JSON, and TOML and link-walk the installed cache. Claude and OpenCode path-and-byte baselines remain exact unless an explicit reviewed exception is recorded.

R23 — Agent delivery and context policy
CodexDialect models AgentDelivery and ContextInheritance explicitly. Plugin-only mode always works using a current built-in/default leaf plus a prompt whose first directive activates the exact namespaced Pasture role skill. Healthy installed mode may select pasture_* leaf agents and elides duplicate self-activation. Self-contained Beads handoffs use no conversation fork/context; follow-up work targets the existing persistent leaf. If the runtime cannot expose a requested custom type, fall back to the plugin-only leaf path instead of failing. Native agents remain optional enhancement; plugin skill workflows are complete without them.

R24 — Versioned CLI bootstrap and prerequisites
The bundle manifest includes installer protocol/schema version, exact compatible Pasture CLI semver constraint, source revision, tested/minimum Codex version, and published checksum metadata. The CLI exposes machine-readable capabilities. Setup verifies capability/schema compatibility, not executable presence. The Codex install-cli accepts an exact release tag or immutable revision, verifies published checksums for release binaries, and never substitutes latest. A local/source-revision path is explicitly development-only. Release artifacts and checksums must exist before the Aura marketplace entry becomes AVAILABLE.

Generate a prerequisite matrix for codex, pasture, bd, Git, conditional repository commit policy, and the optional Claude-backed aura-swarm. Setup/status diagnose absent required capabilities. Landing obeys repository instructions: use git agent-commit when required and available; if it is required but absent, stop actionably; use ordinary commit only where repository policy permits it. Do not silently configure Git or install hooks.

R25 — Recoverable managed-generation transaction
Scope companion files to a dedicated regular directory beneath CODEX_HOME/agents, with control state outside the recursively scanned TOML tree. Mutating commands take one cross-process lock before authoritative preflight. Plan is a non-authoritative zero-write snapshot; install binds approval to a digest and recomputes under lock. Stage a complete generation on the same filesystem, fsync files/directories, journal durable states, move the prior managed directory to a control-area backup, activate the complete new directory by rename, atomically write/fsync the ledger as commit metadata, and clean up. Uninstall uses the same journal. The honest guarantee is crash-recoverable quiescent installation: Codex can observe a brief complete-set absence during a swap but never a mixed Pasture generation; users start a fresh thread only after healthy status. If current Codex or a supported OS disproves directory indirection/recursive loading, narrow further rather than claiming loader atomicity.

Every command recovers an interrupted journal first. Tests use actual subprocess SIGKILL at each durable boundary, two-process contention, stale lock handling, stale plan digest, concurrent upgrade/uninstall/read, symlink/path swaps, permissions, short write/ENOSPC where injectable, cleanup failure, and Linux/macOS directory semantics. In-process error injection alone is insufficient.

R26 — Exact CLI surface and status truth
Commands are:
pasture codex agents capabilities --format=json
pasture codex agents plan --bundle <manifest> [--project-root <path>|--no-project-check] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents install --bundle <manifest> --plan-digest <digest> [--allow-downgrade] [project-check flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents status [--bundle <manifest>] [project-check flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents uninstall --format=text|json

Bundle-less status reports ledger-versus-disk integrity and interruption only. --bundle adds desired-version/hash comparison. Optional codex plugin-list observation is separately labeled and may be unknown; cache paths are never inspected. Define stable JSON schemas and exit categories. Black-box compiled-binary tests cover Cobra registration/help, flags, stdout/stderr, HOME/CODEX_HOME isolation, and proof that no task DB is touched.

R27 — Ownership scope and Home Manager reality
Exclusive authority applies only to the personal Pasture managed directory under one CODEX_HOME: companion XOR Home Manager. Arbitrary project .codex/agents are a higher-precedence Codex layer outside this ownership model. A caller may name one active --project-root to detect/warn/refuse same-name overrides there; no global discovery is claimed.

Aura exposes CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.codex.agents.enable, default false, and installs no Codex skills. Nix evaluation parses and validates the canonical bundle manifest, derives exact mappings without a second role list, and verifies safe relative paths, unique names, and hashes. Mutable companion conflicts are checked by a Home Manager activation DAG guard before link creation, not at evaluation. Tests use a pinned Home Manager input and real module/activation fixture for defaults, enable, repeat enable, conflicts with zero mutation, upgrade, disable, stale ledger, modified/unowned preservation, non-default CODEX_HOME policy, and current Codex loader behavior on symlinked agents.

R28 — Deterministic validation and artifact ownership
Validation has three layers:
1. mandatory hermetic Go/Nix contract tests;
2. a pinned Codex CLI loader test using deterministic app-server skills/list, plugin/list/read, config/debug prompt observables and fresh processes in isolated CODEX_HOME;
3. separately labeled network/model UAT.

Repo-owned Go validation is the mandatory plugin/skill schema gate. Creator-script compatibility is recorded with exact validator hashes/versions when available but is not an ambient-home CI dependency. Full empty-root generation compares exact recursive path/byte inventories for Claude, OpenCode, and Codex. In-place generation tracks owned outputs and removes or fails on stale paths actionably. Seeded stale output must be detected. Every actionable error test asserts what, why, where, operation/when, impact, and repair.

R29 — Single version writer and release readiness
The canonical Pasture release version remains the sole writer. Codegen reads it and deterministically emits the Codex plugin and bundle versions. pasture-release updates the canonical version then invokes/validates generation; it must not independently rewrite generated sibling manifests. status without a bundle cannot claim desired or plugin drift.

R30 — Exact Aura marketplace policy
Append Pasture after existing entries. Use name pasture, source type git-subdir, HTTPS Pasture repository URL, path plugins/pasture, and an immutable 40-hex revision for stacked review. Category is Productivity. policy.authentication is ON_INSTALL per the current marketplace schema; no credential is actually required. Omit policy.products. policy.installation is NOT_AVAILABLE while the compatible Pasture release/checksums do not exist and becomes AVAILABLE only after the release is reachable and the entry is repinned to its immutable release commit. Never use INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT or a mutable main ref.

R31 — Slice ownership and integration
Implementation planning must give each shared file one owner. Foundation owns GenerationRoots, SkillDescriptor, RuntimeText/compiler/dialects, canonical projection, and TargetHarness integration. One Codex codegen slice owns the complete 32-entry UI overlay and all codex_*/template/plugin/bundle emitters. One CLI slice owns internal/codexagents and cmd/pasture wiring while consuming a frozen shared bundle contract. Release integration consumes emitters without editing them. Aura consumes only the frozen manifest/bundle. If a shared edit is discovered, supervisor reassigns it explicitly before the edit; no false parallelism is claimed.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: TEST-QUALITY / FAILURE-MODEL, round 2

Result: 0 BLOCKER, 4 IMPORTANT, 1 MINOR. Round 2 resolves the Round 1 architecture blockers, but it is not yet a fix-free round.

IMPORTANT I1 — Read-only observation and journal recovery remain normatively contradictory.
Evidence: Proposal 2 section 6 defines plan as a zero-write snapshot and bundle-less status as a report of ledger/disk/interruption health. Section 7 correctly says every mutation locks and recovers. However normative URD Amendment 2 R25 still says every command recovers an interrupted journal first. Recovery changes the journal, backup, active generation, or ledger; plan cannot both recover and remain zero-write, and status cannot both report an interrupted state and erase it as a side effect. The proposal also lists concurrent read testing without defining how plan/status obtain a coherent observation while install/uninstall rename the directory and ledger.
Consequence: Implementors and black-box tests have two incompatible success criteria. A supposedly diagnostic command can mutate user state without consent, or an unlocked reader can synthesize a ledger/generation combination that never existed.
Exact correction: Amend R25 and the proposal contract so only install and uninstall recover under the exclusive mutation lock. Define capabilities, plan, and status as observational; on an interrupted journal they report recovery-required and identify the mutating command that will recover. Plan must remain byte/tree zero-write in both healthy and interrupted fixtures. Give plan/status a coherent-read algorithm that does not create the lock file, such as a retrying before/after generation snapshot, with the install digest as the final stale-consent guard. Add tree-hash before/after tests for capabilities/plan/status, interrupted-state tests, and a concurrent reader/writer test that permits only a coherent old, interrupted, or new state.

IMPORTANT I2 — The claimed deterministic custom-agent catalog observable does not exist in the pinned CLI surface as named.
Evidence: The installed Codex 0.144.1 app-server schema does expose skills/list and plugin/list/read, so those plugin/skill checks are executable. It exposes no custom-agent list method. An isolated valid custom-agent TOML does not appear in codex debug prompt-input, and config/read does not expose the loaded custom-agent catalog. Proposal section 10 nevertheless relies on a debug prompt/config observable for exact agent types.
Consequence: The compatibility gate can prove plugin skills while silently failing to prove that the five personal or Home Manager TOMLs were discovered, did not shadow built-ins, and disappeared after removal.
Exact correction: Name and prove a real binary-level agent observable. One hermetic option is a local fake Responses provider that captures the collaboration tool schema emitted by a fresh pinned Codex process; assert its agent-type surface before install, after companion install, after Home Manager activation, and after removal, without a network/model dependency. If no deterministic binary observable is available, state that limitation and move agent enumeration to the separately labeled model UAT instead of calling debug/config deterministic. Keep skills/list and plugin/list/read as the deterministic skill/plugin layer. The test must fail when one TOML is missing, duplicated, malformed, or renamed.

IMPORTANT I3 — The release checksum bootstrap has no public checksum grammar or negative acceptance matrix.
Evidence: Sections 3, 5, and 9 require an exact release tag, a checksum artifact name, SHA-256 verification, and checksum publication, but they do not define the checksum file format, expected binary roster/filenames, duplicate-entry handling, or the activation boundary. The mandatory test list says hashes generally but does not require corrupt/truncated/missing/duplicate/wrong-platform checksum failures or prove that no executable is activated on those failures. The current release workflow publishes binaries only and will need a concrete aggregator contract.
Consequence: The fresh-user bootstrap and release job can implement incompatible parsers, or verification can accidentally accept the wrong artifact while still satisfying a positive happy-path test.
Exact correction: Freeze a strict checksum contract in InstallCLISpec and the bundle manifest, for example a named SHA256SUMS grammar with canonical filenames derived from the supported OS/architecture/binary matrix. Reject missing, duplicate, malformed, path-bearing, wrong-platform, and hash-mismatched entries before chmod/rename. Download into a private temporary path, verify bytes, then atomically activate; preserve the prior executable on every failure. Add a local fake-release integration suite for all negative cases, matrix tests that every release binary appears exactly once, and a post-release gate that downloads the actual tag/checksum artifact and runs capabilities before Aura can change from NOT_AVAILABLE to AVAILABLE.

IMPORTANT I4 — The prior clean-machine prerequisite finding is represented in prose but not in the executable validation matrix.
Evidence: Section 6 now defines the correct prerequisite probes and repository-policy behavior, but section 10's network/model UAT only explicitly demonstrates depth paths, agent selection, missing-plugin behavior, and setup permission. BDD 5 says fresh setup reports prerequisites, yet no case matrix covers absent or incompatible pasture, absent bd, absent Git, required-but-missing git agent-commit, a policy that permits ordinary commit, optional aura-swarm absence, and the fully provisioned path. Round 1 required both failure diagnostics and a clean fully provisioned run.
Consequence: Each individual probe can exist while their ordering, required/optional classification, and stop-versus-continue behavior remain wrong on the primary new-user path.
Exact correction: Add an isolated clean-machine matrix to the setup UAT using temporary HOME/CODEX_HOME/PATH and fixture repositories. Cover each missing/incompatible prerequisite, conditional commit policies, optional swarm, exact-release bootstrap, and the all-present path through healthy status. Assert the six actionable-error fields, no task DB/default-home/Git-config/hook mutation, no download of latest, and no request for agent-home permission before non-mutating prerequisite failures are reported. Keep one real model-driven setup run for end-user behavior and test the generated prerequisite matrix/order structurally so CI is not dependent only on model compliance.

MINOR M1 — The updated research report still contains superseded recommendations.
Evidence: Its adversarial disposition correctly adopts target-owned protocol assets, personal companion-XOR-Home-Manager ownership, structural RuntimeText, and managed-directory recovery. But the earlier surface table still recommends a Codex verbatim allowlist for protocol/install-cli, numbered recommendation 5 omits capabilities, numbered recommendation 6 again makes future project delivery a mutually exclusive Codex-home owner, and the validation list still claims duplicate detection anywhere in the recursive project/personal tree. Those statements conflict with Proposal 2 and URD Amendment 2.
Consequence: The implementation handoff can follow the stale numbered recommendation rather than the later correction, recreating Round 1 defects despite a sound proposal body.
Exact correction: Rewrite the stale table, numbered recommendations, and validation bullets to the final R20-R31 design; add a short supersession note if historical text is intentionally retained.

Prior-finding disposition: Round 1 asset coverage, default-depth topology, structural RuntimeText, one SkillDescriptor catalog, agent delivery/context policy, managed-directory SIGKILL transaction, personal ownership scope, Home Manager activation fixture, CLI/status/version ownership, exact artifact inventory, creator-validator independence, black-box Cobra coverage, marketplace policy, dependency probes, invocation identity, and slice ownership are materially resolved in Proposal 2. Home Manager and exact-inventory tests are now stated at executable production seams. The remaining items above are narrower test-contract gaps and must be corrected before a clean ACCEPT round.

BLOCKER B1 — The normative recovery rule contradicts the zero-write and read-only CLI contract.
Evidence: URD Amendment 2 R25 says every command recovers an interrupted journal first. The same amendment says plan is a zero-write snapshot, and R26 defines capabilities, plan, and status as observational commands. Proposal 2 Section 6 repeats that plan is zero-write and bundle-less status reports interruption health, while Section 7 only defines the exclusive lock for mutations and still requires recovery before mutation. These rules cannot all hold when a PREPARED, OLD_MOVED, or NEW_ACTIVE journal exists: following R25 makes plan/capabilities/status mutate the home without scoped permission, while following the zero-write/reporting contract leaves R25 false. The proposal also requires concurrent read tests but never states whether status takes the transaction lock, blocks, returns busy, or may observe directory/ledger states across the commit boundary.
Consequence: the installer cannot implement the ratified contract consistently. A user asking only for a plan, capability report, or health status may trigger recovery writes; an unlocked status may transiently report healthy state as corrupt or vice versa during install/uninstall. This breaks the consent boundary, stable exit semantics, and BDD 5 through 7.
Exact correction: amend R25 and Proposal 2 so only explicitly mutating install/uninstall, or a separately authorized recover command/flag, performs recovery after taking the exclusive lock. Make capabilities state-independent and zero-write. Make plan and status zero-write for every journal state and take a coherent shared/exclusive snapshot under the same cross-process locking regime; define bounded wait versus stable busy exit. Status must report the exact journal state and recovery action without applying it. Add compiled-binary subprocess assertions that capabilities/plan/status preserve all bytes and mtimes with journals at every durable boundary, plus concurrent status at PREPARED, OLD_MOVED, NEW_ACTIVE, and ledger commit.

The document labels this policy exact, so leaving the implementation to infer a corrected path/key is not a harmless presentation omission.
