author: David Huu Pham
text:
ARCHITECT RESPONSE — guard accepted, with a coverage correction.

You got the hard part right. The invariant is CONTAINMENT, not set equality: every declared identity must appear in the pinned payload shape, while the payload shape legitimately carries fields that are not identities. That is the question I asked you to derive from the data rather than assume, and encoding set equality would have produced a test that fails today for no good reason. Generic over the event enum, covering Claude and Codex, with a failure message naming event, field and the table to edit - all correct.

But the guard covers only half the hazard, and the report claims more than it delivers. Recording this rather than leaving the coverage overstated.

The guard checks: identity is absent from payload shape -> caught.
It does not check: payload shape loses a field that is NOT an identity.

That second direction is the one the task was filed for, and it is the dangerous one. claudeNativeFields declares SessionStart as {source, model, session_title}, none of which is an identity - the only identity is session_id. Delete "source" from that table and your guard stays green, because source was never an identity. The frontend's per-event allowed-set then rejects every real SessionStart payload Claude sends, in production, while the diff reads as tightening. PreToolUse is worse: {tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id} where only tool_use_id is an identity, so two of three fields are unguarded.

This is not a defect in your work - it is the limit of what a parity test between these two tables can prove. Neither table is a record of what the host ACTUALLY sends; the payload shape is the only claim about that, so it cannot be checked against itself. Closing the second direction needs a corpus of authentic captured host payloads, which is real work and a separate task.

Note the same erosion defeats TestParseToleratesEveryFieldTheHostLegitimatelySends from the Claude frontend slice: it iterates the same table, so removing a field silently removes the assertion. Two tests that look like they guard this, neither of which does.

Filing the fixture-corpus task separately. Your guard stays: it is correct, it bites, and it closes the direction that CAN be closed by construction. Please add one comment to the test naming what it does not cover, so the next reader does not infer more from a green check than it earns - that is the same failure mode as the permanently-red grep from the lowering slice, inverted.

Confirmed OpenCode has no payload-shape table yet; it lands with that frontend at M2, and the architect designing M2 has been told not to add a third unguarded pair.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
POLICY CHANGE — workers commit per completed slice.

Previous instruction to workers was no_commit/no_push, with the supervisor landing everything at the end. That is reversed: each worker commits its own slice when its gates pass, and pushes.

Rationale for the change is sound and worth recording: batching five slices into one landing means a single commit that cannot be reverted, bisected, or reviewed independently, and it leaves thousands of lines of working-tree state that no gate has ever run against in a committed configuration. Per-slice commits also make the file-ownership rule enforceable after the fact rather than only by instruction.

Backfilled the four completed units now, one commit each, gates verified before each:
  0f7380e  feat(lifecycle): the canonical lifecycle IR waist        SLICE-1
  4c9c959  feat(lifecycle): the lowering pass                       SLICE-3
  cbed960  feat(lifecycle): the Claude frontend                     SLICE-2
  fb9cd8d  test(codegen): identity/payload-shape parity guard       followup
All pushed. gofmt clean, go vet clean, race tests pass for internal/lifecycle/... and internal/codegen/...

SLICE-4 (aura-plugins-waxkv) is still in flight under the old no_commit instruction; its six files remain untracked and were deliberately excluded. Its work will be committed on completion, and every worker dispatched after this point carries the commit mandate instead.

Standing worker instruction from here:
  - commit with `git agent-commit` when your slice's gates pass, then push
  - one commit per slice, staging ONLY the files you own by path, never `git add -A`
  - if the tree is red from another worker's in-flight slice, confirm the failure
    is not in a file you own before committing, and say so in the commit message
  - still do not close Beads tasks; slice closure remains the supervisor's after review

author: David Huu Pham
text:
AMENDMENT — runtime reverse lookup prerequisite discovered after proposal creation.

Read aura-plugins-57lhx and the later IMPL_PLAN comment. The proposal wording that each frontend owns a contract-derived native-name index is superseded before M2 implementation: use `runtime.LifecycleContract[E].EventByNativeName(name string) (E, error)` from aura-plugins-57lhx. That API validates against the closed pinned catalogue while preserving the typed `Mapping(E)` boundary; it removes the copied Claude/OpenCode/Codex reverse maps rather than merely deriving each independently.

M2-S1 must block on aura-plugins-57lhx and `opencode.Frontend` must retain only the pinned contract, not a `byName` map. The frontend still calls `BindEvent(contract, typedEvent)`, and the rest of the proposal remains unchanged. The actor fixed-ID derivation may iterate the closed typed catalogue only to obtain its stable ordinal after origin validation; it must not construct a second native-name lookup map.

This is a correction to the prior plan, not an interface expansion of `lifecycle.Frontend`: no surface/output parameter is added. The distinction is important: the original no-string-lookup rationale overreached; the real invariant is that host spelling resolves through one contract-derived, validating lookup, not that frontends reimplement it.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE - axis A, round 1. 0 BLOCKER, 1 IMPORTANT (aura-plugins-mgn58), 1 MINOR (aura-plugins-zeij9).

Every acceptance criterion these three slices own is met by the delivered code. The IMPORTANT is not a defect in behaviour; it is that the enforcement mechanism the plan bought for the target-agnostic invariant does not exist and could not work as specified. The MINOR is a plan-text correction, not a code change.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED, AND HOW

1. Waist invariant - HOLDS. Semantics carries {semantic, blocking, identities} only (event.go:259-264). All five target axes (surface, mutation, order, reconciliation, failure) plus stopLoop are absent, and are retained instead on the unexported Origin.behaviour with no accessor (event.go:330-336), matching plan Section 3.1 D9. Structurally pinned, not just observed, by TestWaistTypesHaveNoFieldForPastureAuthority and TestSemanticsCarriesNoTargetDetailTypes (event_test.go:356-427), plus the method-count pins at backend_test.go:93-95. Nothing target-specific leaks.

2. NewEvent as verifier - ALL SIX RULES PRESENT AND EFFECTIVE (event.go:475-611). Unbound binding :477; zero digest :487; the (Kind, NativeName) PAIR check :554-574; required-field sweep :592-607; duplicate-pair rejection :576-587; value re-validation :550. I could not construct an input producing a verified Event that violates a stated invariant. The pair check is genuinely load-bearing: findDeclaredField matches by name, and runtime lifecycle.go:362-369 guarantees native names are unique within a mapping, so name-lookup-then-kind-compare is exactly equivalent to a pair check with no hole between them.

3. Lower never varies by harness - TRUE TODAY. lower.go references no BackendView, has no harness branch, and origin.Harness() appears only inside error formatting (:280, :304, :393, :426). Deps exposes no lifecycle-table accessor, pinned by TestLowerNeedsNothingFromTheBackendView. The indirect path DOES exist - Origin.behaviour is same-package - and is filed as aura-plugins-mgn58.

4. Replay identity - INJECTIVE. ReplayKey = field(contract) field(nativeEventName) field(hex digest) (key.go:77-86). I could not construct a collision, and the reason is solid rather than empirical: strconv.Itoa emits no leading zeros, so the digit run before the first colon uniquely determines each field length, every field boundary is recoverable, and two distinct triples cannot render identically. Distinct payloads stay distinct and byte-identical redelivery collapses (key_test.go:214-225, lower_test.go:343-378).

5. Claude frontend fidelity - CORRECT FOR ALL 30 EVENTS. Strict decode is a token-walk (ir/strictjson.go:92-146) rejecting duplicate members at ANY nesting depth, non-objects, trailing values, and an omitted hook_event_name - genuinely stronger than DisallowUnknownFields, as claimed at frontend.go:222-239. I did not take the per-event allowed-set on trust: I dumped allowedFields(event, identities) from the frontend and the codegen union claudeNativeFields(name) + declared identities for all 30 pinned events and diffed them. IDENTICAL, zero differences. The frontend accepts exactly the shape the generated adapter pins.

6. Refusals write nothing - HOLDS. Every refusal in Lower returns before deps.Recorder is touched, proven positively rather than by absence: lower_internal_test.go:54-69 uses fakes that t.Fatal if called at all, and the black-box table asserts empty records plus zero resolver calls (lower_test.go:243-244). Frontend Parse is pure by import list (ir, errors, lifecycle, runtime + stdlib).

ADVERSARIAL PASS - I did not trust the suite either

Every worker on this epic found one of their own tests proving less than it appeared to, so I broke six claimed-critical behaviours and confirmed a real test fails each time:

  (Kind,NativeName) pair check disabled  -> FAIL TestNewEventRejectsIdentityWhoseKindDoesNotMatchTheDeclaredPair
  encodeField -> separator scheme        -> FAIL 4 tests, incl. the matching separator subtest
  blocking refusal disabled              -> FAIL TestLowerRefusesAnAwaitedOccurrenceWithoutWriting
  identity sort removed                  -> FAIL 2 tests
  rejectUnknownFields disabled           -> FAIL TestParseRejectsUnknownFields + ...BelongingToAnotherEvent
  verifier value re-validation removed   -> FAIL TestVerifierDoesNotTrustAConstructedIdentityFlag (5 subcases)

The collision table specifically is honest: each case carries a require.Equal precondition proving a separator-free encoder really would collide on it, so it cannot pass against a broken encoder. That is the trap SLICE-1 reported hitting and fixing, and the fix holds.

One mutation SURVIVED - the per-host branch in aura-plugins-mgn58. That is the finding.

Gate: nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/lifecycle/... -> ok, ok. All mutations reverted; git diff HEAD empty; the six untracked SLICE-4 files are byte-identical to baseline and were not reviewed.

NOT RE-FILED (already tracked): aura-plugins-m21w5, aura-plugins-ay4yn, aura-plugins-9umx1, and aura-plugins-noqor (the two hand-maintained payload tables - I confirmed they agree today and that a parity guard has since landed).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE - M1-REVIEW-A-1-general (axis A, correctness), review record aura-plugins-7mmj7.

0 BLOCKER, 1 IMPORTANT (aura-plugins-mgn58), 1 MINOR (aura-plugins-zeij9).

The three completed slices implement this plan faithfully. Every acceptance criterion they own is met: semantics and target behaviour are derived from the pinned contract and never caller-supplied; a mis-kinded identity is rejected; actors/assignments/JournalIDs/revisions/evidence have no field to occupy; distinct payloads produce distinct records and identical redelivery collapses; blocking events are refused with nothing written; a nil Deps field fails actionably with no time.Now fallback. Lower today references no BackendView and carries no harness branch.

Two items against the PLAN rather than the code.

1. IMPORTANT - Section 3.1 sells BackendView on one benefit: collapsing the target-agnostic invariant to a question "answerable mechanically rather than by reading for intent". As delivered it is answerable only by reading for intent. The plan qualifies the argument with "Go cannot make this compiler-enforced ACROSS PACKAGES" - but lower.go is in the SAME package as Origin, so Origin.behaviour is an ordinary readable field and the greppable question has a blind spot precisely where the invariant applies. Demonstrated during review: a real per-host branch that silently reports success and writes nothing for one harness compiles, greps clean for BackendView, and passes the entire suite. Separately, the check lower_test.go:471 says is performed "outside the test binary" is performed nowhere - no Makefile target, no CI step. Preferred remedy is a package split (internal/lifecycle/lowering) which makes the boundary compiler-enforced and removes the need for a grep at all.

2. MINOR - D11 (:302-304) and the acceptance criterion (:402-403) require the awaited-reply refusal to carry the string "M5". AGENTS.md forbids process artefacts in user-facing error messages, so the implementation correctly omits it and pins that with a test asserting its absence. The plan text should be amended to require naming the missing capability instead, with the deviation recorded - otherwise it reads as a permanently unmet criterion and invites someone to add it back against the standard.

Neither item requires reworking the shipped waist, verifier, lowering pass, or Claude frontend.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## Component 2: Blocking-event refusal (D11) + dependent question on Digest

**Definition shown:**
  D11 - M1..M3 refuse any event whose Blocking is not NonBlocking, with an
  actionable error, writing nothing.

**Motivating example shown:**
  The pinned table gives Claude FailureExitTwoBlocks for blocking events: exit
  code 2 IS 'deny'. So a non-zero exit while REFUSING a PreToolUse can deny the
  user's tool call. Refusing loudly and breaking the user's editing session are
  the same action. Theoretical at M1 (only SessionStart registered), real at M2/M3.

**Question asked:** "A blocking event (e.g. PreToolUse) reaches Pasture before M5 exists. Claude reads exit code 2 as 'deny'. How should Pasture refuse?"

**Options presented:**
  - Never register blocking hooks until M5: generator emits registrations only for events Pasture can handle; legalization at generation time; cost is hooks.json covering fewer events than the pinned table, needing a visible withheld report.
  - Refuse loudly, non-zero exit: current D11; impossible to miss; cost is that on Claude and Codex it can deny the user's tool call.
  - Exit 0, record as observation: session unaffected, occurrence logged; cost is an event declared a gate silently not gating.
  - Exit 0, warn on stderr, record nothing: session unaffected; cost is the occurrence is lost and hook stderr is rarely read.

**User response (verbatim selection):** "Never register blocking hooks until M5"

**Question asked:** "With dedup gone, PayloadDigest no longer has a job. What should happen to it?"

**Options presented:**
  - Keep as payload provenance: proves which bytes produced this IR, lets a reader detect retries; cost is a field with no enforced consumer.
  - Keep and store the raw payload too: fully reconstructible, would close the host-payload-corpus gap; cost is unbounded growth and payloads may carry prompt text or file contents.
  - Remove it entirely: existed only for the replay key; shrinks the frozen surface; cost is no post-hoc way to tell retries from genuine repeats.

**User response (verbatim selection):** "Remove it entirely"

**Open-ended feedback (VERBATIM):**
"How is ObservedAt half of the disambiguation pair? the disambiguator pair is only the autoincrementing integer ID."

**Disposition: FIX-NOW** (echoed for confirmation)

**Architect correction, recorded against myself:** The user is right and my stated consequence in the component-1 handover was wrong. The autoincrementing row ID is unique by construction and disambiguates on its own; ObservedAt is descriptive metadata about when an occurrence happened, not a component of identity. My claim that the clock becomes 'semantically load-bearing' under append-always is withdrawn - the clock's role is unchanged, and nothing about dedup or identity depends on it.

**Consequences to fold into the next proposal:**
  - Digest, NewDigest deleted; EventBinding.NewEvent(digest, identities) narrows to NewEvent(identities). This changes SLICE-1's already-committed surface.
  - The Claude frontend stops digesting.
  - Generation-time legalization is NEW work in codegen: hooks.json must omit blocking events, and must report what was withheld and why, or the omission is itself a silent no-op.
  - Runtime refusal is retained as defence in depth for hand-written host configs, but is no longer the primary mechanism and no longer the thing standing between a user and a broken session.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## Component 3: Authority boundary (revised after architect framing error)

**First pass - ARCHITECT ERROR.** I offered a 'Telemetry only, permanently' option and the user selected it, then asked: "Maybe I didn't understand what you meant by 'telemetry only'. What's the issue here? a hook on a blocking hook will cause the associated native event to fail?"

The question exposed that my options were built on a bad premise and my explanation had implied blocking hooks make the native event fail. They do not. Blocking means the host WAITS for the hook process and INTERPRETS its exit code: exit 0 proceeds, exit 2 denies (Claude/Codex FailureExitTwoBlocks), other non-zero reports and continues, and a hang stalls the host.

The real hazard is narrower: AGENTS.md maps exit code 2 to CategoryConnection, so an internal connection failure would exit 2 and Claude would read it as DENY, silently converting an unrelated Pasture fault into a denial of the user's work. That - not event failure - is why I had proposed withholding blocking registrations.

**User verbatim on the first pass:** "keep those; telemetry onle was wrong"

**Question asked (re-framed):** "a native event may cause Pasture to ANSWER a waiting host. Separately - may a native event ever WRITE protocol state (advance a phase, close a task, record a decision)?"

**Options presented:**
  - Answer yes, write never: gates allow/deny from existing state; no event writes protocol facts.
  - Answer yes, write only explicit human responses: gates may not write, but ElicitationResult - where a human answered a Pasture-originated prompt - may record that decision; requires byte-exact request-id correlation, which the pinned table already enforces.
  - Answer yes, gates may record their own consultation: decision trail with ambiguous authority.
  - Full authority: events drive transitions.

**User response (verbatim selection):** "Answer yes, write only explicit human responses"

**Question asked:** "how should the lifecycle command handle its own internal failures on a blocking hook?"

**Options presented:**
  - Lifecycle command never exits 2 except deliberate deny (own exit-code contract).
  - Never exit non-zero at all; report on stderr.
  - stdout JSON for verdicts, exit code only for process health.

**User response (VERBATIM):** "Let's JUST exit 0 for now and report on stderr. However: this does not mean 'never exit non-zero'. In future iterations, we will want Pasture's lifecycle and current phase to potentially block some tools from occurring."

**Disposition: FIX-NOW** (echoed for confirmation)

**Consequences:**
  - M5 and M6 are RETAINED. The Responder / response-encoding half of the architecture stays.
  - Authority boundary: gates may ANSWER; only explicit-human-response events may WRITE, and only under byte-exact request-id correlation.
  - Exit 0 always is an explicitly TEMPORARY posture, not the final contract. C2 (exit 2 means CategoryConnection vs deny) remains OPEN and must be resolved before any real deny ships.
  - D11 MUST CHANGE. Refusing a gate event while exiting 0 records nothing and answers proceed - a silent no-op, the exact failure mode this architecture exists to remove. Pre-M5, a gate event must be RECORDED as evidence of consultation and answered proceed, with no authority exercised. Refusal is the wrong verb.
  - Component 2's 'never register blocking hooks' is therefore SUPERSEDED: with always-exit-0, blocking hooks are safe to register, and withholding them would discard the richest telemetry in the catalogue (PreToolUse carries tool_input).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## UAT REQUIREMENT CLARIFICATION — provenance, determinism, and versioned SDLC codebook

**Context:** Asked whether ElicitationResult should be the only native event permitted to write protocol state, and asked the user to choose M1 treatment. User rejected the premise and requested a hook-by-hook audit.

**User response (VERBATIM):**
"There are definitely more hooks that should be allowed in the write path. Audit the Claude Hooks for me, where you place them, why, and how they might interact bi-directionally with the Pasture system."

**Additional user clarification (VERBATIM):**
"One of the main reasons that Pasture exists is to shift agentic workflows towards more deterministic directions, where the SDLC was shfited into explicitly named and phased pieces. This is my own conceptualization and not meant to be the ultimate generic model, but it allows rich metadata into the early stages of what might become a generic model for an agents-and-humans-in-the-loop SDLC. The other goal was to be able to track at a fine-grained level which decisions were made by humans, when humans gave their input, and what was done by the agent. That is, fine-grained data provenance within agent coding sessions, turns, and to be able to trace back to the human signal that prompted, designed, motivated, architected, and verified it --- from the code that is created by agents, even with a multi-agent orchestration setup being used inbetween to create that code. This would be enabled by our metadata enrichment by committing to some code book for the SDLC at an early stage, though that WILL be subject to change, and it is important to know which version of the codebook and Pasture Epoch system that was used."

**Disposition: FIX-NOW proposed — awaiting user confirmation after the hook audit.**

**Architect interpretation to test, not silently assume:**
The earlier UAT question conflated all writes. The design needs at least two planes:
  1. EVIDENCE / PROVENANCE WRITES — append-only facts that a native event occurred, what agent/human/session/turn/artifact it relates to, and which versioned SDLC codebook + Epoch implementation interpreted it. These should be broad and fine-grained.
  2. NORMATIVE PROTOCOL WRITES — transitions, decisions, approvals, assignment changes, and other facts that alter what the deterministic SDLC permits next. These require stronger authority and correlation rules.

A hook may always write evidence without being allowed to manufacture a protocol transition. Explicit human responses are one normative source, but likely not the only legitimate write path. The Claude hook catalogue must be audited event-by-event against these planes rather than classified by the earlier binary 'telemetry vs write' question.

**New load-bearing requirement:** Every enriched record must carry enough version identity to answer which SDLC codebook and which Pasture Epoch implementation interpreted the occurrence. The codebook is intentionally provisional and expected to evolve; records must remain interpretable after it changes.

author: David Huu Pham
text: UAT requirement clarification captured verbatim on aura-plugins-q5ams. Pasture's goals include deterministic explicitly named/phased SDLC, fine-grained human/agent provenance across sessions/turns/multi-agent orchestration, traceability from generated code back to human signals, and version identity for both the evolving SDLC codebook and Pasture Epoch implementation. Requires architectural revision: separate evidence/provenance writes from normative protocol transitions and audit all Claude hooks bidirectionally.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## UAT REQUIREMENT CLARIFICATION — context and harness engineering

**User clarification (VERBATIM):**
"It is also for context and harness engineering: so that we have progressive disclosure as the agents move through an FSM, determined by our model of the SDLC."

**Architect interpretation to test in the hook audit:**
The emerging architecture has THREE distinct planes, not the previous telemetry/write binary:

  1. EVIDENCE / PROVENANCE PLANE
     Append-only facts: native event, human/agent identity, session, turn, tool
     call, artifact, decision inputs and outputs, causal links.

  2. NORMATIVE CONTROL PLANE
     FSM state, legal transitions, gates, approvals, assignments, and authority
     to alter what the deterministic SDLC permits next.

  3. CONTEXT DISCLOSURE PLANE
     Phase- and role-scoped context/instructions/capabilities revealed to an
     agent as it moves through the FSM. Native hooks are harness integration
     points that may request, inject, refresh, or revoke context without thereby
     manufacturing a protocol transition.

The versioned SDLC codebook is not only an analytics taxonomy. It is executable
metadata that classifies evidence, constrains legal transitions, and determines
progressive context disclosure. Therefore every interpreted event needs to be
traceable to the codebook version and Pasture Epoch implementation version that
made those decisions.

**Disposition remains FIX-NOW proposed, awaiting user confirmation after the complete hook audit.**

author: David Huu Pham
text: Additional verbatim UAT requirement on aura-plugins-q5ams: Pasture is also for context/harness engineering and progressive disclosure as agents move through an SDLC FSM. Audit/design must separate evidence, normative control, and context-disclosure planes; versioned codebook governs all three.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## UAT REQUIREMENT CLARIFICATION — broad automated write ingress, semantic alignment

**User clarification (VERBATIM):**
"Keeping this in mind, yes: we will need many hooks that WILL be in the write gate: data entry into the Pasture ecosystem needs to be as automated as possible, but this automation needs to be as semantically aligned as possible as well."

**Architect correction to vocabulary:**
Stop treating "write path" as synonymous with "may advance the FSM." The intended pipeline separates broad automated ingress from semantic interpretation and normative authority:

  native hook
      -> [1] append occurrence               broad, automated, lossless
      -> [2] versioned codebook interpretation one occurrence -> many typed facts
      -> [3] correlate and enrich             human/agent/turn/task/artifact lineage
      -> [4] provenance writes                broad, automated
      -> [5] candidate FSM transition          automatic proposal, non-authoritative
      -> [6] context projection                progressive disclosure for current state
      -> [7] normative FSM commit              separate authority verification

**Derived principle to confirm in revised UAT:**
Automate data entry, not semantic guessing. When a hook has insufficient identity or causal context for one interpretation, append the occurrence and record an explicit unresolved/candidate fact. Do not silently drop it, collapse it, or manufacture normative authority.

This means many hooks belong on automated write paths at layers 1-6. The hook-by-hook audit must state WHICH write(s) each event performs rather than answer one binary "may write?" question. Normative transition authority remains a distinct decision per event and per codebook rule.

**Disposition: FIX-NOW proposed — part of the active PROPOSAL-5 audit/rewrite.**

Architecture must separate occurrence ingress, versioned interpretation, enrichment/provenance, candidate transitions, context projection, and normative commits rather than use a binary write/no-write classification.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## Architecture audit addendum — repository-state grounding

This addendum incorporates the read-only audits completed after the proposal body was created. It clarifies implementation boundaries; it does not alter the UAT authority in `aura-plugins-q5ams`.

### Existing platform state that the implementation must extend

- `pkg/protocol/types.go` and `state_machine.go` already provide typed `PhaseId`, `PhaseSpec`, and `EpochState.CurrentPhase`; `enums.go` provides `RoleId`. Engine state is a mutable `epoch_state_projection` written/read through `internal/engine/projection.go`. Current phase history is only an audit row, whereas decision/UAT/ratification commands already use Provenance `Journal().Apply`. The new control plane must first journal an immutable transition fact and only then update the projection cache.
- There are two separately maintained phase sources: `pkg/protocol/state_machine.go` and `internal/codegen/specs_data.go`. S1 must make one canonical codebook source or add an exact parity test as an integration gate.
- Sessions exist only as `RegisterSessionSignal`/`SessionEntry` projection JSON and `session_entries`; roles there are strings, no durable session-to-epoch/actor/runtime-contract binding exists, and no native turn is persisted. S1/S2 must add typed session/turn bindings. Preserve a host turn ID when supplied; otherwise allocate a monotonic sequence scoped to the bound session.
- Assignment episode state is already a stronger, journal-backed typed path in `internal/tasks/assignment_transfer.go` and `timeline_projection.go`; control commits should consume it rather than create parallel assignment state.
- `audit_events` currently has `(id, phase, agent_id, event_type, payload, timestamp, dedup_key)` and `context_edges` are typed lookup attachments, not causal edges. New occurrence/interpretation/causal tables are additive migrations; do not overload `context_edges` to mean causality.
- Current lifecycle recording directly inserts an `activities` row, bypassing Provenance `Journal().Apply` and `journal_activity_creations`. New occurrence evidence must use journal-backed evidence plus `EffectActivityCreate`, retaining an audit row only as a query projection.
- Existing artifact `Manifest`/`Bundle` is immutable/content-addressed but has no task/engine/audit association. S5 must link bundle identity and manifest reference through typed evidence; keep artifact bytes outside the unified SQLite forensic store.
- Existing versions are independent: CLI `v0.1.0`, plugin `0.0.4`, DBOS recovery cohort `1`, generated XML `2.0`, audit schema revision, adapter schema, and runtime-contract ID. The implementation identity tuple in this proposal is specifically required to prevent any one of these from being misreported as the complete provenance version.

### Compiler-enforced host boundary — correction and exact package layout

The proposal requires a stronger boundary than merely moving `Lower` while leaving host behavior exported from `internal/runtime`. Use:

```text
internal/lifecycle/model/                         occurrence-only public types
internal/lifecycle/ingress/                       frontends and capture orchestration
internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/ immutable host behavior/payload descriptors
internal/lifecycle/lowering/                      codebook interpretation and target-neutral effects
```

`lowering` can import `model` and public `pkg/protocol`, but Go rejects an import
of `ingress/internal/hostcontract` from `lowering`. No type in `model` carries a
host behavior mapping. A generator located under `ingress` emits a mechanical
registration manifest consumed by codegen; codegen does not import the host
contract and does not recreate its semantics. This gives the generator static
target data without opening a target-detail import path to lowering.

Accordingly, `internal/runtime/lifecycle.go` and `lifecycle_profiles.go` are
reworked: retain stable runtime-contract references and typed native names, but
move payload schema, blocking/mutation/failure behavior, and any response
descriptor into `ingress/internal/hostcontract`. The user-facing SDLC codebook
remains separate from this host contract. `Lower` is not permitted to receive
`LifecycleEventMapping`, a frontend, or any behavior-bearing dependency.

### Full prototype and generated-path disposition

| Asset | Disposition | Pivot reason |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/lifecycle/event.go`, `frontend.go` | Rework into `model` + ingress contracts | preserve constructor discipline/identity validation, remove digest, replay and hidden target behavior |
| `internal/lifecycle/key.go` and `key_test.go` | Delete | it exists for replay identity; database occurrence ID is now the only occurrence identity |
| `internal/lifecycle/backend.go` and `backend_test.go` | Delete | same-package side door is not an enforceable boundary |
| `internal/lifecycle/lower.go`, `lower_test.go`, `lower_internal_test.go` | Move/rewrite under `lowering` | target-neutral interpretation/effects remain useful; all replay assertions invert to append-always and the package boundary becomes compiler-enforced |
| `internal/lifecycle/claude/frontend.go`, `payload.go`, frontend tests/fixtures | Rework | retain strict duplicate-member and declared-identity checks; source schema from host contract; return capture plus parse disposition, not one semantic event |
| untracked `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go` and `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go` | Retain only as thin shapes, then rework | their parse-before-store/no-stdout structure is useful, but a malformed delivery policy and always-exit-0 response must be rebuilt |
| untracked `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder.go` and tests | Rework | preserve atomic journal/audit projection composition; remove `ON CONFLICT` dedup, replay-derived activity ID, direct activity insertion, and `RecordReplayed` |
| `internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go`, `codex_manifest.go`, `opencode_hooks.go` | Rework | retain registration emission only; delete foreign-language parsing, identity extraction, env-selected operation, and hidden adapter invocation |
| `internal/handlers/adapter.go`, `cmd/pasture/adapter.go` | Delete as lifecycle ingress | caller-selected hidden operations contradict compiler-owned lower/control selection; retain only DTO/service code that a target-neutral lower actually reuses |
| `hooks/scripts/pasture-lifecycle.py`, `.codex/hooks/pasture-lifecycle.py`, generated `hooks/hooks.json`, `.opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts` | Delete/regenerate | currently bypass the M1 waist and can map an internal exit 2 to host deny |
| `fb9cd8d` codegen parity test | Replace with one-descriptor coverage plus authentic fixture corpus | current guard checks identity containment only and cannot prove non-identity payload fields host reality |

### Dependency and follow-up handling

`aura-plugins-noqor` remains relevant until the triple payload-schema copies are
removed. `aura-plugins-9umx1` remains required for authentic host payload corpus
coverage. `aura-plugins-m21w5` remains a general actionable-error defect and
`aura-plugins-ay4yn` remains an unrelated full-race reliability defect; neither
is silently folded into the pivot. `aura-plugins-57lhx` retains its narrow role
as the sole validating native-name lookup, but it no longer implies the old
semantic waist is authoritative.

### Capture versus invalid input

Append-every-delivery deliberately changes the prior zero-store-on-invalid-input
rule. The ingress result distinguishes an unclassified `NativeOccurrence` with
a parse/contract issue from an interpreted fact. It appends bounded transport
metadata and the policy-controlled payload reference before interpretation; it
never opens a control transaction or creates a normative fact for an invalid
payload. Store-open failure is reported actionably on stderr and exits 0 for now,
but must not falsely claim that evidence was recorded.

text:
## PROPOSAL-5 historical status correction and review disposition

PROPOSAL-6 `aura-plugins-49fsf` now supersedes this draft. The earlier `STATUS: NON-AUTHORITATIVE DRAFT` comment was too broad: this task and its three independent reviews remain authoritative historical evidence of the design and review that occurred. They are not a ratified/current implementation plan, and all three review votes remain `REVISE`. Closing the review tasks as completed reviews does not convert those votes to ACCEPT or transfer consensus to PROPOSAL-6.

PROPOSAL-6 preserves this task unchanged, retains the 30-event audit exactly once, merges unique analysis from duplicate `aura-plugins-3b53b`, and incorporates the findings below.

### Axis A - correctness (`aura-plugins-a9ndn`)

1. **ACCEPT - authoritative capability and correlation boundary.** PROPOSAL-6 section 9 defines typed issuance, native-request binding before callback, exact runtime/session/request/tool/agent/task/worktree/epoch/role/actor/assignment scope, expiry, revocation, and transaction-local single-use consumption. A host claim without a current binding remains evidence/candidate only.
2. **ACCEPT - captured data contract.** Sections 5-6 define a generated closed field enum, typed bounded scalar/reference envelope, per-field capture class/state, explicit task/worktree/environment/context/artifact kinds, and unresolved output whenever required data is missing, redacted, forbidden, invalid, or not retained.
3. **ACCEPT - disclosure history and stop-loop invariants.** Section 10 replaces mutable disclosure state with immutable plan/send/ack/failure/revoke/suppress facts. `Stop` and `SubagentStop` append receipt first and append a suppressed-consultation fact when the active-loop guard prevents consultation.

### Axis B - test quality (`aura-plugins-xhqqr`)

1. **MODIFY - independent manifest and authentic all-30 corpus.** The requirement is accepted, but the fixture corpus blocks broad registration and M1/production completion rather than creation of a reviewable proposal. `aura-plugins-9umx1` is now a direct blocking dependency of `aura-plugins-sgxp6`; sections 12 and 14 require an independent manifest plus one authentic privacy-reviewed fixture for every pinned event.
2. **ACCEPT - append and malformed ingress end to end.** Sections 5, 12, 14, and 15 require file-backed and process-path coverage for byte-identical, semantic-equivalent, malformed, unknown, duplicate-key, truncated/invalid-UTF-8, over-limit, concurrent, and store-failure paths. Identifiable invalid input gets T1 only and temporary exit 0; no false recorded-success claim is allowed.
3. **ACCEPT - version persistence and query.** Sections 4, 7, 8, and 14 require immutable definition identity, same-occurrence interpretation under multiple versions, exact build/schema/contract filtering, dirty/missing identity behavior, and no implicit latest query.
4. **ACCEPT - real authority race.** Sections 9 and 14 require independently opened handles/processes racing distinct and shared single-use capabilities, exactly one normative winner, typed losers, exact retry, changed-operation conflict, and zero partial writes.
5. **MODIFY - context, artifact confidence, and privacy.** Observable disclosure and confidence tests are accepted now. Exact sensitive-content expectations intentionally wait for the focused Plan UAT choice in section 17; the conservative interim rule stores metadata/reference/redaction status and never unrestricted sensitive values.
6. **ACCEPT - executable package and integration fixtures.** Sections 10 and 14 require compile-pass/fail import-boundary fixtures, generated registration -> built binary -> Journal.Apply -> replayable projection -> bounded query proof, and removal/inversion of superseded digest/replay/pre-parse-refusal tests.

### Axis C - elegance (`aura-plugins-s3u3r`)

1. **ACCEPT - one Provenance substrate.** Sections 3 and 7 make `Journal().Apply` the sole semantic write path, journal/result-slot identities the only canonical lifecycle identities, lifecycle SQL rebuildable projections, and the existing `PhaseId`/`PhaseSpecs`/`EpochStateMachine` the sole FSM. No second graph, ledger, store, candidate CAS machine, or independently authoritative row ID remains.
2. **ACCEPT - preserve milestone boundaries.** Section 12 narrows M1 to receipt only, M2 to interpretation only, M3 to queries, M4 to context, M5 to native response, and M6 to authority. Tests prove the foundation cannot perform later-plane behavior.
3. **ACCEPT - generated artifact guard.** Sections 10, 12, and 14 require clean regeneration/golden drift checks and reject parsing, operation selection, semantic branching, or generic exit-to-deny mapping in generated code.
4. **ACCEPT - built production path.** M1 and section 14 require authentic fixtures through generated registration, real stdin, built binary, file-backed database, journal, projection, and query, including append-twice and temporary exit-0 assertions.
5. **ACCEPT - bounded readers.** Section 8 replaces unbounded slices/traversals with explicit page, snapshot, cursor, node, and edge bounds plus indexed filters.
6. **ACCEPT - phase/codebook parity.** Sections 3 and 14 require `protocol.PhaseSpecs` to remain normative and `internal/codegen/specs_data.go` transitions to be mechanically derived or exactly parity-tested.
7. **ACCEPT - clock, copies, and bounds.** Sections 5, 6, and 14 require injected clock/operation-ID source, defensive copies, deterministic ordering, and static input/field/output/context/query bounds.

No finding is rejected. The two MODIFY dispositions preserve the finding's user-visible outcome while locating the fixture gate at implementation readiness and leaving the unresolved privacy choice for explicit user UAT rather than silently choosing it.

The earlier comment naming `aura-plugins-3b53b` as PROPOSAL-5 recorded a duplicate draft created after the already reviewed `aura-plugins-gv9ca`. Preserve that comment as history, but use PROPOSAL-6 `aura-plugins-49fsf` as the current replacement draft.

PROPOSAL-6 preserves the reviewed draft, merges the duplicate's unique correct analysis, and incorporates every historical REVISE finding. This correction does not accept, ratify, close, or implement the proposal. This UAT remains open and blocks PROPOSAL-6. Sensitive-evidence retention, exact uncommitted-code provenance, and context-delivery mechanism remain explicit focused Plan UAT choices.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
INDEPENDENT AXIS B — TEST QUALITY / VALIDATABILITY REVIEW

Scope: PROPOSAL-6 (aura-plugins-49fsf), with UAT aura-plugins-q5ams, URD aura-plugins-hznvh, historical B review aura-plugins-xhqqr, fixture tasks aura-plugins-9umx1 and aura-plugins-noqor, and the current lifecycle/codegen/handler/recorder/race tests.

VOTE: REVISE

The proposal correctly carries forward the historical corpus requirement: §12 (proposal lines 598-611) makes 9umx1 block M1 completion/broad registration, §14.1 requires an independent manifest and authentic fixtures, §14.3 covers artifact confidence negatives/positives, and §14.4 calls for package fixtures, parity, replay, bounds, and inversion of superseded tests. The following load-bearing test contracts still need to be made executable and unambiguous.

BLOCKER 1 — No explicit built production path from registration through T2 to the bounded reader.
Evidence: §14.1 (lines 649-655) specifies generated registration -> built binary/stdin -> file-backed DB -> journal/projection query, but that is the T1/M1 path. §12 explicitly excludes semantic facts from M1 (lines 587-590). §14.4 (lines 700-704) separately says representative effects use Journal().Apply, but does not require those effects to originate from the generated command and does not name a single T2/T3 production-path test. A green suite could therefore test the interpreter or Apply with direct calls while the hook command only appends a receipt. The current prototype shows this separation: `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:123-163` parses before opening storage and `:198-215` calls the old lowering path; `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder.go:399-511` writes lifecycle tables directly; `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:204-260` proves only the old row/dedup path.
Exact fix: add a named M2/M3 black-box test that builds/uses the generated registration or trampoline, invokes the built `pasture hook lifecycle` binary with authentic fixture bytes on real stdin and an isolated file-backed SQLite file, drives the actual T2 orchestration, and queries through the public bounded LifecycleReader. Assert the T1 JournalID, T2 InterpretationID, exact version identity, facts/edges/candidates, and bounded page output. Add a separate M6 black-box authority test from the real hook/production service path to T3. The tests must fail if a test-only export, direct lifecycle SQL writer, or unit-only interpreter is substituted.

BLOCKER 2 — Authority validation omits executable expiry/revocation and exact-retry ordering, and the changed-operation requirement is ambiguous.
Evidence: §9 (lines 452-460) and the design checklist (line 824) claim issuance, expiry, revocation, binding, and single-use semantics. §14.3 (lines 678-684) only asks for races with distinct capabilities and one shared capability plus request binding/response attribution; it does not require an expired capability, revoked capability, scope mismatch, or revocation race. It also says “changed operation identity conflicts” (line 681), which must distinguish a same OperationID reused with different canonical input from a genuinely new OperationID. Existing `internal/engine/control_test.go:145-170` only tests signal-driven state changes, and `internal/engine/concurrency_spike_test.go:19-130` overlaps engines without racing a scoped single-use capability.
Exact fix: specify a file-backed SQLite test matrix with independent handles and separate processes: valid issue/bind; wrong actor, role, epoch, assignment, native binding, and operation; injected-clock expiry; revocation before and during commit; already-consumed capability; two distinct capabilities racing one expected state; and two consumers racing one capability. Snapshot journal, candidate, authority, control, and context rows before/after. Require one winner and one typed loser with no partial effects. Require exact same OperationID plus identical canonical input to return the original commit even after consumption/expiry, same OperationID plus changed candidate/capability/native input to return a typed conflict with zero writes, and a fresh OperationID to follow stale/consumed semantics rather than replay.

IMPORTANT 1 — Invalid-delivery outcome matrix is underspecified.
§5 (lines 291-297) correctly distinguishes an identifiable contract/event, which gets a T1 parse-status receipt, from an unidentifiable contract/event, which gets no receipt. §14.2 (lines 662-669) lists malformed, unknown-event/schema, duplicate-key, truncated/invalid-UTF-8, and over-limit inputs but does not say which side of that distinction each case occupies. Exact fix: add a table and BDD cases for (a) known harness plus registered event with malformed/duplicate/truncated/invalid-UTF-8/over-limit payload => bounded T1 parse issue, no T2/T3/context; (b) known event with unsupported schema => T1 `ParseUnsupportedSchema`; (c) payload-only unknown event => no receipt and explicit no-recorded-success diagnostic; (d) explicit registered event plus malformed bytes => T1 if transport coordinates are available; and (e) store open/write failure => exit 0, actionable redacted stderr, no false success. Exercise every case through the generated process path and independent/concurrent handles. The current opposite contract is asserted by `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_test.go:44-109` and `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:302-355`, so those tests must be inverted, not merely supplemented.

IMPORTANT 2 — Version evolution is not required to inspect every dependent output.
§14.2 (lines 670-674) requires two histories and missing/dirty identity handling, while §4/§7 describe identity propagation through parent batches. The test bullet does not require checking the exact immutable codebook/runtime/build reference on each fact, edge, candidate, control commit, artifact lineage edge, and disclosure. Exact fix: one version-evolution fixture must interpret one occurrence under two codebook definitions and two build identities, then query every dependent record type and assert its exact immutable reference and source JournalID. Tamper or replace a persisted definition and assert resolution fails closed. Cover same VCS revision with different build metadata, dirty/unreproducible identity, and missing identity; require unresolved interpretation with no confident fact or commit.

IMPORTANT 3 — Disclosure tests lack unauthorized/stale and candidate-only negative paths.
§14.3 (lines 685-686) covers positive plan/send/ack/failure/revoke/suppress history and scope, and §15 (lines 730-736) covers no-capability control rejection, but neither explicitly proves that a candidate or stale/unauthorized control result cannot create or alter disclosure history. Exact fix: drive candidate-only, wrong recipient, wrong phase/role/task/worktree, expired/revoked capability, stale current-state, unauthorized acknowledgement, and failed delivery cases through the real context projector/reader. Assert typed rejection, no new disclosure event except the prescribed failure/rejection evidence, no mutation of prior history, exact causal basis facts, and no candidate-as-committed-context.

IMPORTANT 4 — Privacy retention/tombstones and numeric bounds are not yet a testable contract.
§14.3 (lines 689-692) correctly makes canary expectations conditional on the focused retention UAT, but the proposal never defines tombstone behavior. §14.4 (lines 703-706) says static byte/field/output/context/query bounds without naming the maxima or the over-limit behavior, and §17 (lines 783-803) leaves three policy choices open while only the retention branch is explicitly conditioned in §14.3. Exact fix: define named maximum constants and reject/truncate/unresolved semantics for bytes, fields, outputs, context packets, page size, lineage nodes, and edges; seed a graph larger than every limit and assert bounded results and stable continuation. Make the canary suite parameterized by each UAT choice: before UAT, metadata/reference/redaction only; after retention selection, assert the selected raw-content policy, deletion/tombstone preservation of only permitted metadata, and no resurrection on replay. Run prompt/tool/transcript/path/elicitation canaries through store, projections, queries, stderr, and logs.

IMPORTANT 5 — Large-graph reader and per-milestone essential/deferred gates are only prose-level.
§8 (lines 382-391) defines page/snapshot/cursor/lineage bounds and §14.4 (lines 703-704) names reader tests, but neither requires a large fan-out/cycle graph fixture, cursor exhaustion, snapshot isolation, or proof that traversal stops at both node and edge caps. §12 gives milestone “main proof” summaries (lines 587-611) but does not map each validation case to an essential gate or a safe deferral. Exact fix: add a milestone test-gate table: M1 receipt/corpus/append-invalid cases; M2 all-30 independent manifest, authentic fixtures, T2 golden outputs and versioning; M3 bounded reader/replay and lineage ambiguity; M4 disclosure isolation/negative paths; M5 generated response/fail-open/drift; M6 authority issue/bind/expiry/revocation/replay/race; M7 per-contract differential corpus; M8 generated-artifact retirement. Mark exhaustive permutations and additional harness corpus as deferred only when they do not protect the current milestone invariant.

IMPORTANT 6 — Generated-artifact guard needs a failure-producing mechanical contract, not only the current positive adapter tests.
§14.1 (lines 656-658) requires generated code to contain no parsing, environment-selected operation, semantic branch, or generic exit-to-deny map, and §13 (lines 631-632) says the current tests are replaced. The current generator still emits all of those behaviors at `internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go:210-341`, while `internal/codegen/claude_hooks_test.go:114-265` tests the environment envelope, hidden operation selection, stop suppression, and exit-2 behavior. Exact fix: replace these tests with clean-tree generation plus structured source/manifest checks and a subprocess mutation table proving argv/env cannot choose an operation, generated code cannot parse semantic JSON, and blocking internal failure exits 0 without host deny. Keep target registration coverage tied to the independent corpus rather than to the generator’s own event table.

MINOR
None.

CHECKS RUN / SKIPPED
- Read the complete UAT task/comments, URD, PROPOSAL-6, historical Axis-B review and PROPOSAL-5, fixture tasks 9umx1/noqor, AGENTS.md, current lifecycle/Claude/codegen/handler/recorder tests, tracker race test, and engine concurrency/control tests.
- Passed: `nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/codegen/...`.
- Passed: `nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/handlers/... ./internal/tasks/...`. These tests pass the superseded prototype contract and therefore are not acceptance evidence for PROPOSAL-6.
- Skipped full repository/Nix/build gates because this is a design-only review of an unratified proposal; no production files, proposal fields, dependencies, commits, or pushes were changed.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Axis C review complete — VOTE: REVISE

BLOCKER findings and exact fixes:
1. T1 has no production actor/authority contract. Existing Provenance Apply requires an anchor actor and non-genesis authority, but NewOccurrence/Frontend.Capture specify neither; the current registry also covers only nine Claude agents while M1 promises 30 events. Fix: define one stable fixed software ingress actor, its journaled/bootstrap authority, idempotent registration, and a typed EffectEvidence result slot whose JournalID is the occurrence reference; native agent/session claims must remain evidence, not the Apply actor.
2. T2 enrichment/context has no composable production API. Codebook.Interpret is pure, OccurrenceRecord is undefined, and no bounded correlation snapshot, enrichment writer, ContextProjector, disclosure producer, or result-slot mapping is specified. Fix: define pure Interpret -> bounded InterpretationDraft, a separate snapshot-based Enricher that writes typed refs through Journal().Apply, and a ContextProjector that records plan/send/result/revoke facts; canonicalize NewOccurrence vs OccurrenceRecord and milestone gates.
3. The compiler boundary cannot be wired as written. internal/codegen cannot import internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract, while codegen already has a second descriptor table. Fix: make hostcontract the source of truth, generate an allowed-package registration manifest, have codegen consume only that manifest, and add compile-boundary plus clean-regeneration tests.
4. There is no implementable slice plan. No exact file ownership, leaf L1/L2/L3 tasks, dependency edges, merge timing, or disposition for the six untracked lifecycle prototypes is given; M1 is a horizontal mega-slice. Fix: add a P0/P1 vertical-slice table with exact owners, outcomes, integration-point gates, and explicit salvage/rewrite/quarantine disposition for every prototype.

IMPORTANT findings:
- Define historical codebook/interpreter retirement policy and stable fact-algebra evolution.
- Replace arbitrary string NativeEventName ingress with a contract-bound typed kind plus bounded unknown-token representation.
- Establish one authoritative source for the 30-hook audit and generate registrations from it.
- Set host deadline, SQLite work, fanout, storage-retention, and raw-content budgets.
- Resolve the contradictory disposition of untracked files in §13.
- Freeze only minimal M1/M2 public contracts; keep storage/projection DTOs private.

MINOR findings:
- Inject a clock for ReceivedAt.
- Specify defensive-copy guarantees for public slices/fields.
- Avoid conflating HostProceed and HostContinue until host semantics distinguish them.

Checks: read-only design review; no files edited or committed; no tests/build gates run because this is a plan review; no proposal dependency was added per assignment. Full assessment is in this task description.

text: VOTE: REVISE - PROPOSAL-6 is broadly proportional, but five public seams still permit incompatible durable implementations: the pinned Provenance API has no defined mapping for generic lifecycle causal edges; multi-effect transactions have no canonical operation anchor; the Epoch FSM remains mutable, injectable, and duplicated in codegen; occurrence interpretation emits context that requires committed-state inputs; and persisted SemanticFact evolution lacks one versioned envelope and unknown-schema policy. author: David Huu Pham

Required revisions: define the exact Provenance-backed causal representation without a second graph; define mandatory occurrence/interpretation/commit anchor identities for multi-effect Apply calls; derive generated phase metadata from one immutable non-injectable FSM and resolve existing back-edge drift; separate committed-state context policy from Codebook.Interpret; and freeze a bounded versioned SemanticFact envelope with unknown-schema behavior. These are durable public-contract choices, not worker implementation details.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## PROPOSAL-6 Round-2 finding disposition

This comment dispositions every finding from the six independent PROPOSAL-6
reviews before the replacement proposal is created. `ACCEPT` adopts the finding
as written. `MODIFY` adopts its user-visible or safety outcome but changes an
unsupported mechanism. No finding is rejected.

### Axis A general - aura-plugins-07vv6 - VOTE: REVISE

1. **MODIFY - pinned Claude claims.** Correct every row to the exact
   Claude 2.1.210 fields and behavior. `PermissionDenied` has no reason/source,
   `PostToolUse` has no duration or artifact identity, `PostCompact` has no
   summary, and `ElicitationResult` has one observed response with
   `MutationNone`. Missing information becomes unresolved or requires a cited
   enrichment fact; no later host contract is borrowed.
2. **MODIFY - Pasture-issued Elicitation chain.** Define the typed human-request,
   capability, native-binding, revocation, and atomic consumption contracts.
   Claude 2.1.210 has no proven Pasture-owned challenge round trip, so its
   `ElicitationResult` remains evidence/candidate only. The explicit registered
   human CLI remains normative until a later pinned contract proves exact
   correlation.
3. **ACCEPT - second Epoch writer.** Define one journal-backed phase-state fact
   and one control service using the immutable Epoch FSM. DBOS signals become
   candidates or invoke that service; `epoch_state_projection` and legacy audit
   rows become replayed compatibility projections, not writers.

### Axis A mini - aura-plugins-dzaky - VOTE: REVISE

1. **MODIFY - exact 30-hook fields.** Use exact field names and explicit
   unavailable markers. The replacement audit removes title/options/reason/
   duration/artifact/interrupt/summary claims that the pin cannot support.
2. **ACCEPT - T1 Apply contract.** Add one fixed lifecycle-ingress software
   actor, idempotent activation, the existing journaled system bootstrap
   authority, a static non-payload command digest, and an injected fresh
   operation-ID source. Native identities remain evidence claims. A mandatory
   `occurrence` evidence result slot supplies the occurrence JournalID.
3. **MODIFY - capability/Elicitation authority.** Define the complete capability
   state machine and atomic commit path, but do not preserve invented
   original/effective/overrider values for Claude 2.1.210. That pin records only
   the observed response and cannot authorize a human decision.
4. **ACCEPT - compiler boundary.** Host payload/behavior moves behind
   `ingress/internal/hostcontract`; target-neutral interpretation imports only
   occurrence/protocol types. A generated registration manifest is the only
   codegen input, and the same-package `BackendView` route is deleted.
5. **ACCEPT - causal representation.** Causal links are typed
   `EffectEvidence` records with journal/result-slot references. Their JournalID
   is their identity; SQL lineage rows are replayable indexes only. Provenance
   task edges are not overloaded and no second graph is introduced.
6. **ACCEPT - engine/audit path.** Rework the live engine control, workflow,
   projection, activity, handler, and transition-audit paths so no direct phase
   or lifecycle semantic writer remains.
7. **ACCEPT - definition retention.** Persist immutable definition snapshots,
   resolve exact historical refs, never select latest implicitly, and fail
   semantic use closed when an exact definition is unavailable.
8. **ACCEPT - context record contract.** Freeze recipient scope, committed-state
   basis, causal refs, version refs, context snapshot, and immutable
   plan/send/ack/failure/suppress/revoke records before selecting transport.
9. **ACCEPT - per-contract neutral response.** Define a mechanical neutral
   encoder for every pinned contract. Deliberate deny is unavailable before its
   later UAT and generic process failures can never become deny.
10. **ACCEPT - version constructors.** Version/codebook/build identifiers become
    constructor-validated bounded types, not caller-supplied bare strings.
11. **ACCEPT - numeric read bounds.** Name page, capture, output, context, node,
    edge, and invalid-zero behavior before public interfaces freeze.

### Axis B general - aura-plugins-s3gn3 - VOTE: ACCEPT

1. **ACCEPT - overall test strategy and vote.** Preserve the independent host
   corpus, real process/database/journal path, immutable-version, race,
   disclosure, lineage, privacy, package-boundary, phase-source, and bounded
   reader proofs.
2. **ACCEPT - connected M2/M3 path clarification.** Require one named
   generated-registration -> built binary/stdin -> T1 -> T2 -> public bounded
   reader black-box test. Disconnected direct-Apply/unit tests do not satisfy it.
3. **ACCEPT - typed fixture manifest clarification.** Keep typed fixture
   metadata while preserving authentic raw bytes in referenced files so YAML
   cannot normalize duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, ordering, or truncation.
4. **MODIFY - retention clarification.** Tombstone/deletion cases are mandatory
   only if focused UAT selects retained content. Under the interim metadata-only
   rule, tests prove no raw-content object exists to resurrect.

### Axis B mini - aura-plugins-ejxci - VOTE: REVISE

1. **ACCEPT - connected T2/T3 production paths.** Add the named M2/M3
   black-box path above and a separate M6 path from a real hook-produced
   candidate through the production authority service. Test-only exports,
   direct lifecycle SQL, and direct interpreter-only substitutes fail the gate.
2. **ACCEPT - authority matrix and retry ordering.** Test wrong actor, role,
   epoch, assignment, native binding, and operation; injected-clock expiry;
   revocation before and during commit; consumed state; two capabilities racing
   one phase; and two consumers racing one capability. Exact same OperationID
   plus identical canonical input returns the original result before current
   expiry/consumption checks; changed input conflicts; a fresh operation follows
   current stale/consumed semantics.
3. **ACCEPT - invalid-delivery matrix.** Define outcomes for registered-event
   malformed/duplicate/truncated/invalid-UTF-8/over-limit input, unsupported
   schema, unknown payload-only event, explicit registered event plus malformed
   bytes, event mismatch, and store failure. Exercise all through the generated
   process path and invert the old pre-parse/no-store tests.
4. **ACCEPT - exact version propagation.** One evolution fixture inspects every
   fact, link, candidate, control state, artifact link, and disclosure for exact
   runtime/codebook/schema/build/parent refs. Modified definitions fail closed;
   same VCS/different build, dirty, and missing identity are covered.
5. **ACCEPT - disclosure negative paths.** Exercise candidate-only, stale,
   unauthorized, wrong recipient/scope, expired/revoked capability,
   unauthorized acknowledgement, and failed delivery. Prior history is
   immutable and candidate state never drives context.
6. **MODIFY - privacy/tombstones/bounds.** Name all numeric limits now and make
   retention tests branch on focused UAT. Metadata-only is the pre-UAT contract;
   retained-content tombstones are specified only for a selected content mode.
7. **ACCEPT - large graph and milestone gates.** Use fan-out plus cycle fixtures,
   cursor exhaustion, snapshot isolation, both node/edge caps, and an explicit
   essential/deferred test table for every milestone.
8. **ACCEPT - generated-artifact negative guard.** Replace positive tests of the
   old Python adapter with clean regeneration and subprocess mutation cases
   proving argv/env cannot select semantics and internal failure remains neutral.

### Axis C general - aura-plugins-kycz0 - VOTE: REVISE

1. **ACCEPT - one-substrate mapping.** Use lifecycle evidence envelopes and
   typed link records over `EffectEvidence`; derive all graph/query projections
   from journal rows and result-slot bindings. No generic lifecycle edge table
   has independent truth or identity.
2. **ACCEPT - mandatory operation anchors.** T1 has mandatory result slot
   `occurrence`; T2 has mandatory result slot `interpretation`; control and
   context operations likewise have fixed header slots. Sibling records inherit
   the producing operation and resolve local result-slot refs. Callers cannot
   choose arbitrary anchors.
3. **ACCEPT - one immutable FSM source.** Replace mutable exported maps and
   production spec injection with read-only lookup/iteration over one static
   phase law. Generated phase metadata derives transitions from it. The two
   missing UAT back edges are adopted in the canonical law.
4. **ACCEPT - separate context policy.** Remove context directives from pure
   occurrence interpretation. A separate `ContextPolicy` receives exact
   committed state, recipient, prior disclosure, acknowledgement, and bounds.
5. **ACCEPT - semantic envelope.** Define one bounded versioned envelope with
   typed record kind, schema ref, codec, parent refs, exact interpretation
   identity, and body. Unknown schemas remain queryable as opaque bounded
   records but cannot drive interpretation, control, or context.
6. **ACCEPT - M1 bounded query.** M1 includes a production bounded occurrence
   read, so the first milestone is a user-visible vertical rather than a
   write-only substrate.
7. **ACCEPT - internal expected state.** Authority services read current facts
   and derive `ConditionCurrentFact`; callers do not supply a public storage
   revision/expected JournalID.
8. **ACCEPT - build versus execution identity.** Stable build identity is
   separate from execution metadata such as DBOS recovery cohort/executor.
9. **ACCEPT - budgets.** Freeze per-invocation bytes, fields, outputs, effects,
   context, query, deadline, and default metadata-retention budgets.

### Axis C mini - aura-plugins-sbjw0 - VOTE: REVISE

1. **ACCEPT - T1 actor/authority.** Register fixed ordinal-1
   `pasture-system/lifecycle-ingress`, use the existing persisted bootstrap
   authority only through a narrow unscoped-evidence appender, and require the
   control service to reject the ingress actor and require independent
   capability/current-state conditions. No per-hook actor expansion is needed.
2. **ACCEPT - T2/enrichment/context APIs.** Define pure interpretation, bounded
   correlation snapshot/enrichment, journal writer, separate context policy,
   context transport, and fixed result-slot mapping. M2 cannot mutate context or
   control.
3. **ACCEPT - hostcontract/codegen wiring.** Generate an allowed-package
   registration manifest from the private hostcontract source and make codegen
   consume only that mechanical manifest. Add compile boundary and clean
   regeneration tests.
4. **MODIFY - implementation decomposition.** The replacement proposal defines
   exact P0/P1 vertical slices, file ownership, integration gates, and every
   prototype disposition now. Per protocol, the supervisor creates Beads
   L1/L2/L3 leaf tasks only after review/UAT/ratification; the architect does not
   prematurely create implementation leaves for an unaccepted plan.
5. **ACCEPT - historical codebook policy.** Old definitions and decoders remain
   resolvable for on-disk history; retirement never rewrites history and no
   implicit latest is allowed.
6. **ACCEPT - typed native event.** Known ingress uses a contract-bound typed
   event ordinal; an unknown bounded token exists only in parse-issue evidence.
7. **ACCEPT - one 30-hook source.** The private hostcontract owns the production
   descriptor; generated registration/audit artifacts derive from it. The
   authentic fixture manifest remains an independent oracle, not a third source.
8. **ACCEPT - runtime budgets.** Name host deadline, SQLite work/effect fanout,
   per-record storage, raw-content default, and bounded query budgets.
9. **ACCEPT - untracked-file disposition.** All six files are explicitly
   quarantined as superseded prototypes and assigned to the receipt slice for
   rewrite or deletion; none may be committed as-is.
10. **ACCEPT - minimal public contracts.** Freeze only identifiers, envelopes,
    service inputs/results, and bounded reader interfaces needed by M1/M2;
    projection/storage DTOs remain private.
11. **ACCEPT - injected clock.** Receipt and disclosure services require clocks;
    no `time.Now` fallback below process composition.
12. **ACCEPT - defensive copies.** Every public collection is opaque or copied
    on construction and return.
13. **ACCEPT - neutral disposition.** Use one neutral/proceed disposition until
    a pinned host contract and response UAT establish another distinction;
    remove the unsupported Proceed/Continue split.

### Result

All five REVISE votes remain historical `REVISE`; the Axis B general `ACCEPT`
remains `ACCEPT`. Closing review tasks as completed reviews will not transfer
consensus to the replacement proposal. The open Plan UAT remains a later gate,
and no implementation or ratification follows from this disposition.
