| `internal/engine/{control,workflow,projection,activities}.go` and direct transition audit writers | S8 | route through journal-backed control; projections/operational evidence only |

## 18. Open Plan UAT decisions

No option below is selected here. The open UAT records the final choice and
updates the URD before ratification and slicing.

### 18.1 Retention mode

- Metadata only: lowest privacy/operations cost, but unavailable content remains
  explicitly unresolved.
- Encrypted local payload: richer local reconstruction, but requires key,
  deletion, rotation, tombstone, and no-resurrection guarantees.
- External content-addressed payload: durable/shared evidence, but adds store,
  credential, availability, deletion, and privacy obligations.

### 18.2 First activated high-value hooks

UAT receives the current activation readiness report and may select only events
whose authentic exact-version fixture and production path already pass. Candidate
value groupings are session spine, human-signal ingress, tool/artifact lineage,
or multi-agent orchestration. No grouping overrides per-event proof, and this
proposal does not preselect an event.

This choice is also the shared-file write throttle described in 3.2 and 3.3, so
the UAT must weigh two properties per candidate event and not only its evidence
value:

- Fanout: session- and turn-scoped events (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`)
  produce far fewer deliveries than per-tool-call events (`PreToolUse`,
  `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`), which fire on every tool call and scale
  with subagent count.
- Blocking profile: a gate event appends inside a window the host is holding
  open, so its contention competes directly with engine signal delivery, whereas
  an observational event does not.

Enabling any blocking per-tool-call event additionally requires
`aura-plugins-cvlu6` to have resolved the start-signal deadline question.

### 18.3 Context delivery and acknowledgement

Delivery alternatives are generated start/compaction material, dynamic
per-contract host response, or explicit `pasture epoch context` pull.
Acknowledgement alternatives are positive host evidence, explicit agent receipt,
or unavailable acknowledgement (record delivery/unknown only). UAT selects one
compatible pair and its failure/retry semantics.

### 18.4 Future verdict and process-health encoding

Alternatives are a typed host-native verdict separated from process health,
exact native exit/status semantics where the pinned contract proves them, or
continued neutral-only behavior. No deny/ask/defer value becomes reachable until
this UAT and exact response fixture pass.

### 18.5 Artifact enrichment depth and storage

Alternatives are commit/path metadata only, encrypted local diff/snapshot, or
external content-addressed evidence. This decision is orthogonal to occurrence
identity and must be compatible with the selected retention mode. Missing depth
never promotes an observation beyond `ObservedPath`.

text:
PROPOSAL-8 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION REVISION 2 - 3/3 (Sections 19-21 and Appendix A)

## 19. Validation checklist

- [ ] Corrected Claude 2.1.210 audit remains exactly 30 events in pinned order.
- [ ] Hostcontract is the sole production event/name/field/identity/behavior source.
- [ ] Enabled and Withheld are disjoint, complete, typed, and independently proved.
- [ ] At least one UAT-selected fixture-ready event can deliver M1 without all 30.
- [ ] Every separate delivery has a fresh operation ID and occurrence JournalID.
- [ ] No lifecycle/public symbol exposes replay, dedup, repeat count, or payload occurrence identity.
- [ ] `OccurrenceRecord` is the only public post-T1 occurrence type and is deeply immutable.
- [ ] Raw JSON is confined to private ingress/retention code.
- [ ] T2 defines every input/output, exact definition, operation, clock, effect, and slot.
- [ ] Enrichment snapshots are immutable, snapshot-bound, and bounded.
- [ ] Missing/contradictory enrichment is typed unresolved evidence.
- [ ] Context projection is pure and plan/attempt/result facts correlate exactly.
- [ ] Disclosure current state rebuilds identically from immutable journal history.
- [ ] Definitions resolve by immutable JournalID; retirement never erases history.
- [ ] Transaction time is checked after SQLite lock acquisition and exact replay.
- [ ] Capability Bound->Consumed, expiry, and phase CAS share one Apply.
- [ ] Readers define concrete typed filters/pages/cursors/truncation/errors for every record family.
- [ ] Production tests read only public bounded APIs.
- [ ] Selected retention matrix passes end to end, including tombstone/no-resurrection behavior.
- [ ] Positive human-to-code lineage passes forward and reverse production queries.
- [ ] One immutable FSM and one journal-backed control writer remain.
- [ ] Every M1-M6 file, generated artifact, migration, projection, test, and upstream extension has one owner.
- [ ] All six untracked and all committed prototype paths are rewritten/deleted by their named owner.
- [ ] T1 is exactly one write transaction per delivery on the shared file, with no second per-delivery projection, audit, or activation write.
- [ ] Hook ingress uses the 1-second caller lock deadline, never a fixed sub-100 ms retry loop, and measured p99 T1 lock-hold is <= 5 ms at the stated 48-writer ceiling.
- [ ] `TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad` proves the 2-second start-signal deadline either holds under representative hook load or fails honestly and diagnosably, with all receipts still readable.
- [ ] No blocking per-tool-call event is Enabled before `aura-plugins-cvlu6` resolves the start-signal deadline question.
- [ ] All Go tests run with `-race`; static/build/Nix/generation/diff gates pass before implementation commits.

## 20. BDD acceptance criteria

- **Given** two byte-identical host CLI invocations, **when** an Enabled
  registration receives both, **then** it mints two operation IDs and returns two
  distinct occurrence JournalIDs in database order, **and should not** expose or
  infer replay, deduplication, a repeat count, a time window, or payload identity.
- **Given** one internal T1 Apply retry, **when** the same operation ID and exact
  canonical input is retried, **then** Provenance returns the original journal
  result, **and should not** convert that storage property into host-delivery
  semantics.
- **Given** only one authentic event fixture is ready, **when** activation is
  generated, **then** that event may be Enabled and queryable while the other 29
  are visibly Withheld with typed reasons, **and should not** claim full-catalogue
  support or register an unproved event.
- **Given** a registered malformed/duplicate/invalid/truncated/over-limit
  delivery, **when** trusted contract/event coordinates exist, **then** T1 records
  one bounded `OccurrenceRecord` and later planes remain empty, **and should not**
  drop the receipt, retain forbidden bytes, or guess semantics.
- **Given** T2 fails after T1, **when** the occurrence is read, **then** the
  receipt remains visible and eligible for later exact interpretation, **and
  should not** roll back with enrichment.
- **Given** one occurrence and two exact codebook/interpreter/build definitions,
  **when** both are interpreted, **then** both immutable batches and all outputs
  resolve their exact definition JournalIDs, **and should not** overwrite history
  or select latest implicitly.
- **Given** unavailable or contradictory capture/enrichment, **when** T2 runs,
  **then** it emits a typed unresolved fact with typed basis, **and should not**
  assert a human, actor, artifact, commit, causality, delivery, or authority fact.
- **Given** a path-only artifact signal, **when** lineage is queried, **then** it
  returns only `ObservedPath` plus the causal gap, **and should not** invent bytes,
  diff, commit, actor, or human motivation.
- **Given** the positive M3 production fixture, **when** forward and reverse
  readers run, **then** the same explicit human-signal/agent/tool/VCS/worktree/
  artifact/commit chain is returned within bounds, **and should not** use direct
  SQL, test exports, or timestamp proximity.
- **Given** one committed state and two context policy versions, **when** each
  plans disclosure, **then** two immutable plan histories resolve their exact
  policy/build definitions and later attempts/results cite the right plan, **and
  should not** mutate FSM state or prior disclosure facts.
- **Given** a delivery attempt whose host acknowledgement is unavailable, **when**
  the result is recorded, **then** history remains delivered/unknown according to
  the selected acknowledgement mode, **and should not** infer acknowledgement.
- **Given** candidate-only, stale, unauthorized, wrong-recipient, or unknown-
  definition context input, **when** planning is attempted, **then** no disclosure
  or FSM state changes, **and should not** let candidate state drive context.
- **Given** a fresh capability operation queued before expiry but admitted after
  expiry, **when** it acquires SQLite write ownership, **then** transaction time
  returns typed expiry and zero partial writes, **and should not** consume the
  capability or advance phase based on a pre-Apply clock check.
- **Given** an already committed capability operation after expiry, **when** its
  exact operation ID/input is retried, **then** exact replay returns the original
  result before current/deadline checks, **and should not** create a second commit.
- **Given** two processes race one capability or one current phase, **when** T3
  commits, **then** one wins and every loser has a typed current/expired/consumed
  result with zero semantic writes, **and should not** mutate context or a direct
  phase projection.
- **Given** Claude 2.1.210 `ElicitationResult`, **when** only host request/server
  strings correlate it, **then** it remains evidence/candidate, **and should not**
  become a registered-human decision or normative transition.
- **Given** each retention option, **when** its parameterized canary/deletion/
  replay matrix runs, **then** only policy-permitted content behavior occurs and
  occurrence/causal metadata remains, **and should not** leak or resurrect raw
  content.
- **Given** a cursor from another query, a future/stale/tampered cursor, zero or
  oversized page, or oversized lineage bounds, **when** a public reader runs,
  **then** it returns the exact typed error before SQL, **and should not** silently
  restart, skip, duplicate, or run an unbounded traversal.
- **Given** lifecycle/phase/lineage/disclosure projection deletion, **when** the
  journal replays, **then** public readers return identical canonical history and
  current state, **and should not** depend on independent projection IDs.
- **Given** representative hook-ingress write load at the stated ceiling on one
  shared `pasture.db`, **when** a slice waits for its `start_slice` signal,
  **then** the slice either starts within the 2-second deadline or fails with the
  exact "enqueued but never started" error while every receipt committed in that
  window stays readable, **and should not** fabricate slice success, drop a
  receipt, exceed one write transaction per delivery, or retry the lock on a
  fixed sub-100 ms interval.
- **Given** a clean generation run, **when** a second host descriptor table,
  replay symbol, semantic generated branch, env/argv operation selector, or
  generic exit-to-deny mapping is introduced, **then** a static/generation test
  fails, **and should not** require a broad custom taint analyzer.

## 21. Tradeoffs, deferrals, and exit state

| Decision | Benefit | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| One Provenance journal and one FSM | No split-brain graph, phase, context, or identity truth | Services use explicit operations and bounded reads |
| Append every delivery | No silent undercount | Host retries remain visible for later analysis |
| Event-granular activation | Useful verified value arrives early without false claims | Registration/support output changes as proof becomes available |
| One canonical occurrence | No conversion drift after T1 | Private ingress capture cannot be reused as a public model |
| Immutable definition JournalIDs | Historical semantic meaning is resolvable | Activation/retirement and old decoders must be retained |
| Separate T1/T2/context/T3 operations | Receipt and honest external-side-effect gaps survive later failures | Users can observe partial processing |
| Minimal transaction-time condition | Correct expiry at lock admission without a predicate language | Requires a reviewed upstream Provenance release before M6 |
| Concrete snapshot readers | Bounded stable black-box validation | Callers paginate and handle typed cursor errors |
| UAT-parameterized retention | No privacy policy is silently chosen | Activation waits for the selected mode's full matrix |
| One write transaction per delivery on the shared file, with activation as the throttle | Keeps hook ingress from starving the engine's 2-second start-signal deadline without adding a batching layer or a new writer daemon | Caps how many high-fanout blocking events can be Enabled at once, and makes the budget a measured gate rather than an assumption |

Deferred without loss of M1-M6 integrity: runtime-authored codebook language,
probabilistic causal inference, cross-machine total order, generic fourth
harness, unsupported Claude 2.1.210 human authority, and any deliberate native
deny before its focused UAT.

Deliberately stated but not solved here: the engine's 2-second start-signal
deadline. Sections 3.2 through 3.4 fix the write budget hook ingress must meet,
name the measured coupling, and require the load case that proves the deadline
either holds or fails honestly. Whether 2 seconds itself remains defensible once
hook writes share the file, and whether it should become configurable,
budget-derived, or replaced by a readiness handshake, belongs to
`aura-plugins-cvlu6`. Changing that deadline inside this proposal would be
editing another subsystem's contract from the outside.

The next valid action is a fresh independent mirrored review wave coordinated
outside this proposal task. If that wave accepts, the still-open Plan UAT must
resolve Section 18 before ratification. The obsolete IMPL_PLAN remains blocked
by this proposal and must be replaced by the supervisor after those gates. No
implementation, reviewer launch, ratification, commit, or push follows from
creating PROPOSAL-8.

## Appendix A: PROPOSAL-7 mirrored review disposition summary

The complete rationale is PROPOSAL-7 comment 6614. This appendix preserves the
per-review mapping in the replacement proposal.

text:
Routed into the architecture work as requested. PROPOSAL-8 (aura-plugins-4ah84) now carries this coupling as load-bearing design content, not colour:

- Description sections 3.2-3.4 state that T1 evidence append shares one pasture.db with the DBOS notification store, the audit tables, Provenance, and the engine projection (internal/engine/engine.go:211,227-233 hands dbconn.OpenSharedDB to dbos.Config.SqliteSystemDB), and that hook write fanout can delay signal delivery past the 2s window at internal/engine/slice.go:65.
- It names the budget inversion explicitly: busy_timeout=5000 exceeds the 2s deadline, so a contended append can succeed inside the storage contract having consumed the entire engine window.
- Combined write budget for engine + audit + hook ingress: T1 is exactly one write transaction per delivery (no second projection/audit/activation write); T2 adds exactly one more; assumed ceiling is 48 concurrent writers (DefaultSliceQueueConcurrency=8 slices x an assumed 4 agents/subagents, plus daemon/CLI); derived requirement is measured p99 T1 lock-hold <= 5 ms, giving ~240 ms worst-case serialized queueing, under 13% of the 2s deadline; hook ingress uses a 1s caller lock deadline and no fixed sub-100 ms retry loop.
- Section 3.3 weighs five contention-control options without picking: bounded per-process batching, single-writer ingress, existing WAL/busy_timeout tuning, deferring T1 off the blocking path, and staging activation. It records one correction: PostToolUse before PreToolUse does not materially reduce delivery count (both fire per tool call); it changes the blocking profile. The genuinely fanout-reducing lever is session/turn-scoped events over per-tool-call events.
- Validation case added as section 15.1 item 8 and section 3.4: TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad, owned exclusively by S1-RECEIPT in new internal/engine/shared_write_budget_test.go. author: David Huu Pham
text:
INDEPENDENT AXIS B — TEST QUALITY / VALIDATABILITY

VOTE: REVISE

## BLOCKER 1 — The shared-SQLite load test accepts the regression it must prevent

PROPOSAL-8 §3.2 derives the 5 ms T1 lock-hold budget to keep hook ingress from starving the engine 2-second start_slice window. Sections 3.4 and 15.1 item 8 make TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad the only test for that production characteristic. Its first assertion explicitly accepts either a timely start OR an honest timeout. The second assertion proves durability only: a slow, contending implementation can time out every slice yet retain every receipt. The third assertion is the only possible regression signal, but the proposal does not define the sample size or quantile calculation, a measurement of lock-acquisition wait or end-to-end T1 completion, or the production-path mechanism that counts transaction boundaries. Lock hold alone does not bound queueing; a 5-second busy timeout can consume the entire 2-second engine window. The test can pass while the user-visible slice failure remains reproducible. Current timeout behavior is internal/engine/slice.go:61-106.

Fix: split this into TestSliceStartDeadlineHoldsUnderHookWriteLoad, which launches the stated 48 concurrent hook deliveries as distinct built-binary child processes or independently opened handles on one file behind a barrier and requires timely start for every fixed run; and a deterministic injected-delay test that requires the exact honest timeout, failed hook, projection state, and no fabricated success. Keep public-reader receipt checks as a distinct durability assertion. Define a fixed sample count and percentile algorithm, and measure attempted BEGIN IMMEDIATE through commit, including admission wait, plus actual transaction count in the real receipt path. The load test must fail on any deadline miss, second per-delivery transaction, p99 violation, or ingress deadline/retry violation.

## BLOCKER 2 — Capability scope enforcement is not executable through the stated API/test contract

Section 10.2 defines CapabilityScope over operation, epoch, actor, role, assignment, source JournalIDs, native bindings, and expiry, but exposes only EpochControlService.CommitCandidate; it does not define issuance, binding, revocation operations or a typed scope-mismatch result. Section 15.1 item 6 merely says production services issue and bind, while section 15.2 calls for an undifferentiated issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume matrix. A green implementation could check only consumed or revoked state and omit a scope axis. It also leaves changed-input conflict and fresh-operation stale or consumed cases unpaired with an observable mismatch outcome.

Fix: add a production capability service/input/result contract and a typed scope-mismatch error or result. Require a public-service matrix that mutates exactly one valid scope axis at a time: operation, epoch, actor, role, assignment, source, and native binding. Include issuance, binding, expiry, revocation, two-consumer single-use race, two-capability phase race, exact retry before current-state checks, same-operation changed-input conflict, and fresh operation after revoked, consumed, or expired state. Each loser needs before/after public-reader snapshots proving zero partial journal, capability, phase, decision, context, and projection writes. Races need separate processes or independently opened handles on one file.

## BLOCKER 3 — Version evolution omits dirty and missing build honesty

Section 15.2 requires two codebooks, interpreters, builds, and exact definition JournalIDs, but has no dirty-source, missing-build-identity, or same VCS revision/different-build test. Section 6 models DefinitionEpochImplementation as a generic definition but does not define the dirty or missing outcome or make it an M2 assertion. A green suite could claim an exact build envelope when the build is absent or derived from dirty source, defeating historical interpretation.

Fix: define build-identity validity and a typed unresolved or failure outcome. Add production-reader fixtures for one occurrence interpreted by two codebook/interpreter/build identities without overwrite; same VCS revision with different build content identities; dirty source; and missing or unknown build identity. Assert the exact immutable envelope on every dependent record family, and assert that dirty or missing input remains unresolved and cannot create context or control effects.

## IMPORTANT

1. Section 12.1 is a strong invalid-delivery contract, but section 15.1 does not name one file-backed built-process table proving all rows. TestEnabledClaudeEventToOccurrenceReader proves byte-identical append, but does not explicitly cover semantically-identical different-byte delivery, malformed JSON, unknown event, duplicate key, truncation, invalid UTF-8, over-limit, or store failure against a pre-seeded file. Add a table-driven production test using generated registration, built binaries, and public readers only. Assert one distinct T1 record and exact capture disposition/no later effects where required; untrusted or unregistered input and store failure must assert no false receipt without SQL. This is essential invariant coverage, not deferred host breadth. The obsolete opposite tests are at internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder_test.go:104-134, internal/lifecycle/lower_test.go:335-377, and cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:231-255.

2. Section 15.3 requires compile/dependency and mutation guards, but omits the requested mutation making a generated artifact parse payload bytes. It names environment or argument operation selection, semantic branching, and deny mapping, so a generated parser could be introduced without an explicitly required failure. Add compile-fail/dependency fixtures plus generated-artifact source or subprocess mutations for payload parsing, environment-selected operation, semantic branch, and generic-error-to-deny. This replaces the current environment-selected Python path at internal/codegen/claude_hooks_test.go:114-265.

text:
VOTE: REVISE — independent Axis B (test quality and validatability), general half of the mirrored pair, on PROPOSAL-8 aura-plugins-4ah84.

Four blockers, all in Section 15:

B1 — TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad (§15.1 item 8, §3.4) cannot measure its own budget at the milestone that gates on it. Assertion 1 is NOT vacuous (each disjunct is conjunctive; a generic error, panic, fabricated success, or missing SliceFailed fails it) but it is not a budget assertion. Assertion 2 detects receipt loss, not budget. Assertion 3 is the only budget assertion and its p99 write-lock-hold half is not implementable by its owner at M1: T1 appends through Journal.Apply, and Pasture does not own that connection — internal/tasks/open_unified.go:199 calls provenance.OpenSQLite(dbPath), with the in-tree comment at :194-198 confirming provenance manages its own *sql.DB. Instrumenting lock hold needs an upstream change, and §17.1/§17.3/§17.4 schedule all upstream Provenance work in S7 at M6, while §16 makes the measurement an M1 gate owned by S1. Second defect: §15.3 mandates -race for all Go tests, so a 5 ms absolute wall-clock p99 is either trivially green or permanently red. Third: the p99 clause is absent from the design-field BDD then/should_not entirely. The transaction-count half IS measurable and should be kept.

B2 — §15 is a compression of PROPOSAL-7 §14 that dropped seven specific cases, while Appendix A records aura-plugins-xwiuk as 'ACCEPT unchanged'. Lost: 13 named scope-mismatch axes; the three distinct revocation timings; already-consumed; fresh-OperationID stale/revoked/consumed; same-VCS/different-build-digest, dirty source, and missing build identity; 'generated code cannot parse semantics'; and the fixture anti-normalization rule. §15.2's cursor coverage did improve — the compression was not uniformly lossy, but it was lossy in exactly the authority and version matrices where a missing case means forged authority or a false clean-provenance claim.

B3 — The URD FIX-NOW corpus idiom (typed YAML Case/Corpus with must-pass/must-fail, provenance and mutation metadata, non-vacuity/coverage guards, bounded combinatorial expansion, named typed mutation operators) is absent from §15. No 'must-pass', 'mutation operator', 'combinatorial', or 'coverage guard' appears anywhere; 'non-vacuity' appears only as an Appendix A label. Meanwhile §12.1, §13, §14, and §15.2 are four large matrices left as prose with no named test. Non-vacuity guards are precisely the mechanism that catches all three self-deceiving tests this project already paid for.

B4 — 'Production tests read only public bounded readers' is asserted in §11.2, §15.1 items 1/3/4/5/6, §19 line 22, design checklist 18, and the §20 BDD, and guarded nowhere. §15.3 gives the replay rule a focused source guard and the host-descriptor rule a go/ast plus go list guard; the reader rule gets prose. The violation is already live and reads as ordinary test code at cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:132-195 (sql.Open plus raw SELECT over audit_events, activities, context_edges). One more rule in the existing go/ast pass closes it.

Also required in the same revision: A1 §14 and §16 disagree on when the retention matrix gates (M1 Enables payload-bearing events and §6.2 makes RetentionPolicyDefinitionRef mandatory at T1, so retention gates M1, not M4); A2 §15.1 item 4 does not name the M3-available production path that issues the human signal; A3 §12.1's seven-row matrix has no named owner.

CLOSED with evidence: prior aura-plugins-0gvfe blockers 1-3 and importants 1-2 — replay removed rather than renamed plus a static guard and named prototype dispositions; two disjoint manifests with an independently-authored 30-event oracle that does not iterate the production hostcontract; the bounded reader frozen to field level across all ten record families including definitions, capabilities, and commits; all three retention modes with full deletion/tombstone/no-resurrection matrices; and a named forward-and-reverse human-to-code proof with its two negatives.

Explicitly NOT requesting: a semantically-identical-different-byte delivery case (byte-identical strictly dominates it for dedup detection), further cursor/lineage matrix expansion, or tightening the all-30 corpus beyond the catalogue-completeness claim. That scoping is correct.

Full review with citations and concrete fixes is in this task description.

text:
VOTE: REVISE — Axis B test quality / validatability, general half of the mirrored pair. Review task: aura-plugins-237wx.

Four blockers, all in Section 15.

B1 §15.1 item 8 / §3.4 — the new load test cannot measure its own budget at the milestone that gates on it. Assertion 1 is not vacuous (each disjunct is conjunctive, so a generic error, panic, fabricated success, or missing SliceFailed fails it), but it is not a budget assertion. Assertion 2 detects receipt loss, not budget. Assertion 3's p99 write-lock-hold half is not implementable by S1 at M1: T1 appends through Journal.Apply and Pasture does not own that connection — internal/tasks/open_unified.go:199 calls provenance.OpenSQLite(dbPath) and the in-tree comment at :194-198 says provenance manages its own *sql.DB. Lock-hold instrumentation therefore needs an upstream change, which §17.1/§17.3/§17.4 place in S7 at M6, while §16 makes the measurement an M1 gate. Separately, §15.3's blanket -race mandate makes a 5 ms absolute wall-clock p99 either trivially green or permanently red, and the p99 clause is missing from the design-field BDD entirely. Suggested fix: assert hold as p99 <= 5 ms in an uncontended single-writer run (no wait to subtract, measurable in S1 today), assert contention as contended p99 <= K x uncontended p99 measured in the same run and same race mode (self-calibrating, K ~ 48 from §3.2), keep the transaction-count assertion as an absolute with a named counting mechanism, add the p99 to the BDD, and state sample size and flake policy. Also resolve the ownership loop: §3.4 needs S2's generated registration for an S1-owned L2 test that §17.4 IP-2 orders after S1.

B2 §15 vs PROPOSAL-7 §14 — the compression dropped seven specific cases while Appendix A records aura-plugins-xwiuk as 'ACCEPT unchanged'. Lost: the 13 named scope-mismatch axes; revoke-before-bind / revoke-before-commit / revoke-racing-commit as three distinct races; already-consumed; fresh-OperationID stale/revoked/consumed; same-VCS-different-build-digest, dirty source, and missing build identity; 'generated code cannot parse semantics'; and the rule keeping raw bytes in separate files so duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, ordering, and truncation are not normalized. §15.2's cursor coverage genuinely improved, so this is not a blanket regression — but the losses are concentrated in the authority and version matrices, where a missing case means forged authority or a false clean-provenance claim. Fix: restore the seven, and either mark that disposition MODIFY or make 'unchanged' true. Per-axis scope mismatch is the one I would not compress: 'issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume matrix' reads as five cases, not twenty.

B3 URD FIX-NOW absent — the corpus idiom the user required for 'current and subsequent epoch acceptance tests' (typed YAML Case/Corpus with must-pass/must-fail, provenance and mutation metadata, non-vacuity/coverage guards, bounded combinatorial expansion, named typed mutation operators) appears nowhere in §15. §12.1, §13, §14, and §15.2 are four large matrices left as prose with no named test attached, and §17.3 S1 L2 reduces §12.1's seven rows to 'malformed T1'. Non-vacuity guards are exactly the mechanism that catches the three self-deceiving tests this project already paid for. Fix: bind the matrices to corpora, require a per-corpus non-vacuity guard, and name the mutation operators for §15.3's guards instead of 'subprocess mutation' in prose. If it is being deferred, say so as an explicit deferral against the URD and route it to §18.

B4 unguarded reader rule — 'production tests read only public bounded readers' is asserted in §11.2, §15.1 items 1/3/4/5/6, §19 line 22, design checklist 18, and the §20 BDD, and enforced nowhere. §15.3 gives the replay rule a focused source guard and the host-descriptor rule a go/ast plus go list guard; this one gets prose. The violation is live and looks like ordinary test code at cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:132-195. Fix: one more rule in the existing go/ast pass over the named production-path test files (no database/sql import, no projection internals, no SQL literals), proven to bite, with a single whitelisted helper for the §15.2 zero-write delta snapshots — which the plan should also say which side of the line they are on.

A2 §15.1 item 4 requires a 'Pasture-issued human signal' but names no M3-available production path that issues one, so the worker will seed it in the test and the M3 gate will pass anyway. A3 §12.1 has no named test owner.

Credit where due, with evidence in the review: replay is removed rather than renamed and backed by a static guard plus named prototype dispositions in §17.5; §5.2's two-manifest split with an independently-authored oracle that does not iterate the production hostcontract is the correct fix for the self-derivation defect; §11.1-§11.2 freeze the reader to field level across all ten families including the three that were missing; §14 specifies all three retention matrices in full; §15.1 item 4 is a real named lineage proof, not a generic traversal. Not requesting: a semantically-identical-different-byte case (byte-identical strictly dominates for dedup detection), further cursor/lineage expansion, or tightening the all-30 corpus past the catalogue claim. That scoping is right.

Items 10, 12 and 13 also verified sound: the 48x5ms=240ms arithmetic is right, per-event activation cannot silently advertise unverified hooks, and the malformed matrix gives every invalid class a distinct typed disposition with no interpretation/control/context fact.

ONE BLOCKER, in the freshly written resource section. Sections 3.1, 3.2 point 4, 15.2, 16 M1, 17.3 and 19 require hook ingress to pass a 1-second SQLite lock-acquisition deadline, but no such primitive exists on the pinned Provenance API and no slice adds it. journal_api.go:288 Apply takes no context.Context; internal/sqlite/operations.go:450 binds the Apply scope with context.Background(), so limitTransactionBusyTimeout (internal/sqlite/db.go:597-604) is inert on that path; upstream states at operations.go:459-461 that the 5s busy_timeout retries lock contention; busyTimeoutMS=5000 is private (db.go:39) and appended last by withSQLiteQuery (db.go:440-442) so a caller DSN cannot lower it; the only OpenSQLite option is WithModelRegistry (options.go:6-27) and Tracker exposes no sql handle; and the ctx-carrying DBOSAdapter.Apply documents (dbos_adapter.go:141-146) that the caller context controls pre/post work only. Consequence: hook ingress silently falls back to section 3.3 option C, which the proposal itself disqualifies as masking precisely the observed failure, so an M1 essential gate is unsatisfiable and the 3.2-3.4 mitigation is partly vacuous. Compare the transaction-time condition, which is handled correctly with named files, a dedicated S7 slice and IP-7; the caller deadline has the same upstream dependency but is an M1 gate while S7 is an M6 prerequisite. Fix: split S7 into an M1 caller-deadline extension (ApplyContext or an ApplyOption threading the caller ctx into bindScope, with a new IP gating S1 L3) plus the unchanged M6 time condition, or drop the 1-second claim and re-derive the budget on the levers actually available. Also fix two smaller feasibility gaps in the one-transaction-per-delivery rule: index rows cannot be written inside the owning Apply on the pinned API (WithModelRegistry seeds ml_models only), so state that M1 derives the projection by replay; and internal/tasks/system_identity.go:87-89 calls ActivatePastureSystem on the already-persisted path, which takes an unconditional BEGIN IMMEDIATE at actor_namespace.go:27-33, yet that file has no owner in 17.1 despite the section 19 claim that every M1-M6 file has one. No severity tree (plan review).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
## UAT DECISION — shared-SQLite write budget enforceability

**Context shown to user:** PROPOSAL-8 review wave returned 5 REVISE / 1 ACCEPT. Every remaining blocker traced to one root cause: the M1 resource gates require upstream capabilities scheduled at M6 or absent from the pinned Provenance API. Specifically the 1-second ingress lock deadline cannot exist, because Journal.Apply takes no context.Context and limitTransactionBusyTimeout is inert without a deadline.

**Question asked:** how much effort to make the write budget enforceable, given three options:
  A - deadline only: upstream ApplyContext threading ctx into bindScope, plus a relative-bound test. ~1 day. Bounds the wait; does not prove the 240ms figure.
  B - A plus off-path spool: hooks append to a spool, a drainer moves it to the journal, hooks never take the SQLite write lock. 1-2 weeks. Deadline protected by construction.
  C - cross-process admission control with bounded permits and priority. Weeks. Proves the 48 ceiling.

**Architect recommendation given:** A now, B later only if measurement demands it, not C. Reasons: every cross-process mechanism for C is bad here (flock leaks permits on crash; a daemon socket makes hooks FAIL when the daemon is down, worse than slow; SQLite-as-semaphore is self-defeating); the 5ms p99 assumption is 5-50x pessimistic for a WAL insert so the gap is about proving the budget rather than the risk being large; and A makes B measurable.

**User response (VERBATIM):** "Do A."

**Disposition: FIX-NOW.**

**Grounding verified before dispatch:**
  - provenance internal/sqlite/db.go:604 limitTransactionBusyTimeout already caps the connection-local busy_timeout to the caller's remaining deadline, and returns a no-op when the ctx carries none.
  - It is already wired into the transaction-begin path at db.go:641.
  - bindScope(ctx, ...) already threads a context.
  - internal/sqlite/governed_allocation.go:431 already passes a real ctx, so the pattern is proven in this package. Apply is simply not one of the callers - comments.go, tasks.go and the Apply path still pass context.Background().

This makes the upstream change an extension of an existing proven pattern rather than new design.

**Consequences for the plan:**
  - The budget becomes an honest SLO with a bounded, fast, typed failure instead of an unbounded stall behind a 5s busy_timeout.
  - The load test adopts the relative-bound form (contended p99 <= K x uncontended p99, same run, same race mode) so it is immune to CPU contention and race-detector overhead. Absolute 5ms wall-clock under mandatory -race is rejected as reproducing the flakiness just fixed.
  - S7 does NOT need splitting for this: the deadline lands upstream now, ahead of any Pasture slice, rather than at M6.
  - Option B remains available and is explicitly NOT chosen. Revisit only if measurement shows real contention.
  - Option C is rejected on design grounds, not cost.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
ARCHITECT DISPOSITION — fix accepted at 02bebf4, with one correction to how it was characterised.

The information loss was real and the placement is good: Details sits between Reason and Where, reuses writeAligned so alignment stays consistent, is conditional on Cause != nil, and Error() was updated too. Confirming Unwrap was already correct is useful - it means errors.Is/As always worked and only the human-readable path was lossy. 177 production sites setting a field that was never rendered is a substantial finding.

BUT this was not purely a bug fix, and the report did not say so. It REVERSED a documented, deliberate design decision.

The previous comment read: 'It is NOT surfaced in user-visible output (Report) - that prose must be plain English with no Go symbol names, package qualifiers, or SQL column references.' That is a considered UX stance with a stated rationale, not an oversight. The new comment replaces it with 'it is surfaced in user-visible output, so it must use operator-safe text with no secrets'.

Two consequences that were not assessed:

1. The 177 sites all wrap collaborator errors - err, cause, attachErr, gErr, cErr - originating from SQLite, migrations, DBOS and file I/O. Their text now reaches users: driver strings, SQL fragments, file paths. For a developer-facing CLI that is probably an improvement, since the audience is technical and a driver error is diagnostic. But it is a change in user-visible output at 177 call sites, and it was landed as a bug fix rather than surfaced as a decision.

2. The call sites were COUNTED, not AUDITED. Counting establishes blast radius; it does not establish content. No site was inspected for paths, connection details or tokens before its wrapped text became user-visible.

The deeper objection is consistency. 'Callers must not wrap errors containing secrets' is an obligation imposed retroactively on 177 sites written under the opposite contract, enforced by a comment and nothing else. This epic has now rejected exactly that pattern three times: the BackendView grep that could not detect a same-package violation, the bounded-reader rule asserted five times and guarded zero times, and the mutable-field-in-immutable-record class found in three separate rounds. A rule that depends on every future author reading a doc comment is not an invariant. Applying the same standard here rather than exempting our own change.

Keeping the fix. Filing the enforcement gap separately and raising the contract reversal to the user, since it changes user-visible output and only they can weigh the UX tradeoff the original author was protecting.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Implemented and pushed Provenance commit 0976165224e93175225bad42dcea3807cd578bd9 on feat/governed-allocation-integration.

API/compatibility: added optional exported ContextJournal interface with ApplyContext(context.Context, OperationInput), rather than adding a method to Journal. DB.Apply remains byte-for-byte caller-compatible and delegates through context.Background(), whose lack of a deadline leaves limitTransactionBusyTimeout a no-op. This avoids breaking external Journal implementers and the existing DBOS test doubles. ApplyContext was chosen over an Apply option name because session.go already owns ApplyOption for the distinct Session API. borrowedJournal exposes and delegates ApplyContext when supported, with legacy Apply fallback; DBOSAdapter now forwards its caller context on both journal Apply paths executed in its caller-facing preflight/classification flow.

Implementation: DB.ApplyContext threads ctx through bindScope and the shared prepared-operation transaction path, producing errors.Is(context.DeadlineExceeded)-classifiable, actionable errors that state stage, impact/no commit, and remedy. Assignment transfer deliberately retains no-deadline behavior. Files changed: journal_api.go, dbos_store.go, dbos_adapter.go, internal/sqlite/operations.go, internal/sqlite/assignment_transfer.go, internal/sqlite/apply_context_test.go.

Measured deterministic file-backed WAL contention under -race: deadline-aware 300ms budget returned in 303.14015ms; legacy no-deadline Apply returned in 5.00808547s under busy_timeout=5s. The deadline test asserts <2s and <half busy_timeout, plus >half its requested budget so it cannot pass without actually waiting. It also proves no partial operation, immediate already-expired failure, and successful legacy Apply on the same one-connection contender after lock release (no invisible pending transaction).

Test-bite proof: temporarily changed applyPreparedOperation back to bindScope(context.Background()); the focused test failed after 5.01319151s with its under-2s assertion. Restored context plumbing before commit.

SQLite/WAL finding: WAL permits readers during the held write transaction, but BEGIN IMMEDIATE still serializes all writers. A separate connection holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE is a deterministic contention fixture; no retry race is needed. busy_timeout is connection-local, so deadline capping and restoration must stay on the same pinned connection. A no-deadline caller still waits the full configured timeout.

Checks: go vet ./... passed; go test -race -count=1 ./... passed (root 380.538s, internal/sqlite 93.396s); git diff --check passed. gofmt -l . reports pre-existing formatting in dbos_family_retry_test.go, internal/journal/conflict.go, internal/journal/context.go, internal/journal/operations.go, journal_result_slot_matrix_test.go; all touched files were gofmt-clean and those unrelated files were not changed.

Consumer pin (do not modify Pasture here): github.com/dayvidpham/provenance v0.0.4-0.20260730015136-0976165224e9. Branch push succeeded and is up to date with origin. Blockers: none.

## 4. Axis B — `aura-plugins-0lbsy` (reviewer), VOTE REVISE

| # | Finding | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-r.1 | BLOCKER 1: the load test accepts the regression it must prevent. Fix: split into `TestSliceStartDeadlineHoldsUnderHookWriteLoad` (requires timely start) and a deterministic injected-delay test (requires the exact honest timeout). | **ACCEPT the split, MODIFY the thresholds** | PROPOSAL-9 §3.4 splits availability from honest-failure into two named tests, which is the right decomposition and is not what PROPOSAL-8 had. The thresholds move to the relative form per B-g.2 and the wall-clock availability assertion is quarantined out of the mandatory `-race` wave per B-g.3. |
| B-r.2 | BLOCKER 1 tail: define fixed sample count and percentile algorithm; measure attempted `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` through commit including admission wait; count actual transactions in the real receipt path. | **PARTIAL ACCEPT** | Sample count, percentile algorithm (nearest-rank on a fixed-size sorted sample), and the transaction-count mechanism are all specified in §3.4. Measuring `BEGIN`-through-commit *including admission wait* separately from hold is **not implementable at M1** for the reason B-general traced (`open_unified.go:199`); §3.4 records that limitation explicitly rather than promising it. |
| B-r.3 | BLOCKER 2: capability scope enforcement is not executable — only `CommitCandidate` is exposed; no issuance/binding/revocation operations and no typed scope-mismatch result. A green implementation could check only consumed/revoked and omit a scope axis. | **ACCEPT in full** | PROPOSAL-9 §10.2 adds `Issue`, `Bind`, `Revoke`, typed inputs, `CapabilityScopeMismatch{Capability, Axis}`, and `CapabilityStateError{Capability, Observed, Required}`. §15.2 requires a public-service matrix mutating exactly one of the thirteen `CapabilityScopeAxis` values at a time, plus issuance, binding, expiry, the three revocation timings, already-consumed, two-consumer single-use race, two-capability phase race, exact retry before current-state checks, same-operation changed-input conflict, and fresh operation after stale/revoked/consumed/expired — each loser with before/after public-reader snapshots proving zero partial writes, races in **separate processes**. |
| B-r.4 | IMPORTANT 1: §15.1 does not name one file-backed built-process table proving all §12.1 rows; add a table-driven production test including a semantically-identical-different-byte delivery case. | **PARTIAL ACCEPT** | The table-driven built-process public-reader test is **accepted** as `TestIngressInvalidDeliveryCorpus`. The **semantically-identical-different-byte case is REJECTED**: B-general showed byte-identical strictly dominates it for detecting content-derived dedup, so it buys nothing and costs a fixture. Two reviewers disagreed; B-general's argument is the correct one and this records the ruling. |
| B-r.5 | IMPORTANT 2: §15.3 omits a mutation making a generated artifact parse payload bytes. | **ACCEPT** | Added as `MutateGeneratedPayloadParse`, alongside `MutateEnvSelectedOperation`, `MutateGeneratedSemanticBranch`, and `MutateGenericErrorToDeny`. Each operator must be proven to turn its guard red. |
| B-r.6 | BLOCKER 3: version evolution omits dirty and missing build honesty; a green suite could claim an exact build envelope from a dirty or absent build. | **ACCEPT in full** | PROPOSAL-9 §6.3 adds `BuildIdentityStatus{Exact, DirtySource, Unresolved}` and a new `UnresolvedUnverifiedBuild` reason. Only `BuildIdentityExact` may back an Enabled activation or a normative T3 commit. §15.2 adds public-reader cases for same-revision/different-build-content, dirty source, and missing build identity. |
| B-r.7 | Verified prior findings 1-5, 7 CLOSED. | **PRESERVE** | Unchanged. |

## 5. Axis C — `aura-plugins-oygyo` (general), VOTE **ACCEPT**

The ACCEPT stands and its substance is preserved. It is the one vote in this wave that does
not require a change, and its scoping and steelman are load-bearing inputs to the others.

| # | Finding | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-g.0 | Steelman: append-events-plus-typed-labels satisfies exactly **1 of the 7** queries §1 requires, and that one *is* M1. Complexity is proportional. 172 ownership paths parsed mechanically, zero real cross-slice conflicts. Zero upstream schema change for the causal graph. S8 must not split (IP-8 requires one atomic cutover). Replay removed rather than renamed. | **PRESERVE** | Carried forward verbatim into PROPOSAL-9 Appendix B. The proportionality ruling is not reopened. |
| C-g.1 | R1: collapse `EnrichmentConfidence` and `CausalConfidence` — identical value sets, and §8's no-promotion rule must *compare* them, so one type is simpler and safer. | **ACCEPT** | One `Confidence{Observed, Correlated, Verified}`. The no-promotion rule becomes a direct comparison instead of a hand-written conversion that can be written wrongly. |
| C-g.2 | R2: five reader records carry a bare `JournalID` beside a typed ID; equality stated only for two. | **ACCEPT** | PROPOSAL-9 deletes every redundant bare `JournalID` field and gives each typed ID view a `JournalID()` accessor. No caller maintains an equality invariant. |
| C-g.3 | R3: validate candidate `(From, To)` against `PhaseSpecFor` at emit time so adjacency lives in exactly one place. | **ACCEPT** | §7.2 makes it a constructor rule with a typed `CandidateAdjacencyError`, and §15.4's no-second-table guard is extended to reject a phase-adjacency table outside `pkg/protocol`. This is precisely how a second FSM gets born; it is closed explicitly. |
| C-g.4 | R4: relabel §3.3 — option E is already selected, so "not selected here" understates what the proposal decided. | **ACCEPT, superseded in form** | §3.3 is rewritten around the settled decision: **A chosen**, B available and explicitly not chosen with its revisit trigger, C rejected on design grounds, D rejected, E (activation as throttle) already selected. Only *which events* to Enable remains open, and that is genuinely the user's tradeoff. |
| C-g.5 | R5: type `EvidencePayloadRef.Definition` as `RetentionPolicyDefinitionRef`. | **ACCEPT** | Done in §4.2. |
| C-g.6 | R6: give `DisclosureAttemptID [16]byte` its one-sentence rationale, or an implementer may read it as the application-derived second identity the UAT rejected. | **MODIFY — removed instead** | C-reviewer IMPORTANT 1 is right that it is an unearned third identity: the attempt JournalID plus the operation ID already identify the durable attempt and the exact retry. PROPOSAL-9 removes it and defers any channel nonce (`DeliveryCorrelationToken`) to the UAT-selected adapter, where the need can actually be demonstrated. |
| C-g.7 | R7: `EpochControlService` exposes only `CommitCandidate` while S8 L2 lists an issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume matrix. | **ACCEPT** | Closed by the same change as A-g.8 and B-r.3. |
| C-g.8 | R8: qualify the bare `testdata/**` globs in S3 and S5. | **ACCEPT** | Both become package-scoped paths in §17.1. |
| C-g.9 | R9: put the load test in its own package so it does not inherit `internal/engine/main_test.go`'s shared `TestMain`, hermetic-env setup, and `goleak.Find` — a file S1 does not own. | **ACCEPT** | The test moves to a new S1-owned package `internal/engine/budget/**`. This **removes the §17.1 ownership exception entirely** rather than merely declaring it, and it removes the failure mode where a goroutine leak in S1's harness fails the whole engine package with S1 unable to touch the fixture. |
| C-g.10 | R10: interrogate `InterpreterDefinitionRef` against `EpochImplementationRef`; if one build ever ships exactly one interpreter, the pair should fuse. | **MODIFY — keep separate, record the asymmetry** | §6.2 now states the reason rather than asserting the separation: over-separating costs one JournalID per envelope; under-separating costs unrecoverable ambiguity in an append-only ledger. The two-argument `InterpretationRegistry.Resolve` is the evidence that one build may ship several interpreters. Revisit only if a build is ever proven to ship exactly one. |
| C-g.11 | Declined over-testing: no further cursor/lineage expansion; do not tighten the all-30 corpus past the catalogue claim. | **PRESERVE** | PROPOSAL-9 adds neither. |

Both are right about different halves; see C-r.1. |
| C-g.13 | §14 resource quantification judged proportionate. | **PRESERVE, with one recorded override** | The proportionality ruling stands. I am overriding it **only** on the instrumentation point (B-g.6): B-general traced concretely that `open_unified.go:199` puts true lock-hold instrumentation upstream at M6 while the gate is M1. The override and its reason are recorded in PROPOSAL-9 §3.4. Nothing else in C-general's §14 judgement is disturbed. |

## 6. Axis C — `aura-plugins-u2d51` (reviewer), VOTE REVISE

| # | Finding | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-r.1 | BLOCKER 1: `TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad` is S1 L2 but needs S2 L3 outputs, while IP-2 orders S1 L3 before S2 — an L2/L3 loop. Fix: move the file and its M1 gate ownership to S2. | **ACCEPT the defect, MODIFY the fix** | The loop is real and three reviewers found it (C-reviewer, B-general B1 tail, and C-general's R9 residual). C-general's counter-argument is also right: S1 owns the T1 write budget, so S1 owning its proof is correct, and S8 arrives at M6. Both hold. PROPOSAL-9 keeps **S1 as owner** and moves the **gate**: sequence is `S1 L3 → S2 L3 → shared-file black-box test`, recorded as new integration point **IP-2b**. S1 additionally keeps a receipt-service transaction-budget test that needs no generated artifact and can go green inside S1. Moving ownership to S2 is rejected: it would hand the write budget's proof to a slice that does not own the write. |
| C-r.2 | BLOCKER 2: `DefinitionSnapshot.Status` — a snapshot cannot be both immutable and change Active→Retired. Remove Status; append definition-state facts; fold active/status-filtered reads in JournalID order. | **ACCEPT, and generalized into a standing invariant** | This is the **third instance** of one defect class: `Semantics.Identities` and `ContextDisclosure.State` in earlier rounds, now `DefinitionSnapshot.Status`. Three rounds, three reviewers, one class. PROPOSAL-9 §3.0 states **INV-1**: any type described as an immutable snapshot exposes no mutable field and no lifecycle status; state is expressed as append-only facts with a derived projection that carries `SnapshotJournalID`. §15.4 adds a static guard (`MutateMutableFieldInSnapshot` proves it bites), and §3.0 classifies every record in the proposal as immutable-snapshot, immutable-fact, derived-projection, or build-input. Concretely: `DefinitionSnapshot.Status` is removed, `DefinitionStateFact` is appended, and `DefinitionStateRecord` is derived in JournalID order. Point-fixing stops here. |
| C-r.3 | IMPORTANT 1: disclosure APIs define typed IDs then accept bare `provenance.JournalID`; `DisclosureAttemptID` is an unearned third identity. | **ACCEPT in full** | Typed IDs at every plan/attempt/result boundary with `JournalID()` accessors; the random `[16]byte` attempt identity is removed; any channel nonce is deferred to the UAT-selected adapter as a bounded, adapter-local `DeliveryCorrelationToken` whose relation to the attempt is recorded — never a generic lifecycle identity. |
| C-r.4 | IMPORTANT 2: `ContextProjectionInput.Basis`/`PriorPlans`/`Acknowledgements`, `DisclosureResultInput.Evidence`, and `CapabilityScope.Sources` have no stated maximum or snapshot/truncation behaviour, so history growth can defeat the 1 MiB operation and hook-lock budgets. | **ACCEPT in full** | §3.1 and §9.1 add explicit constructor limits and a snapshot-bounded newest-first selection rule, with a typed truncation result and a typed `ContextCompletenessError` that suppresses the packet where completeness is required. Tested at the public service boundary. |
| C-r.5 | MINOR: `OccurrenceRecord{OccurrenceID, EvidenceJournalID}` and `InterpretationResult{Interpretation, JournalID}` are equal values under two names. | **ACCEPT** | Both redundant fields deleted; typed accessors added. Same change as C-g.2. |
| C-r.6 | MINOR: the S1 engine-directory exception is otherwise justified and becomes safe once owner/timing is corrected. | **ACCEPT, and improved** | C-general R9's own-package move removes the exception entirely rather than making it safe. |
| C-r.7 | Prior Axis-C verification: activation, one occurrence type, no replay vocabulary, one hostcontract, explicit ownership, one substrate, one-cutover FSM direction, separate definition refs, small typed seams — all CLOSED. | **PRESERVE** | Unchanged. |

---

## 7. Rejection ledger

Five things this wave asked for and PROPOSAL-9 deliberately does not do, each recorded so the
next reviewer sees a decision rather than an omission:

1. **Cross-process admission control, permits, and a priority lane** (A-r.2, A-r.4). Rejected on
   the user's Option-A decision and on design grounds. Option B (off-path spool) is the recorded
   escalation if measurement shows real contention.
2. **Splitting S7 into S7a/S7b** (A-g.2). Unnecessary; the deadline lands upstream ahead of every
   Pasture slice, so the M1 dependency is a re-pin, not a slice.
3. **A hard worst-case derivation of the write budget** (A-r.5). Unobtainable without (1). The
   estimate is stated as an estimate with a revisit trigger instead.
4. **A semantically-identical-different-byte ingress case** (B-r.4). Byte-identical strictly
   dominates it; B-general's argument overrides B-reviewer's request.
5. **Moving the shared-file load test's ownership to S2** (C-r.1). S1 owns the write, so S1 owns
   the proof; only the gate timing moves.

## 8. Standing invariant added by this wave

**INV-1 (immutable snapshot).** Any type the design calls an immutable snapshot exposes no
mutable field and no lifecycle status. State is expressed as append-only facts with a derived
projection that carries its `SnapshotJournalID`. Enforced by a static guard and proven to bite by
a named mutation operator. This exists because the same defect class arrived three rounds running
from three different reviewers, and point-fixing it a fourth time would be the wrong response.

Successor proposal: PROPOSAL-9. This proposal is superseded; no vote transfers.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PROPOSAL-9 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 1/3 (Sections 10-15)

Authoritative continuation of PROPOSAL-9. Read with the description and continuations 2/3 and 3/3.
Section numbering and its map to PROPOSAL-8 is at the end of the description.

## 10. Complete context disclosure contract

### 10.1 Pure policy projection with bounded history

```go
type ActorRef struct {
    Actor   provenance.AgentID
    Session NativeBinding
}

type AssignmentRef struct {
    Assignment provenance.JournalID
    Task       provenance.TaskID
}

type CommittedPhaseRef struct {
    PhaseState PhaseStateID
    Phase      protocol.PhaseId
}

type ContextBounds struct {
    MaxItems uint16 // 1..64
    MaxBytes uint32 // 1..256 KiB
}

// Explicit constructor limits and a deterministic selection rule for every
// history collection. Without these, a long-lived multi-agent epoch grows the
// projection input without bound and defeats the 1 MiB operation budget.
type ContextHistoryBounds struct {
    MaxBasis            uint16 // 1..64
    MaxPriorPlans       uint16 // 1..32
    MaxAcknowledgements uint16 // 1..32
}

type ContextSelectionRule uint8

const (
    // The only rule. Newest-first by descending JournalID at or before the
    // reader snapshot, then truncate at the bound.
    SelectNewestFirstAtSnapshot ContextSelectionRule = iota + 1
)

type ContextSelection struct {
    Bounds    ContextHistoryBounds
    Rule      ContextSelectionRule
    Truncated bool
    Reason    TruncationReason
}

type ContextCompletenessError struct {
    Policy    ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Recipient ActorRef
    Reason    TruncationReason
}

type ContextPacketRef struct {
    Schema  ContextPacketSchemaRef
    Payload EvidencePayloadRef
}

type ContextProjectionInput struct {
    Recipient        ActorRef
    Role             protocol.RoleId
    Phase            CommittedPhaseRef
    Assignment       AssignmentRef
    Policy           ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Envelope         SemanticEnvelopeRef
    Basis            []provenance.JournalID // bounded, newest-first at snapshot
    PriorPlans       []DisclosurePlanID     // bounded, newest-first at snapshot
    Acknowledgements []DisclosureResultID   // bounded, newest-first at snapshot
    History          ContextHistoryBounds
    Bounds           ContextBounds
}

type ContextProjection struct {
    Recipient ActorRef
    Role      protocol.RoleId
    Phase     protocol.PhaseId
    Policy    ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Envelope  SemanticEnvelopeRef
    Basis     []provenance.JournalID
    Selection ContextSelection
    Packet    ContextPacketRef
}

type ContextProjector interface {
    Project(ContextProjectionInput) (ContextProjection, error)
}
```

`ContextProjector` is pure and receives only exact committed phase/assignment facts and exact
definitions. It has no Journal, FSM, control service, transport, or mutable projection.
Candidate-only, stale, unauthorized, wrong-recipient, and unknown-schema input fails before
planning and cannot mutate any state.

Truncation is never silent. When any bounded history collection is truncated, `ContextSelection`
reports it. Where the context policy declares completeness required for that packet class, the
projector returns `ContextCompletenessError` and the packet is **suppressed**, producing a
`DisclosureSuppressed` fact rather than a partial packet. (`aura-plugins-u2d51` IMPORTANT 2.)

### 10.2 Plan, delivery attempt, and immutable result facts

```go
type DisclosureChannel uint8

const (
    DisclosureGeneratedMaterial DisclosureChannel = iota + 1
    DisclosureDynamicHostResponse
    DisclosureExplicitPull
)

type AcknowledgementMode uint8

const (
    AcknowledgementPositiveHostEvidence AcknowledgementMode = iota + 1
    AcknowledgementExplicitAgentReceipt
    AcknowledgementUnavailable
)

type DisclosureDeliveryStatus uint8

const (
    DisclosureDelivered DisclosureDeliveryStatus = iota + 1
    DisclosureAcknowledged
    DisclosureFailed
    DisclosureRevoked
    DisclosureSuppressed
)

type DisclosurePlanInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Projection  ContextProjection
}

type DisclosurePlan struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Operation provenance.OperationID
    Recipient ActorRef
    Phase     protocol.PhaseId
    Role      protocol.RoleId
    Policy    ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Envelope  SemanticEnvelopeRef
    Basis     []provenance.JournalID
    Selection ContextSelection
    Packet    ContextPacketRef
}

func (p DisclosurePlan) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureAttemptInput struct {
    Plan        DisclosurePlanID
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Channel     DisclosureChannel
    AckMode     AcknowledgementMode
}

type DisclosureAttempt struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT
    Attempt   DisclosureAttemptID
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Operation provenance.OperationID
    Channel   DisclosureChannel
    AckMode   AcknowledgementMode
}

func (a DisclosureAttempt) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureResultInput struct {
    Plan        DisclosurePlanID
    Attempt     DisclosureAttemptID
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    Status      DisclosureDeliveryStatus
    ObservedAt  time.Time
    Evidence    []provenance.JournalID // 0..32
}

type DisclosureResult struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Result  DisclosureResultID
    Plan    DisclosurePlanID
    Attempt DisclosureAttemptID
    Status  DisclosureDeliveryStatus
}

func (r DisclosureResult) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureService interface {
    Plan(context.Context, DisclosurePlanInput) (DisclosurePlan, error)
    BeginAttempt(context.Context, DisclosureAttemptInput) (DisclosureAttempt, error)
    RecordResult(context.Context, DisclosureResultInput) (DisclosureResult, error)
}

type DeliveryRequest struct {
    Plan    DisclosurePlan
    Attempt DisclosureAttempt
}

type DeliveryObservation struct {
    Status     DisclosureDeliveryStatus
    ObservedAt time.Time
    Evidence   []provenance.JournalID
}

type ContextTransport interface {
    Deliver(context.Context, DeliveryRequest) (DeliveryObservation, error)
}
```

**`DisclosureAttemptID` is now the typed attempt JournalID, and the random `[16]byte` identity is
gone.** PROPOSAL-8 carried three identities for one attempt: a journal ID, an operation ID, and a
random nonce. The attempt JournalID plus the operation ID already identify the durable attempt and
the exact retry, so the nonce was an unearned third identity of exactly the kind the UAT rejected
for occurrences (`aura-plugins-u2d51` IMPORTANT 1; `aura-plugins-oygyo` R6 asked for its rationale
and the honest answer is that it does not have one yet).

If the UAT-selected channel genuinely needs a host-visible correlation token that cannot expose a
JournalID — §13.1 forbids JournalIDs crossing the host boundary — the **selected adapter** in S5
introduces a bounded, adapter-local `DeliveryCorrelationToken`, records its relation to the
attempt as a fact, and does not make it a generic lifecycle identity. Deferring it to the adapter
is what lets the need be demonstrated instead of assumed.

Every plan/attempt/result boundary now uses typed IDs with `JournalID()` accessors; no signature
accepts a bare `provenance.JournalID` where a typed disclosure identity is meant.

The operation service captures plan/attempt/result timestamps through an injected clock and
persists the complete operation input. Transport never constructs a plan or mutates disclosure
history. A crash after the attempt fact but before a result remains an honest unknown attempt.

Each write has a mandatory slot: `disclosure-plan`, `disclosure-attempt`, or `disclosure-result`.
Exact same operation ID and input returns the original slot; changed input conflicts. A result
must match its plan and attempt. Delivered, acknowledged, failed, revoked, and suppressed are
separate facts. Acknowledged requires positive evidence under the UAT-selected mode; delivery never
implies acknowledgement.

The channel and acknowledgement constants are typed alternatives, not an active choice. UAT selects
one compatible pair before M4 slicing (§19.3).

### 10.3 Rebuildable current disclosure state

```go
type DisclosureCurrentStatus uint8

const (
    DisclosureStatePlanned DisclosureCurrentStatus = iota + 1
    DisclosureStateAttempted
    DisclosureStateDelivered
    DisclosureStateAcknowledged
    DisclosureStateFailed
    DisclosureStateRevoked
    DisclosureStateSuppressed
)

// DERIVED PROJECTION (INV-1 class 3).
type DisclosureCurrentState struct {
    Recipient         ActorRef
    LatestPlan        DisclosurePlanID
    LatestAttempt     DisclosureAttemptID
    LatestResult      DisclosureResultID
    Status            DisclosureCurrentStatus
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
}

type DisclosureStateProjector interface {
    Rebuild(context.Context, ActorRef, provenance.JournalID) (DisclosureCurrentState, error)
}
```

The projector folds immutable facts in JournalID order. It writes no truth. Deleting disclosure
projection rows and replaying the journal returns the same state. Candidate, stale, unauthorized,
wrong-scope, and unknown-policy facts are never admitted to the fold.

`DisclosureCurrentStatus` (7 values) and `DisclosureDeliveryStatus` (5 values) are deliberately two
enums over different domains: one folds history including "planned, no attempt" and "attempt, no
result" — the crash gap — while the other records what a single result fact says. Two enums over
different domains is simpler than one enum with invalid combinations (`aura-plugins-oygyo`).

## 11. One immutable FSM, the complete control API, and transaction-local expiry

### 11.1 Preserved FSM direction

`pkg/protocol` owns one private static phase table. Production constructors no longer accept a spec
map. Read-only lookup and iteration return deep copies:

```go
func PhaseSpecFor(protocol.PhaseId) (protocol.PhaseSpec, bool)
func AllPhaseSpecs() []protocol.PhaseSpec
func NewEpochStateMachine(string) *protocol.EpochStateMachine
func NewEpochStateMachineFromState(protocol.EpochState) *protocol.EpochStateMachine
```

The transition law remains the PROPOSAL-7 corrected law, including the Review -> Propose, Plan UAT
-> Propose, Code Review -> Worker Slices, and Implementation UAT -> Worker Slices feedback edges.
Generated transition metadata derives from this source. `PhaseSpecFor` is also the single adjacency
oracle consulted by `TransitionCandidateDraft`'s constructor (§8.2). The live engine/audit writer
is cut over once at M6; direct phase projection writes cannot remain active.

### 11.2 Capability API, complete

PROPOSAL-8 exposed only `CommitCandidate` while claiming issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume as
behaviour. A green implementation could have checked only consumed-or-revoked state and omitted a
scope axis entirely, and no test could have caught it (`aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 2;
`aura-plugins-oygyo` R7; `aura-plugins-4acdq` item 8). The API is now complete and scope mismatch is
a typed, observable result.

```go
type CapabilityState uint8

const (
    CapabilityIssued CapabilityState = iota + 1
    CapabilityBound
    CapabilityRevoked
    CapabilityConsumed
)

type CapabilityOperation uint8

const (
    CapabilityRecordHumanDecision CapabilityOperation = iota + 1
    CapabilityBindSession
    CapabilityBindAssignment
    CapabilityCompleteTask
    CapabilityCommitTransition
)

// The thirteen scope axes, each independently checkable and each with its own
// test case. This restores PROPOSAL-7 section 14.2's "wrong actor, role, epoch,
// assignment, candidate, contract, native session, request, tool, agent, task,
// worktree, and operation", which PROPOSAL-8 compressed into the single phrase
// "issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume matrix" (aura-plugins-237wx B2 row 1).
type CapabilityScopeAxis uint8

const (
    ScopeAxisOperation CapabilityScopeAxis = iota + 1
    ScopeAxisEpoch
    ScopeAxisActor
    ScopeAxisRole
    ScopeAxisAssignment
    ScopeAxisCandidate
    ScopeAxisRuntimeContract
    ScopeAxisNativeSession
    ScopeAxisNativeRequest
    ScopeAxisNativeToolCall
    ScopeAxisNativeAgent
    ScopeAxisNativeTask
    ScopeAxisNativeWorktree
)

type CapabilityScope struct { // opaque constructor
    Operation  CapabilityOperation
    Epoch      provenance.TaskID
    Actor      provenance.AgentID
    Role       protocol.RoleId
    Assignment provenance.JournalID
    Candidate  TransitionCandidateID
    Contract   ir.RuntimeContractID
    Sources    []provenance.JournalID // 1..32
    Bindings   []NativeBinding        // 0..16
    ExpiresAt  time.Time
}

type CapabilityRevocationReason uint8

const (
    RevokedSupersededScope CapabilityRevocationReason = iota + 1
    RevokedOperatorWithdrawal
    RevokedAssignmentEnded
)

type CapabilityIssueInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Scope       CapabilityScope
}

type CapabilityBindInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Capability  CapabilityID
    Actor       provenance.AgentID
    Bindings    []NativeBinding // 0..16
}

type CapabilityRevokeInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Capability  CapabilityID
    Reason      CapabilityRevocationReason
}

type CommitCandidateInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Candidate   TransitionCandidateID
    Capability  CapabilityID
    Actor       provenance.AgentID
}

type CommittedTransition struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT; no replay flag
    PhaseState PhaseStateID
    Capability provenance.JournalID // the Consumed state fact
    Decision   provenance.JournalID
}

type EpochControlService interface {
    Issue(context.Context, CapabilityIssueInput) (CapabilityID, error)
    Bind(context.Context, CapabilityBindInput) (CapabilityID, error)
    Revoke(context.Context, CapabilityRevokeInput) (CapabilityID, error)
    CommitCandidate(context.Context, CommitCandidateInput) (CommittedTransition, error)
}

// Typed failures. Each is separately observable through a public reader, so a
// test can assert WHICH check refused, not merely that something refused.
type CapabilityScopeMismatch struct {
    Capability CapabilityID
    Axis       CapabilityScopeAxis
}

type CapabilityStateError struct {
    Capability CapabilityID
    Observed   CapabilityState
    Required   CapabilityState
}

type CapabilityExpiredError struct {
    Capability CapabilityID
    Deadline   time.Time
}

type BuildIdentityError struct {
    Implementation EpochImplementationRef
    Status         BuildIdentityStatus
}
```

`Decision` may be zero only for a transition kind whose constructor declares no decision effect;
there is no pointer ambiguity. Only `BuildIdentityExact` may back a commit; a dirty or unresolved
build returns `BuildIdentityError` with zero writes (§7.3).

### 11.3 Minimal upstream Provenance extension for transaction-local expiry

This section is **unchanged from PROPOSAL-8** and was verified line-by-line against pin `bcce714`
by `aura-plugins-4acdq` and `aura-plugins-oygyo`. It is the S7 / M6 prerequisite. It is **not** the
P0-PIN caller deadline, which is a separate and earlier upstream change (§4.3), and **S7 is not
split**.

```go
type ConditionTransactionTimeBefore struct {
    Deadline time.Time
}

const ConditionTransactionTimeBeforeKind provenance.ConditionKind = 3
const ConditionTimeExpired provenance.ConditionFailureReason = 3

type Condition struct { // upstream tagged union after the extension
    Kind                  provenance.ConditionKind
    Selector              provenance.FactSelector
    AssertedJournalID     provenance.JournalID
    TransactionTimeBefore ConditionTransactionTimeBefore
}

type ConditionFailure struct { // upstream typed failure after the extension
    Index             int
    Kind              provenance.ConditionKind
    Reason            provenance.ConditionFailureReason
    AssertedJournalID provenance.JournalID
    ActualJournalID   provenance.JournalID
    Deadline          time.Time
    TransactionTime   time.Time
}
```

Ordinals 3 and 3 are both free (`facts.go:55-69` and `facts.go:93-98` at the pin). The new
condition kind carries exactly one UTC deadline and requires the fact-selector/JID arm to be zero;
existing ExactFact/CurrentFact conditions require the deadline arm to be zero. Canonical encoding
stores signed Unix milliseconds; sub-millisecond deadlines are rejected rather than rounded
differently across processes.

The default transaction-time source executes, on the same pinned SQLite connection after write-lock
acquisition:

```text
SELECT CAST(unixepoch('subsec') * 1000 AS INTEGER)
```

`transaction_now_ms < deadline_ms` passes; equality or later returns typed `ConditionTimeExpired`.
The source is private, database-backed production authority; upstream internal tests inject a fake
transaction-time source, so application callers cannot weaken production time.

Evaluation order is fixed:

```text
BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquired
  -> exact OperationID lookup
       -> exact input: return original result
       -> changed input: OperationConflict, zero writes
       -> new operation: continue
  -> CurrentFact(capability == Bound)
  -> scope match on all thirteen axes
  -> TransactionTimeBefore(capability.ExpiresAt)
  -> CurrentFact(phase == expected current state)
  -> write capability Consumed + phase/decision/task effects
  -> COMMIT
```

Pasture maps `ConditionTimeExpired` to `CapabilityExpiredError`. A fresh operation queued before the
deadline but acquiring the lock at or after it loses with zero journal, capability, phase, decision,
task, context, and projection writes. An exact already-committed retry still returns before
deadline and current-state checks. Same operation ID with a changed deadline or any other changed
input conflicts.

No arbitrary SQL, callback, boolean expression, or application-specific predicate is added to
Provenance.

## 12. Complete bounded public reader

### 12.1 Cursor and bounds

```go
type PageSize uint16

func NewPageSize(uint16) (PageSize, error) // accepts 1..256 only

type QueryFingerprint [32]byte

type Cursor struct { // opaque; encoded token has version + checksum
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
    LastJournalID     provenance.JournalID
    QueryFingerprint  QueryFingerprint
}

func ParseCursor(string) (Cursor, error)
func (Cursor) String() string

type PageRequest struct {
    Size   PageSize
    Cursor *Cursor
}

type TruncationReason uint8

const (
    TruncatedPageSize TruncationReason = iota + 1
    TruncatedDepthLimit
    TruncatedNodeLimit
    TruncatedEdgeLimit
    TruncatedHistoryBound
)

type PageState struct {
    Next      *Cursor
    Truncated bool
    Reason    TruncationReason
}

type LineageDirection uint8

const (
    LineageForward LineageDirection = iota + 1
    LineageReverse
)

type LineageBounds struct {
    MaxDepth uint16 // 1..32
    MaxNodes uint16 // 1..256
    MaxEdges uint16 // 1..512
}

type CursorErrorKind uint8

const (
    CursorInvalidPageSize CursorErrorKind = iota + 1
    CursorQueryMismatch
    CursorSnapshotFuture
    CursorStale
    CursorTampered
    CursorUnsupportedVersion
    CursorInvalidLineageBounds
)
```

An initial query with no cursor snapshots the current maximum JournalID. Every page is ordered by
ascending JournalID and resumes strictly after `LastJournalID`. The query fingerprint is SHA-256
over the canonical typed filter and direction/bounds. `Cursor.String` includes a versioned canonical
frame and checksum; `ParseCursor` rejects malformed or tampered frames. A cursor with a different
query fingerprint, future snapshot, last ID after snapshot, missing retained snapshot, or
unsupported version returns a distinct typed error before SQL. A cursor is an integrity and
stability token, not authorization; authorization is checked independently on each read.

### 12.2 Concrete records, queries, pages, and methods

No record below carries a bare `provenance.JournalID` beside its own typed identity
(`aura-plugins-oygyo` R2, `aura-plugins-u2d51` MINOR 1). Where a field genuinely refers to a
different record of unknown kind — link endpoints, fact basis — `provenance.JournalID` is correct
and is retained.

```go
type InterpretationRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    Occurrence     OccurrenceID
    Envelope       SemanticEnvelopeRef
    RecordedAt     time.Time
}

type FactRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Fact           LifecycleFactID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    Kind           FactKind
    Schema         LifecycleSchemaDefinitionRef
    Payload        EvidencePayloadRef

}

type UnresolvedFactRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Unresolved     UnresolvedFactID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    FactKind       FactKind
    Reason         UnresolvedReason
    Basis          UnresolvedBasis

}

type CausalLinkRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Link           LifecycleLinkID
    Interpretation InterpretationID

    To             provenance.JournalID

}

type TransitionCandidateRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Candidate      TransitionCandidateID

    From           protocol.PhaseId
    To             protocol.PhaseId

}

type CapabilityStateRecord struct { // DERIVED PROJECTION
    Capability        CapabilityID
    State             CapabilityState
    Scope             CapabilityScope

type CommitRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    PhaseState PhaseStateID
```
