author: David Huu Pham
text: CONTRACT REVISION 1 — exact L2 oracle matrix, addressing review aura-plugins-amtj6. (1) Three-effect rollback: use a real file-backed unified tracker and real receipt.Service; construct valid interpreted and consultation effects; install a test-only SQLite abort trigger/fault at insertion of consultation evidence so occurrence and interpreted insertion have begun before the third effect fails; call one Receive; assert no operation, journal, evidence, or result-slot row for that operation and no partial projection row, while the separately committed payload blob may exist only as reclaimable. Do not mock Service, Appender, or Provenance. (2) Append every: with a fixed clock and two distinct production operation IDs, submit byte-identical deliveries twice; assert distinct occurrence and interpreted journal IDs/operations, exactly one shared blob row/digest, no replay flag/count, and unchanged exact body. (3) Canonical evidence: compare literal compact interpreted and consultation JSON bytes in exact field order; raw SHA-256 effect digests; OCI sha256 interpreted reference text; slot/kind; owned payload/digest copies. Reject typed-nil ports, IsValid false, marshal failure, null/array/scalar, duplicate object members, trailing JSON, oversized final payload, and mutation of marshal-returned bytes. (4) Read/paging: prove reordered and duplicate-equivalent filters share a fingerprint/cursor, any semantic filter change rejects, page-size change accepts; append after page 1 is excluded by the pinned snapshot; fresh pagination sees it. Place nonmatching rows between matches and prove exact BINARY multi-binding AND predicates execute before LIMIT with no skipped/duplicate rows. Prove malformed capture has zero interpretation, valid has one, same-operation duplicate is corruption, adjacent operations never cross-associate, and corrupt/noncanonical/digest-mismatched interpreted evidence fails with no partial page. (5) Migration: v6→v7 valid zero/equal-duplicate binding preservation, stable positions, lookup/cascade, v5→v7 chaining, current-v7 idempotence; malformed/unknown/duplicate-member/null/missing-NativeName/invalid-kind/oversized binding causes full rollback with schema version 6, original lifecycle_occurrences schema and exact bindings_json bytes/rows unchanged, no surviving v7 table, and clean foreign_key_check after success. (6) Payload: exact read, missing digest, byte_count mismatch, content digest mismatch, noncanonical/non-sha256 input, and defensive-copy reread after caller mutation. (7) Handler/CLI: every invalid contract/event/binding/page/cursor/format is rejected before an injected opener is called; real built hook command writes a temporary file DB and real built list command rebuilds then emits grouped occurrence+interpreted output with distinct registration/semantic contracts, [] not null, cursor semantics, and no raw body/full envelope/consultation/private path leakage. Assert exit 1 validation, 2 open/connection, 5 migration/rebuild/stored-evidence, and 0 empty/nonempty success. Every Go invocation uses -race; red evidence must identify missing production behavior, never a test-only export.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

## BLOCKER — consultation contract creates an import cycle
- References: SLICE CONTRACT FREEZE A/3 (2026-08-01 20:44), llm/plan/impl-plan-m1-claude-vertical.md:282-328, and current internal/lifecycle/receipt/interpreted.go:9-14,30. Freeze A requires internal/lifecycle/waist/consultation.go to declare NewConsultation(interpreted receipt.Record, ...), while the authoritative receipt API already imports waist for NewInterpreted(waist.L2, ...). Implementing both makes waist -> receipt -> waist, which Go cannot compile. Exact fix: keep only the marker-port interfaces in waist (they must not import receipt), and move ConsultationRecord, NewConsultation, its canonical payload validation, and Effect() into receipt/consultation.go (or another neutral package). Update the frozen contract, dependency table, and L1/L2 tests accordingly.

## BLOCKER — same-operation interpreted reference is not enforceable as frozen
- Freeze A specifies only result_slot=interpreted plus the digest of interpreted.Effect in the consultation JSON. A digest is not an operation identity: identical interpreted payloads can occur in distinct operations, and a Record has no operation ID before append. The current receipt.Record.Effect() (internal/lifecycle/receipt/interpreted.go:96-112) likewise carries no operation identity. Exact fix: specify and test an operation-scoped invariant at the single-Append boundary: Receive must assemble occurrence, exactly the corresponding interpreted effect, and consultation effect, then reject and rollback if the consultation reference does not match the interpreted effect in that same operation (including a duplicate-identical payload from another delivery). The read association must additionally verify the referenced interpreted result slot belongs to the producing operation, not merely find any matching digest. Add a concrete cross-operation swap test.

## IMPORTANT — global snapshot has no executable API or transaction contract
- Freeze B requires a global maximum journal-ID watermark, but the proposed LifecycleReader injection is only DB plus provenance.FactQueryAPI; the existing projection reader snapshots MAX(lifecycle_occurrences.journal_id) (internal/lifecycle/projection/reader.go:29-39), which is not the global journal watermark. Exact fix: name the FactQuery or Journal API used to read the global max, and require the watermark, occurrence projection reads, and interpreted FactQuery association to use one consistent read snapshot or explicitly define the allowed race and proof. Add a test with unrelated journal rows above the last occurrence and concurrent append behavior.

## IMPORTANT — exact BINARY bytes are underspecified by the migration SQL
- Freeze C says native_name and binding_value are exact BINARY 1..512-byte values, but the proposed column declaration is native_name BINARY / binding_value BINARY; that does not unambiguously specify SQLite BLOB storage or bytewise comparison. Exact fix: define the columns as bounded BLOB values with explicit byte-length checks and BINARY comparison and index semantics, bind and query []byte, and test invalid UTF-8, embedded NUL, case differences, and prefix values.

## MINOR
- The plan should remove the obsolete receipt/reader.go from the owned-path list or consistently retain the explicit deletion; the slice description says delete it, while impl-plan:284 still lists it under Owns.

Vote is REVISE because the first two blockers prevent a compilable and integrity-preserving implementation. Checks: independently read the full slice description and all A/3, B/3, C/3 freeze comments, URD/request/UAT/IMPL_PLAN, both authoritative plan files, current receipt/model/projection code, and the clean baseline diff. No source files or other Beads tasks were modified.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CONTRACT REVISION 2 — correctness, addressing aura-plugins-3jddh. Import direction is explicit: `internal/lifecycle/waist/consultation.go` contains ONLY the two marker/json interfaces and never imports receipt; `internal/lifecycle/receipt/consultation.go` imports waist and declares `NewConsultation(interpreted Record, ...)` using its own package-local Record type. There is no waist↔receipt cycle. Add receipt/service.go and tests to SLICE-3 ownership. Before Appender.Append, Receive validates known lifecycle extras as a coherent ordered pair: zero-or-one canonical interpreted effect, zero-or-one canonical consultation effect; consultation requires the immediately preceding interpreted effect in the same extras; strict consultation decoding must name result_slot `interpreted` and its referenced digest must equal SHA-256 of that exact interpreted payload; both effects must have exact slots/kinds/content digests. Missing, duplicate, reordered, forged, or cross-swapped pairs fail before Append. The fixed result slot is operation-local; one validated OperationInput makes the reference resolve to the interpreted row produced by that same operation without predicting a JournalID. Add different-digest cross-operation swap and duplicate/reorder tests plus the separate third-effect transactional rollback test.

Global snapshot uses the existing executable Provenance API, not projection-local MAX and not a new upstream method: issue a bounded `Facts().QueryEvidence` for interpretedKind with FactTaskAny, Limit=1, SnapshotMaxJournalID=0; Provenance returns the global committed journal maximum even with zero matching rows. Use that returned watermark for occurrence SQL and every batched interpreted fact query. Occurrence selection runs in one read transaction with journal_id<=snapshot; immutable journal rows plus the shared watermark exclude later commits, while rebuild transactions remain atomically old-or-new to readers. Never derive snapshot from lifecycle_occurrences.

Revise v7 normalized binding columns to byte-exact BLOB, not TEXT: `native_name BLOB NOT NULL CHECK(length(native_name) BETWEEN 1 AND 512)` and equivalent binding_value; lookup index remains `(binding_kind,native_name,binding_value,journal_id)`. Production and migration validate UTF-8, no NUL/control, no padding, declared kind, and byte bounds before storing []byte; SQL compares bound []byte with exact `=` and no collation/wildcard/prefix normalization. Tests reject invalid UTF-8/NUL/control/padding and prove case variants and strict prefixes do not match. `receipt/reader.go` is owned only for explicit deletion.

text:
VOTE: ACCEPT - Axis A correctness review for M1b SLICE-4 contract.

End-user alignment: ACCEPT. The contract serves the request's end users (Pasture operators and agent-workflow maintainers) by preserving the accepted compiler pipeline while keeping M1's deferred authority mechanism explicit. Gate hooks are recorded and answered proceed, not silently no-oped or denied, which matches URD R8/R9 and V8.

Correctness evidence:
- Accepted URD requires broad automated evidence before legalization, separate authority at legalization, temporary exit-0/proceed behavior, and no semantic guessing (llm/plan/urd-harness-lifecycle.md:124-134,238-275,386-399). The SLICE-4 contract preserves this with observation terminal, gate consultation record + Proceed, and ElicitationResult NoAuthority.
- Proposal-11 fixes the M1 terminals: observation -> interpreted record; gate-consultation -> interpreted + consultation + Proceed; human-response -> interpreted + NoAuthority (llm/plan/proposal-11-harness-lifecycle-compiler.md:108-115). It also says M1 static proof is no authority/write in legalize/backend and human response returns typed NoAuthority (lines 271-294).
- Current runtime exposes the sole semantic enum (`runtime.EventSemantic`) and enforces gate-consultation => blocking plus human-response request identity (internal/runtime/lifecycle.go:15-27,418-443). Claude mappings classify PreToolUse, PostToolBatch, PreCompact, Elicitation as gate and ElicitationResult as explicit human response; PostToolBatch carries unresolved tool-call metadata (internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go:323-364).
- Current waist L2 is constructor-owned and carries semantics, origin, identities, and unresolved facts from the runtime mapping without a second arm enum or authority field (internal/lifecycle/waist/event.go:132-161,225-283).
- Current receipt layer is the correct persisted identity/write owner: `Service.Receive` owns blob write, operation actor/authority via `IdentityResolver`, and the single Append (internal/lifecycle/receipt/service.go:47-90,113-118). SLICE-4's no context/actor/writer/read dependency is therefore not a regression; it avoids re-porting historical lower.go's obsolete observation recorder, replay, actor resolver, and awaited-reply refusal, which Proposal-11 explicitly supersedes.
- The consultation constructor already accepts a real interpreted gate record plus legalize/response ports and produces canonical interpreted-paired evidence; `Receive` validates interpreted-then-consultation ordering (internal/lifecycle/receipt/consultation.go:26-57,119-153; internal/lifecycle/receipt/service.go:120-145). Delegating backend construction to `receipt.NewConsultation` is the right production path and avoids a second Append/I/O path.
- SLICE-7 is correctly left as the single production wiring owner: the impl plan requires one `receipt.Service.Receive` carrying occurrence, interpreted, and consultation effects, with SLICE-4 exporting only the consultation effect/HostResponse contract (llm/plan/impl-plan-m1-claude-vertical.md:489-510,723-732,836-875).

No required replacement contract text. I found no underspecified, contradictory, unsafe, or invented requirement in the frozen SLICE-4 API for Axis A correctness.

End-user and technical correctness: ACCEPT. Revision 2 is faithful to the accepted M1 contract. It strengthens the L2/backend oracle matrix without changing the public legalize/backend API, package ownership, production wiring ownership, or enabled M1 event set.

Evidence reviewed:
- URD R8/R9/V8 require broad automated evidence before legalization, separate authority at legalization, and temporary proceed behavior for blocking gates; gates should record consultation evidence and answer proceed, while the write-gate mechanism remains deferred (llm/plan/urd-harness-lifecycle.md:238-275,382-399).

SLICE-7 remains the owner of handler/built-command reachability and the one receipt.Service.Receive call (lines 489-510,723-732).
- Current runtime has one semantic enum and a separate BlockingMode; gate-consultation is invalid only when nonblocking, so conditionally-blocking gate semantics are real runtime state and not a test-only mutation (internal/runtime/lifecycle.go:15-22,73-84,418-425). author: David Huu Pham
text:
CONTRACT REVISION 2 — supersedes the Evaluation details in the original freeze; all other requirements remain unchanged.

Add the exact immutable result surface:

```go
type Evaluation struct { /* private case name, resolved event, decision, reason, event-present and constructed state */ }
func (e Evaluation) IsValid() bool
func (e Evaluation) CaseName() string
func (e Evaluation) Decision() Decision
func (e Evaluation) Reason() CorpusReason
func (e Evaluation) Event() (model.ContractEventKind, bool)
```

Zero/error semantics are binding: `Evaluation{}` is invalid; CaseName is empty; Decision and Reason return their zero values; Event returns `(0,false)`. `Evaluate` returns a zero invalid Evaluation with every actionable error. Every expected rejection returns a valid constructed Evaluation with exact typed withheld decision/reason. An enabled Evaluation is valid, has ReasonNone, and MUST expose a generated target event through Event. CaseName preserves the selected corpus case name.

Provenance decoding MUST retain the existing top-level JSON `event` string in a private envelope beside `acceptance.CaptureProvenance`; intentional extra fields such as `redaction` remain allowed. Empty or unknown event is actionable. After path, origin, digest, harness and version checks, resolve the retained native event by exact match against `registration.ClaudeCode2_1_210().Entries()` and require the resulting typed ordinal to belong to `ClaudeCode2_1_210TargetEvents()` before a success result. Do not add a native-name map or whitelist. Only after this resolution and `ValidateFixture` success may Evaluate return DecisionEnabled with Event present.

Expected path/origin/digest/version rejections preserve binding precedence and return Event absent because no typed event has been admitted. Future SLICE-2 compares `got.Decision()` and `got.Reason()` to each case oracle and, for every enabled result, requires `got.Event()` present and equal to a static enabled entry. This closes both round-1 correctness blockers without widening scope.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CONTRACT REVISION 3 — extends Revision 2 with the exact immutable Case read surface; Revision 2 and every unchanged original requirement remain binding.

Case is opaque and scalar-backed:

```go
type Case struct { /* private name, fixture, expected decision/reason, classification, provenance source/ref, mutation description, and constructed state */ }
func (c Case) IsValid() bool
func (c Case) Name() string
func (c Case) Classification() Classification
func (c Case) ExpectedDecision() Decision
func (c Case) ExpectedReason() CorpusReason
```

Zero semantics are binding: `Case{}` is invalid; Name is empty; Classification, ExpectedDecision, and ExpectedReason return their typed zero values. `LoadCorpus` constructs only valid Case values after strict metadata and non-vacuity validation. `Corpus.Cases()` returns a fresh slice of those immutable values. Classification reserves its zero value as invalid; Decision reserves its zero value as invalid; CorpusReason zero is CorpusReasonNone and is valid only with DecisionEnabled on a constructed valid Case/Evaluation.

Do not expose fixture, provenance, or mutation fields. `Evaluate` alone consumes the private fixture path; provenance and mutation remain reviewed metadata/oracles and are never evaluator inputs. This prevents callers from mutating a Case or accidentally substituting YAML prose for system behavior.

Future SLICE-2 must, for every real corpus Case, require `c.IsValid()`, call `Evaluate(root, c)`, require `got.IsValid()` and `got.CaseName() == c.Name()`, and compare `got.Decision()`/`got.Reason()` exactly to `c.ExpectedDecision()`/`c.ExpectedReason()`. It also uses `c.Classification()` to prove both classes were exercised. For every enabled Evaluation, it additionally requires Event present and equal to a statically enabled manifest entry. No reflection or package-private access is permitted.

text: VOTE: ACCEPT — Final-budget fresh Axis C elegance review of the original freeze plus Revisions 2 and 3, grounded at baseline dd5e290, accepted IMPL_PLAN/URD, and prior reviews. The private provenance envelope is necessary because CaptureProvenance has no event field, while exact generated-registry resolution followed by ten-event target admission avoids a second native-name map or whitelist. Event withholding is coherent: path/origin/digest/version expected rejections return valid withheld results without Event; actionable errors return zero invalid Evaluation; only exact registry resolution, target-set membership, and ValidateFixture success admit Event. No redundant variants/maps, mutable leakage, needless public metadata, hidden API gap, or combinatorial-growth risk found. No code/spec edits; no tests run because this is a contract/plan review.

OPENCODE 1.18.10 FACTS
- session.created is a durable catch-all observation delivered to legacy plugin event callbacks without awaiting callback completion. Its source schema carries session identity, but generated legacy plugin types expose correlation through properties.info.id and disagree about a separate sessionID field. Authentic capture must settle the actual plugin payload.
- tool.execute.before is a named awaited hook immediately before normal tool execution. It carries tool, sessionID, callID, and mutable args; hooks run sequentially in registration order, later hooks observe earlier mutations, and hook failure prevents that tool execution.
- No explicit plugin-hook timeout or retry exists. Cancellation of an already-running native Promise requires runtime proof.
- Some direct internal tool calls bypass tool.execute.before, so M2 proves lifecycle-hook delivery, not universal interception of every internal OpenCode tool action.
- Pasture's 1.17.18 profile is stale for the installed 1.18.10 catalog. The narrow tool.execute.before shape remains valid; session.created identity and the wider catalog require reprofiling.
- Pasture opencode.json and target manifest reference .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts, but that generated file is absent at current main and must not be assumed available.

CODEX 0.146.0/CURRENT SOURCE FACTS
- Current command-hook events total eleven and include SessionEnd, absent from Pasture's pinned 0.144.1 profile.
- PreToolUse is the strongest counterpart to OpenCode tool.execute.before. It runs before the tool handler, carries session/thread, turn, tool-use, tool name/input, model/permission/context data, and supports explicit block plus updated input.
- Matching Codex handlers run concurrently. Explicit blocks deny; ordinary spawn/parse/timeout failures are recorded as failures and do not necessarily block. This differs from OpenCode's sequential throw/fail behavior.
- PostToolUse is a correlated post-success event. It can reject result delivery or add feedback but cannot undo execution; Pasture currently overstates its output-mutation semantics.
- SessionStart/SessionEnd are configured hook executions, not exact equivalents of OpenCode's persisted session aggregate creation/deletion events.
- Pasture's Codex adapter/profile lacks SessionEnd, optional current fields, and native event-specific response encoding.

EQUIVALENCE RESULT
- OpenCode tool.execute.before and Codex PreToolUse are PARTIALLY equivalent: same broad pre-execution gate position, ability to block, ability to change input, and session/tool-call correlation.
- They are not equivalent in authority model, handler ordering, mutation representation, full identity set, ordinary failure behavior, hook-run observation, or stop-loop semantics.
- No exact OpenCode session.created/Codex session-hook pair exists. Any session event used for Codex is an ingress smoke proof, not the same semantic equivalence class.
- The typed middle-end must normalize only the proven common semantic core and retain provider-specific source facts; it must not flatten these differences into a shape-only boolean.

CAPTURE AND PRIVACY
- Both harnesses support disposable isolated capture with no persistent config edits: OpenCode through temporary XDG paths, OPENCODE_DB, OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, and a temporary plugin; Codex through temporary CODEX_HOME/project state and a temporary command hook.
- Neither source tree contains provenance-bearing raw lifecycle captures equivalent to Pasture's reviewed Claude SessionStart fixture. Existing tests/recordings are synthetic, recorded-runtime with insufficient provenance, or source-defined schema evidence.
- New captures require sidecars recording exact host/source version, timestamp, raw digest, capture method, and redaction declaration. Exact bytes stay local unless reviewed secret-free; otherwise only a marked derivative may be committed.

SCOPE CONSEQUENCE
These findings constrain but do not yet define the middle-end API. The scoped URD/proposal must first choose exact current-wave version profiles and Codex event/depth acceptance. No production code is authorized by this research comment.

text:
COMPONENT 1 FINAL: SHARED POST-L2 MIDDLE-END (2026-08-03)

EXPLANATION SHOWN VERBATIM
Plan is a short-lived, immutable Go value for one verified event. It is not an implementation plan, database record, provider registry, or persisted object.

plan, err := middleend.Evaluate(l2)       // pure: no DB, clock, or provider
_, err = receipts.Receive(
    ctx,
    delivery,
    plan.Effects()...,                    // fixed interpreted -> consultation order
)
if err == nil {
    return plan.Response()                // Proceed only after durable commit
}

ALTERNATIVE CONSEQUENCES SHOWN VERBATIM
- Plan owns order: The middle-end is the single semantic/effect compiler. Handlers become mechanical commit/emit shells. Adds one small constructor-owned type, preventing callers from reordering or omitting consultation evidence.
- Return typed records: Avoids the Plan wrapper, but the handler must interpret zero values, order records, convert effects, and pair the response. The middle-end becomes a helper rather than the invariant owner; future callers can diverge.
- Build full operation: Moves actor resolution, time, operation IDs, and persistence into the middle-end. This couples semantic compilation to SQLite/Provenance execution and starts duplicating the receipt service.

The proposed Plan packages existing receipt.Record, optional receipt.ConsultationRecord, and optional backend.HostResponse. It introduces no new semantic enum.

QUESTION SHOWN VERBATIM
With those consequences, which boundary should own the invariant that interpreted evidence precedes optional consultation evidence and that Proceed is emitted only after commit?

OPTIONS SHOWN VERBATIM
- Plan owns order (Recommended): One pure constructor-owned value makes handlers mechanical and keeps provider paths consistent.
- Handler owns order: Return separate typed records; fewer wrapper methods, but orchestration owns coupling/order.
- Middle-end owns execution: Build full operations with identity/time/storage; strongest ownership but tightly coupled.

USER RESPONSE VERBATIM
Plan owns order (Recommended)

OPEN FEEDBACK QUESTION SHOWN VERBATIM
Any remaining concern about what Plan means, its name, or this architecture boundary?

USER RESPONSE VERBATIM
No additional feedback (Recommended)

text:
COMPONENT 1: SHARED DERIVATION AND COMMIT BOUNDARY (2026-08-04)

DEFINITION AND ACTUAL OUTPUT SHOWN VERBATIM

Your original requirement was a tight, minimal post-L2 API with semantics owned in Go.

Actual interface at `c059ffb`:
```go
func Derive(event waist.L2) (Derivation, error)
func (d Derivation) Effects() []provenance.Effect
func (d Derivation) Response() backend.HostResponse
func (d Derivation) IsValid() bool
```

For a gate, `Derive` orders `interpreted` before `consultation`, builds typed Proceed, and the handler returns that response only after `receipt.Service.Receive` commits. A persistence failure returns no response.

Actual race demonstration:
```text
PASS TestDeriveGateUsesCanonicalOrderAndProceed
PASS TestHookLifecycleResponseOpenCodeCommitsBeforeReturning/{observation,gate}
PASS TestHookLifecycleResponsePersistenceFailureReturnsNoResponse
```

Which ownership and commit boundary should M2 accept?

- Keep current boundary (Recommended): Go owns ordered semantics; durable commit must succeed before Proceed is emitted.
- Move semantics outward: Let provider adapters choose operations; simpler handler, but duplicates semantic policy.
- Respond before commit: Lower gate latency, but can acknowledge Proceed without durable evidence.

Keep current boundary (Recommended)

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RENAME DECISION (user, 2026-08-06): 'codebook' is renamed to LifecycleMetamodelManifest across Stage 3. Rationale: 'codebook' collides with qualitative-coding (subjective interpretive scheme) whereas this artifact is a mechanically-derived, content-addressed, versioned registry of per-event behavior metadata for every harness hook, derived from the PINNED contracts. Also only 1 of the 6 axes (semantic/blocking/mutation/failure/stop_loop/identities) is literally 'semantic', so *Semantics* naming was rejected. 'Metamodel' = what it contains; 'Manifest' = versioned + hash-addressed how it is held.

RENAME MAP:
- pkg internal/lifecycle/codebook -> internal/lifecycle/metamodel
- codebook.BuildCanonicalBody() -> metamodel.GenerateLifecycleMetamodel()  (Build* oversold an entirely-derived build-time render; Derive* rejected because middleend.Derive + lineage.DeriveLinks already mean 'runtime per-event transform')
- codebook.gen.go / var canonicalBody -> metamodel.gen.go / var lifecycleMetamodel
- model.CodebookCoordinate -> model.LifecycleMetamodelManifest
- model.CodebookDefinitionRef -> model.LifecycleMetamodelRef
- CodebookID/CodebookVersion -> LifecycleMetamodelID/LifecycleMetamodelVersion
- wire id pasture.lifecycle.codebook -> pasture.lifecycle.metamodel (NOTE: this string is INSIDE the hashed body, so the content-address changes; regenerate metamodel.gen.go + re-pin the v1 golden fixture SHA-256 + update agreement test)
- interpreted.v2 coordinate field -> renamed to match
- CLI 'pasture hook lifecycle codebook' -> 'pasture hook lifecycle metamodel'
- SemanticEnvelopeRef.Codebook (dormant M1 slot) -> .Metamodel
- render string 'codebook unresolved (pre-M5)' -> 'metamodel unresolved (pre-M5)'

SEQUENCING: applied by a dedicated rename worker AFTER the 3-IMPORTANT fix pass lands (avoid worktree collision), BEFORE the Stage-3 PR. Nothing is persisted yet (pre-land) so the content-address change is free.

text:
CORRECTION (supersedes the two prior rename comments where they conflict). The earlier "RENAME MAP" comment also stated the CLI as -> metamodel, which is NOW OVERRIDDEN. This comment is the authoritative record. Full spec: /tmp/opencode/codebook-rename-spec.md.

AUTHORITATIVE DECISIONS:

1. TWO replacement words, deliberate asymmetry:
   - Go symbols / internal vocabulary use: Metamodel  and  LifecycleMetamodelManifest
   - USER-FACING CLI subcommand uses: manifest  (NOT metamodel)
   So: the command "pasture hook lifecycle codebook" becomes "pasture hook lifecycle manifest".

2. Command wiring split:
   - cobra Use: string  "codebook" -> "manifest"
   - backing var  hookLifecycleCodebookCmd -> hookLifecycleManifestCmd
   - handler  HookLifecycleCodebook -> HookLifecycleMetamodel  (handler keeps the Metamodel vocab; only the Use: string is manifest)
   - HookLifecycleCodebookInput -> HookLifecycleMetamodelInput

3. Type + coordinate machinery (gopls rename, DEF line:col in the spec):
   - CodebookCoordinate -> LifecycleMetamodelManifest
   - CodebookDefinitionRef -> LifecycleMetamodelRef
   - CodebookID / CodebookVersion -> LifecycleMetamodelID / LifecycleMetamodelVersion
   - BuildCanonicalBody -> GenerateLifecycleMetamodel

4. Group-2 verbs ALL rename:
   - EnsureActiveCodebook -> EnsureActiveMetamodel
   - ResolveActiveCodebook -> ResolveActiveMetamodel
   - decodeCodebookCoordinate -> decodeMetamodelManifest
   - lessCodebook -> lessMetamodel

   - fields codebook (model/interpreted.go:19, receipt/interpreted.go:40) -> metamodel

7. Content-address id: the string value  "pasture.lifecycle.codebook"  -> "pasture.lifecycle.metamodel". Lives inside the hashed metamodel body; the content-address changes exactly ONCE by design (pre-land, nothing persisted). Regenerate metamodel.gen.go, re-pin the v1 golden fixture SHA-256, update the agreement test.

8. Render/comment string  "codebook unresolved (pre-M5)"  -> "metamodel unresolved (pre-M5)".

9. Package: internal/lifecycle/codebook -> internal/lifecycle/metamodel (git mv + goimports; package clause package codebook -> package metamodel).

author: David Huu Pham
text: VOTE: ACCEPT — axis B (test quality) round 1. Test strategy is adequate and integration-first; every URD Stage-4 validation case maps to an independently testable criterion. (1) Enabled→receipt with raw origin: AC-1 (ONE occurrence via real receipt.Service.Receive, Origin=="raw", commit-before-stdout) + AC-6 (list text|json read-back through the production projection — mirrors gate_integration_test.go's real-Receive + rebuild + query pattern, which is exactly the right integration-over-unit shape). (2) Native-vs-raw equivalence modulo origin: AC-3 explicitly demands equivalent L2/interoperation material; testable by delivering the same fixture payload through both paths and diffing committed records minus CaptureProvenance. (3) Withheld→activation refusal: AC-2 requires the SAME typed activation refusal as native before any DB write — the gate_test.go refusal-before-any-IO proof pattern (calls-slice assertion) applies directly. (4) Malformed/oversized→disposition: AC-4 + checklist 8 pin typed refusal, exit 0, empty stdout, non-empty stderr, NO DB file, with the existing M1 pin named. (5) No flags→native untouched: checklist 6 (gate ZERO diff vs 8bfdf4c — an executable git-diff check) + checklist 4 (golden native bytes byte-identical). Origin-discrimination regression IS testable despite WriteIntent carrying no origin: the writeIntentShape compile-time lock + the ZERO-diff gate check + AC-5's same-warrant-class assertion together prove the gate cannot observe origin — this is a sound compile-time-proof + diff-pin strategy, not assertion-only. Checklist is not over-specified (11 items, each executable: typecheck, test-race, zero-diff, golden bytes, no-new-kind via reader kind-set unchanged, docs marking) and the no-second-L2-constructor invariant is honestly stated as code inspection + S1-STOP. Two gaps to carry to implementation (MINOR, not blocking): (1) pin a raw-specific production-binary mirror of TestInvalidInvocationCreatesNoDatabaseFile — the existing pin only runs `hook lifecycle --harness not-a-harness` on the NATIVE path; raw's own new failure surfaces (unknown --schema-version, malformed raw stdin, over-limit stdin) need their own exec-binary assertions of exit 0 / empty stdout / non-empty stderr / no DB+WAL+SHM, else a raw handler opening the store before validating --schema-version would slip through green. (2) add a 1 MiB boundary test (exactly-at-limit accepted, +1 byte refused) — 'over 1 MiB' is stated but the exact boundary is not pinned; cheap off-by-one protection given MaxNativePayloadBytes is a constant.

text:
REVIEW-A SLICE-1: Found: 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 3 MINOR — verdict: PASS (0 BLOCKER).

Scope verified: full diff origin/main..HEAD (32af2f6, 09527cf, 14e495c, ab16ca3, 2e3fb36). CHECK RESULTS (axis A):
1. Provenance-only, non-discriminating — PASS. Gate package zero-diff (git diff origin/main..HEAD shows no gate files); no WriteIntent field; NewDeliveryIntent(delivery.Contract, delivery.Event) origin-blind (:service.go:209 + integration test); validateDelivery untouched (no origin discrimination).
2. Enum stringly-safety + normativity — PASS. origin.CaptureOrigin (internal/acceptance/origin/origin.go:22-41) keeps one IsValid/UnmarshalText incl. OriginRaw; acceptance re-exports type+all 5 heap — public API preserved byte-for-byte (alias keeps method set + consts typed); ValidateFixtureBytes (capture.go:94-97) still returns nil for anything != authentic-capture, so raw is non-normative like authored. Leaf-package relocation ENDORSED: real import cycle verified (acceptance/loader.go:17 imports tasks -> tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:11 imports receipt); ratified proposal G8/T1 said extend the acceptance enum — public surface unchanged.
3. Envelope+receipt carrier (UAT-Q4) — PASS. occurrencePayload.Origin (service.go:57) + Envelope.Origin (envelope.go:20), omitempty; integration test proves both read back through real store + projection. Four definition-refs stay zero: raw test passes empty envelope (model.OccurrenceEnvelopeRef{}), bj1vc scope untouched (no ingress/definition-ref changes in diff).
4. Tolerant decode + real byte-identity — PASS. Decode sites (projection/rebuild.go:41, reader.go:263) plain json.Unmarshal, no DisallowUnknownFields; interpreted/consultation strict decoders untouched (raw rides occurrence.v1). Byte-identity proof is REAL: TestReceiveUnsetOriginPayloadByteIdenticalToBaseline compares production encoder bytes to the frozen baseline string; the 4 cmd/pasture pins are pre-existing (cmd/ not in diff) and pass — native committed bytes == baseline 8bfdf4c bytes.
5. No second L2 constructor / no evidence-kind — PASS. receiveOnce asserts effect.EvidenceKind == occurrence.v1; journal.go unchanged; waist.BindEvent/EventBinding.NewEvent untouched.
6. Race/idempotence — PASS. Only serialize change is an additive struct literal member in json.Marshal (no shared state); EnsureActiveMetamodel untouched (not in diff); TestReceiveOriginPayloadDeterministic races 8 Receives, all byte-identical.
7. Worker flagged decision — ENDORSE. Native stays sentinel-unset (zero + omitempty) so frozen pins stay green; raw is the only origin producer; coherent with R4.3(b) (raw disclosure required; native needs no lower-trust marking) and with the ratified 'no frozen pin changes' stop. The alternative (stamping authentic-capture) would have violated the frozen pins — correct call.

FINDINGS (all MINOR):

M1 (test, internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_origin_test.go:41-46): NotContains(members, "origin") is vacuous. json.Marshal(capture.delivery) serializes Delivery whose untagged Origin field always emits the PascalCase key "Origin" (no omitempty on Delivery.Origin, service.go:31), so the lowercase key "origin" can never exist and the assertion can never fail — e.g. a closure stamping the delivery origin would NOT trip it. text:
CODE REVIEW (axis C — elegance) round 1 — SLICE-2 raw CLI+handler. VOTE: REVISE (2 IMPORTANT).

IMPORTANT-1 (continuation bytes duplicated AND divergent): rawAcknowledge (internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_raw.go:115-129) re-states the native continuation spellings as a second source of truth — the registry row already carries the encode seam (nativeresponse.CanonicalProceed/CodexContinuation) and HookLifecycleRaw already computes derivation (line 246), so dispatch.encode(derivation.Response()) would give byte-identical native output with zero new literals. Worse than duplication: the hardcoded switch emits proceed bytes for EVERY event, while native emits nothing for observations (Claude/OpenCode) and {} for Codex observations (nativeresponse.go:83-107) — so raw ingestion of an observation event prints a continuation native would never print, contradicting the doc claim 'byte-identical to the native continuation shapes'. S2's own test cements this: TestRawLifecycleGateFlowMirrorsNative asserts {"decision":"proceed"} for a Claude SessionStart (an observation). Fix: return dispatch.encode(derivation.Response()) — one encoder seam, true parity. (Escalate to axis A: if any consumer treats the hatch's stdout as a host ABI, this is a BLOCKER-candidate; operator-import semantics keep it IMPORTANT here.)

IMPORTANT-2 (orchestration duplication — 'same pipeline' erosion): HookLifecycleRaw re-orchestrates ~60-90 lines already written in hookLifecycle (activations resolve, host-version check, event lookup loop, withheld refusal, bounded read + over-limit, gate warrant, EnsureActiveMetamodel, bind/NewEvent, Derive, Receive) with per-copy error texts. The M4 seam's whole point (URD R4.2, 'all flow into the same pipeline') is that there is ONE verifier sequence; two divergent bodies means the M5 gate/metamodel sequence must be edited twice and can drift. Suggest extracting the common verification+commit tail (warrant → EnsureActiveMetamodel → bind → NewEvent → Derive → Receive) into one shared helper both handlers call, keeping only the truly raw-specific pieces (schema-identity gate, reject-outright disposition) in the raw body.

MINOR-1: the three rawParse closures (hook_lifecycle.go rows) are byte-identical 4-line bodies differing only in the ingress.Parse call — the same stamping (envelope{Origin:OriginRaw} + Delivery.Origin) could be one 2-line wrapper over the row's existing parse result; 12 duplicated lines.
MINOR-2: RawSchemaVersion constants duplicate the rawSchemaVersionFor derivations (two spellings of 'claude-code/2.1.210' in one file); the doc comment claims the set is 'pinned by tests against the generated registrations' but no such test exists (only exec tests with literals) — runtime is fail-closed via the derived comparison, so either add the pin or soften the comment.
MINOR-3 (carried S1 watch): receipt.Service.Receive/validateDelivery never checks Origin.IsValid at the durable-write boundary; with raw now the first real producer it is the right moment to add the 3-line closed-enum check so an invalid origin can never be committed (typed-enum invariant at the boundary, per CONSTRAINTS).

Praise: surface is proportionate (one subcommand, one handler, no new gate/enum-kind/options); error-constructor pattern mirrors native; M1 §8 ordering (refuse-before-store-open) preserved; the 1 MiB exact-boundary pin (MINOR-2 from plan review) is a good integration test; gate untouched (zero diff).

nobody has ever run the install yet. we don't have to worry about migrations for this right now.

Unified plus filtered (Recommended)

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE - Three BLOCKERs and one IMPORTANT remain in cumulative commits d1cee8a + 5605e36.

BLOCKER aura-plugins-ezzylb: Unix Load is now nonblocking, but Save still opens an existing FIFO without O_NONBLOCK and can hang before type validation.
BLOCKER aura-plugins-pjhph9: the Windows backend only cross-compiles; its exact POSIX 0600 check rejects Go Windows file modes, 0600 does not establish a private ACL, and directory Sync can return an error after replacement. It needs Windows-native runtime semantics and tests.
BLOCKER aura-plugins-r4adj9: the strict fixture now passes, but production install status still loads the global inventory facade and filters out every project row; output has no scope/root, contrary to unified status.
IMPORTANT aura-plugins-dpzbmd: round-1 single-ownership finding aura-plugins-jxpldy is not fully resolved because inventory.Load remains exported and used in production, creating an isolated Store rather than a projection over the caller-owned shared Store.

Independently verified resolved behavior: presence-aware required v1 tables and record fields (including managed:false), strict enum/unknown/duplicate/trailing rejection, descriptor validation before Load reads, prompt FIFO/directory Load rejection, canonical root acceptance/rejection and retained-absent semantics, typed record construction boundaries, deterministic mixed-scope round-trip/projections, Unix failed-rename preservation and temp cleanup, strict no-legacy/no-migration decoding, and the updated focused install-status fixture.

Gates: focused registry/inventory/apply race tests PASS; focused install-status CLI race test PASS; go vet PASS; native CGO-disabled build PASS; Windows amd64 and Darwin amd64/arm64 cross-builds PASS; gofmt and git diff --check PASS. author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE - Axis C round 2 found two BLOCKERs and two IMPORTANT maintainability findings.

BLOCKER aura-plugins-mdig94: internal/install/registry/read_nofollow_unix.go:89-101 still opens an existing Save destination O_RDONLY without O_NONBLOCK before Fstat, so a FIFO can hang mutation indefinitely. Apply the descriptor-first nonblocking check to Save and add a bounded production Save regression.

BLOCKER aura-plugins-haylf3: internal/install/registry/persistence_windows.go:94-95,125-159 cross-compiles but is not operational. Windows Stat synthesizes writable files as 0666 while Chmod(0600) only controls read-only, so Save output rejects on Load; directory File.Sync is unsupported and can report failure after a committed rename. Implement and test a Windows-native owner/access and durability contract or obtain an approved support-matrix change.

IMPORTANT aura-plugins-op0u4r: internal/install/inventory/inventory.go:106-115,136-139 still exports New/Load and cmd/pasture/install.go:101 uses the second persistence facade. Remove compatibility entry points; load through registry and project all callers over a caller-owned Store.

IMPORTANT aura-plugins-p9xwm3: internal/install/registry/record.go:14-43 uses exported string-based value types, so constructors are bypassable and validation is duplicated. Make Version, Selector, and SharedConfigIdentity opaque private-field values parsed once at the raw boundary.

MINOR group aura-plugins-e20veb was EAGER-created and closed empty.

Checks: clean worktree; gofmt check PASS; git diff --check PASS; go vet ./... PASS; CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./... text:
VOTE: REVISE — Axis A correctness round 2 found one unresolved production-path BLOCKER and two IMPORTANT boundary defects.

Round-1 resolution verification (independent; worker preflight ignored):
- RESOLVED: typed compatible finals/opt-in prerelease listing, opaque in-memory candidate identity, and exact Candidate/Version resolution with no fallback (`catalog.go:102-118,209-255,283-332`); non-newest and tampered-choice tests cover the path.
- RESOLVED: current production runtime identities are typed and match Claude/OpenCode/Codex runtime profiles (`aggregate_types.go:37-110`, IR alias, current profile values); manifest validation rejects wrong/unknown profiles.
- PARTIAL: bounded Link pagination, cumulative page/candidate/byte limits, cycles, later-page selection, and repository path confinement exist, but the production constructor accepts `?page=N` and can silently start after page 1 (IMPORTANT aura-plugins-pzgsra).
- PARTIAL: catalog-vs-asset request purposes and final destination checks exist, but the asset allowlist accepts all `*.githubusercontent.com` services and arbitrary github.com paths rather than release-asset destinations (IMPORTANT aura-plugins-rg7d6v).
- RESOLVED: one opaque RuntimeContractID type authority is exported from artifact and reused by IR; current values match all three registered profiles.
- RESOLVED: production NewGitHubSource accepts injected HTTPDoer; test-only constructor was removed and production construction/OpenURL are exercised.
- RESOLVED: exact canonical JSON keys, case variants, duplicates, unknown/trailing/malformed data, malformed sidecars, channel/range/count/asset/revision faults are rejected independently.
- RESOLVED: arbitrary-size numeric prerelease comparison uses digit length/bytes and has overflow-scale coverage.
- NOT RESOLVED: cancellation and operational manifest/checksum failures are swallowed as skipped candidates, post-read cancellation is not checked, and apply methods have no final cancellation guard (BLOCKER aura-plugins-x1e90k).
- RESOLVED: exported producer/consumer round trip covers all nine components and every public field using the public Aura-facing package.
- RESOLVED: manifest/component slices and verified asset bytes are defensively copied.
- PARTIAL: normal verification failures call the mutator zero times and success/error call it once, but mid-final-read or pre-apply cancellation can still reach a context-ignoring mutator; included in aura-plugins-x1e90k.

author: David Huu Pham
text: BLOCKED after complete round-1 review/URD/ratified-plan/API inspection at clean c03cc72. Exact method-level impossibility: service.GroupReconciler.PlanSelection is constrained by validateGroupPlan to exactly three canonical cell steps; engine.executeGroup calls Execute(step) -> Inspect(step) -> persists only that step's one GroupAction before advancing, stops immediately on action/inspection/save failure, and exposes neither a final all-cell probe/finalization nor abort. The required Claude migration is two-phase across cells: ensure every selected split, remove the shared v0.0.4 monolith, then remove every unselected split. For selections such as agents-only with pre-existing skills/hooks splits, truthful order requires skills step to wait, agents step to ensure, then shared monolith removal, then skills/hooks removals; the one-pass skills step cannot be revisited. Mutating all phases in skills Execute changes later cells before their facts persist (review A1); deferring to hooks Execute changes already-persisted earlier facts; removing skills before the monolith violates the ratified frozen argv/order and failure matrix.
